Public trust in smart glasses is very important for selling lots of smart glasses.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the world has changed in the ten years since snap first launched its camera-equipped spectacles. Not only has the smart glasses market grown, the number of people sharing videos online has also jumped significantly. Nowadays, thanks to the rise of platforms like TikTok and Reels, anyone can be an influencer. And the possibility of innocent passersby inadvertently being included in a viral clip is far higher than it was.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it is in this climate that google launches its intelligent eyewear devices today. This year has already seen Meta catch heat for what people called its "pervert glasses" or "creep glasses. " In addition to making people feel uncomfortable about being spied on or filmed without their consent, the controversy has also discouraged existing users of those glasses from continuing to wear them, not to mention possibly putting off potential buyers.

Diungkapkan bahwa google has been working on this launch for years, and it can be easy to see why it doesn't want its own camera-equipped glasses to suffer the same backlash or be painted by the same brush. It's published a blog post outlining the privacy protections it's bringing to the platform, and they don't just revolve around preventing tampering with the LED indicator lights. Google is taking a fairly comprehensive approach that goes beyond device-specific measures, and includes using its wide sphere of influence to prevent surreptitious videos spreading online. Perhaps that's why it's taking pains to make its privacy policies around the intelligent eyewear platform clear today. In fact, Juston Payne, the lead for XR at Google, told Engadget that there are quite a few ways privacy protection has been considered.

Berdasarkan laporan, let's start with what's happening on the glasses. It's basically table stakes at this point, but they all have an LED light on them to indicate when someone is taking a picture or recording a video. The light, which sits on the left side of the frame while the camera is next to the right eye, has sensors to detect if it's covered or tampered with and will prevent the capture of pictures or video.

Diungkapkan bahwa "unfortunately, some of the glasses that have launched in the past launched without any kind of detection for those things, and that broke trust. "And that's a problem," he added. " Payne said. He also said Google's methods are "pretty effective," though that's something that we'll have to test for ourselves to verify.

Berdasarkan laporan, and just as there are bad actors who will continue to try to break security protections for any safe in the world or online, there will be people attempting to get around google's anti-tampering measures here. "But nonetheless, we're very happy with where we're starting on this one. Payne said "there will always be ways around what we build, and then we'll try to fix those holes," and that he expects there will be an ongoing back-and-forth. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one of the main functions of google's smart glasses is the ability for gemini ai to use the camera to see what the wearer is looking at and provide more relevant information. During this process, the company says that the camera visuals won't be stored in your Gemini history. When there are faces in view, Google says "your glasses are also designed to automatically redact bystanders' faces before Gemini processes the visuals. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, the camera stream also won't be used in ai training or ad targeting, and google says any data that is sent off the glasses for processing, say in the cloud or on your phone, is encrypted for transit. It's also promising to bring the Private AI Compute processing platform to glasses, enabling these new devices to use the "hardware-secured sealed cloud environment" for greater processing.

Berdasarkan laporan, while the camera may be the most obvious recording sensor on these devices, they also have four microphones onboard to allow you to speak to gemini or get translations for people around you. Google uses beamforming to help focus on the individuals you're looking at when deciding whose speech to translate, and the company also said it "designed Gemini to focus on your voice by default, and not other voices around you, using directional microphones on the glasses. ".

Payne said that the microphones will filter out "all the world audio, as we call it, the bystander audio," It helps prevent accidental recording of people in your vicinity, but also improves Gemini's effectiveness by making sure it doesn't confuse someone else's heated argument as your query.

Berdasarkan laporan, of course, to make the glasses more useful, you'll have to grant it access to your apps and personal information. The intelligent eyewear can work with apps like Messages, Keep or YouTube Music, for instance, to send replies or create lists for you. Like on most phones, you'll have to grant permission to specific apps before they can access the camera on your glasses, and even after you do, you can still add or revoke access for every app.

Berdasarkan laporan, google also said you can view your past interactions with gemini, delete individual chats or all of them. You'll also be able to decide if your conversations are used to train AI. And to make sure there's no confusion over whether you left the glasses on or off, and if the microphones or camera might still be tuning in, all the new eyewear have a power switch with a clear red indicator to tell you when they've been shut down.

Diungkapkan bahwa most intriguing are the measures google is implementing across its entire ecosystem. The company said it has protections in place "across Google apps and services to deter misuse of the glasses," and they're pretty far-reaching.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for one thing, google shopping and google ads will "ban the sale and advertising of stickers or accessories designed to hide recording lights. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, the company is also working to cull the demand for videos of a harassing or creepy nature. Payne said that one of the problems Google has seen is a small number of people "who use glasses to take creepy videos. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, youtube will "prohibit content that depicts things like harassment and unwanted sexualization. Any video uploaded to YouTube — whether it's recorded on a phone, a camera, or glasses — has to follow these policies, and videos that don't are removed. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa there are also considerations for apps that request permission to use the cameras on these devices. "And there's actually some use cases that we're just blanket cutting off. "There's multiple approval layers if an app wants to use the camera," Payne said. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, to that end, google said that the play store and api policies will "prohibit apps from using the camera for social live-streaming or real-time facial identification, and from changing the behavior of the outer indicator light. " This live-streaming restriction also applies to YouTube.

Sebagaimana diketahui, of course, since the eyewear will be compatible with ios devices as well, it's possible that someone finds an app of that nature in the app store and uses it. And though Google may ban the advertisement or sale of physical goods that can be used to hide the LED indicator, people could very easily procure one on Amazon or Temu. There's more that needs to be done against this problem, and Google alone cannot cover all bases.

Diungkapkan bahwa sure, there's the honor system approach that most modern recording devices already use. Things like requiring an 18+ Google account to activate an intelligent eyewear device and asking users to agree to not recording others without permission or in sensitive places are in place here as well.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but the responsibility of prevention of misuse doesn't just fall to the user or google. There needs to be greater collaboration across the industry for these measures to be effective. Payne said that Google is sharing these statements now in an attempt to set an example and send a message. "We hope that it resonates with people, and we hope that as a byproduct of that, some others in this space say, 'You know what? We should probably tighten up some of our policies. '".

Berdasarkan laporan, payne believes that there is time to regain the public's trust. It allows the company a chance to "reset this conversation a bit, raise the bar on privacy. He said that while there is momentum building in the smart glasses space, it is still early days for the category. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa if it's able to get the attention and cooperation of other players in the space, google stands to benefit. "We think that that will then earn a lot of trust back in the category, then we can focus a lot on how cool and valuable these are. ".

#51. Measles is surging in the U.S. — and outbreaks can cost millions

📅 11 Nov 2026

Measles is surging in the U.S. — and outbreaks can cost millions

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/11/measles-outbreak-us-economic-cost.html

Berdasarkan laporan, measles outbreaks aren't just a public health threat. S. They can also be a financial burden on the U. — and the cost could only deepen as the once-eliminated disease spreads more widely.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the u. S. is expected to lose its official measles elimination status following a review by the Pan American Health Organization this week, after cases ratcheted to recent highs this year.

Diungkapkan bahwa more than 5,100 measles cases have been reported nationwide in 2026 as of early november, marking the country's worst outbreak in more than three decades. Eight deaths associated with the disease have been confirmed by states so far in 2026: six in Pennsylvania, one in New York and one in Wisconsin.

Berdasarkan laporan, based on this year's case count, a new tool developed by researchers at johns hopkins university estimates an economic cost of nearly $83 million for the outbreaks. That total includes $56 million in public health response costs, almost $25 million in lost productivity and more than $1. 8 million in direct medical expenses.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the tool also estimates that 2025 measles outbreaks in the u. S. — which involved 2,289 confirmed cases nationwide – carried an economic cost of more than $37 million.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the costs extend beyond treating people who become sick, accounting for the resources health departments spend investigating and containing outbreaks, as well as wages lost when people have to miss work. The tool uses more recent, state-specific cost and financing data than an initial study by the researchers, which relied on historical outbreak costs.

Diungkapkan bahwa the estimates from the tool are not a definitive accounting of what the outbreaks actually cost. S. CNBC previously reported on how the return of measles in the U. But it illustrates the hefty bill tied to the spread of a disease that can be prevented through vaccination, and the potential economic consequences of falling childhood immunization rates. exposes weaknesses in the nation's public health system that raise concerns about the return of other eliminated diseases.

"We're starting to see a whole bunch of people who decided not to get vaccinated as kids or have never gotten exposed to measles because they benefited from herd immunity, who now make it into adulthood and risk potentially getting quite seriously ill and requiring very significant medical expenses, or dying at the hospital," Bryan Patenaude, a health economist at the International Vaccine Access Center at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, who helped develop the tool, said in an interview.

Measles outbreaks can trigger a costly public health response, even when many people who are exposed never become sick.

Sebagaimana diketahui, when a case is identified, public health officials must investigate the infection, identify and notify people who may have been exposed, coordinate with hospitals and schools, and sometimes organize vaccination campaigns to prevent further spread. Those efforts can divert staff and resources from other public health priorities.

Costs could differ heavily depending on the state.

Berdasarkan laporan, johns hopkins' data includes national averages alongside state-specific inputs, including inpatient hospital costs and wages from government data or trusted health policy sources. In New York, for example, the average inpatient hospital stay is roughly $4,200 a day, while the minimum wage is $16 per hour.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the tool estimates that the 48 cases reported by new york in 2025 carried an estimated $1. 1 million in costs, including nearly $749,000 in public health responses, $333,000 in productivity losses and roughly $24,500 in direct medical expenses.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, meanwhile, the 803 cases in texas, the epicenter of the largest u. S. measles outbreak in 2025, carried estimated costs of nearly $13 million, according to the tool. That includes $9 million in public health costs, $4 million in productivity losses and around $288,000 in direct medical expenses.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the tool builds on a study published by patenaude and other researchers in august, which examined the costs of measles outbreaks in the u. S. The researchers reviewed published studies and government reports to compile historical estimates of medical expenses and public health response costs across 18 states.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the paper estimated that outbreaks carried a historical average cost of nearly $59,000 per case, just from the public health response. The researchers also estimated how costs scale with outbreak size, separating fixed up-front response expenses from the additional costs associated with each new case.

Diungkapkan bahwa "a lot of this is incurred up front, and that's because of the human labor that's involved in contact tracing and all of the different actors that sort of need to be mobilized to deal with the fact that there's an outbreak," patenaude told cnbc. "It's a largely labor-driven cost. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, that model estimated roughly $298,000 in fixed costs and about $16,300 for each additional case. But it relied on historical data, including a particularly large 2019 outbreak in New York City, where contact-tracing labor costs were high. The researchers also excluded productivity losses from that model because most of the historical studies they reviewed did not consistently account for them.

The economic burden of measles extends beyond the costs of treating infected patients and organizing a public health response.

Sebagaimana diketahui, people who are exposed to measles may have to quarantine, even if they never develop symptoms. Parents can also be forced to miss work to care for sick or exposed children, while workers who contract the disease may lose wages during their recovery.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a 2025 study by joey mattingly, a pharmacist and health economist at the university of utah, used published epidemiological and cost data to model the potential economic burden of a hypothetical 1,500-case outbreak. His analysis included direct medical expenses, public health spending and lost productivity, and examined how the estimates changed under different assumptions, including hospitalization rates.

The study estimated that the hypothetical outbreak could cost about $90 million, including roughly $26 million in productivity losses.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, those indirect costs can add up quickly because measles is highly contagious and a single infected person can expose dozens of others. Those contacts may need to quarantine or miss work while health officials determine whether they have been infected, creating costs even when they never develop the disease.

Mattingly estimated that each person who is quarantined could amount to roughly $300 in lost productivity alone.

If a single measles case exposes 40 to 50 people who then need to quarantine, that could translate into an estimated $12,000 to $15,000 in lost productivity, even if none of those contacts become sick.

That ripple effect is one reason Mattingly argues that the economic costs of outbreaks can quickly outweigh the investment required to vaccinate people against measles.

Berdasarkan laporan, "even if you don't get the infection, the contact costs you," he said. "And so it's just showing that there's this multiplication or exponential growth on the economic side that happens. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, the financial burden can also fall unevenly across communities. While the costs of responding to an outbreak may be shared among local, state and federal agencies, Mattingly said the impact is often felt directly by local health departments.

Diungkapkan bahwa "it's not like your health department is sitting around waiting for measles outbreaks," he said. "They're working, doing all these other things, and imagine having to just drop what you're doing because there's been a huge outbreak in the community. ".

Patenaude said the findings could help state and local health departments better anticipate the resources needed to contain outbreaks — particularly as measles cases continue to rise.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "it's not super expensive to treat and deal with a single case of measles compared to a single case of cancer," he said. "But if you have these outbreaks popping up and you're having to constantly divert resources that could be spent elsewhere by state and local health departments on measles, then you're going to wind up spending a lot of money very quickly. ".

#53. The first batch of Android XR smartglasses made me rethink my stance on specs without displays

📅 12 Nov 2026

The first batch of Android XR smartglasses made me rethink my stance on specs without displays

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.engadget.com/2314258/android-xr-smartglasses-hands-on/

I still want models with built-in screens, but Google’s first run of intelligent eyewear has a lot to offer.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the first device powered by android xr came out last year when samsung released the galaxy xr headset. But this fall, Google is taking its augmented reality platform in a different direction with the launch of intelligent eyewear from partners such as Warby Parker and Gentle Monster. This gives Google its own version of lightweight smartglasses to rival competitors like the third-gen Ray-Ban Meta line, and after testing them out, it made me reconsider my feelings about smart specs without built-in displays.

Berdasarkan laporan, as this first generation of intelligent eyewear is a bit of a departure from previous android xr devices, i think it's important to get some of the basics out of the way first. For this family of specs, Google is in charge of the OS while Samsung is handling much of the tech — including things like the cameras, mics, touch sensors and more. All of that then gets handed over to Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, who are in charge of the glasses design, lenses, general sales and customer support.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, right off the bat, this seems like a great division of responsibilities because it allows each company to do what they're best at. Google handles the software, Samsung takes care of the hardware and the real glasses makers ensure you have good-looking frames with the right prescriptions (you can even opt for transition/photochromic lenses). And right out of the gate, it feels like there's already a lot of interesting styles and color combos to choose from, regardless if you're a bit more fashion-forward or if you, like me, prefer a more traditional frame.

Diungkapkan bahwa another important thing to note is that while gentle monster's eyewear will be a touch more expensive than warby parker's models ($449 and $395, respectively), they will have the same general tech specs. Those include the same 2GB of RAM and 64GB of storage, a 12MP camera (that also handles up to 3K video), stereo speakers, far-field mics and a built-in touch sensor. Battery life is also the same across the board with around nine hours of use on a single charge, while the case for the glasses stores enough juice for multiple full charges.

Sebagaimana diketahui, furthermore, you won't be required to have a paid gemini plan to use any of the features of the glasses; it's all free. These glasses will even work with both Android devices and iPhones with feature parity across both OSes. That said, there won't be any options with a built-in display, which means Google won't have a true rival to the Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses, at least not yet.

Sebagaimana diketahui, when it comes to features, it's no surprise that these glasses have a lot of overlap with the ray-ban meta specs. And of course, the glasses are connected to your phone wirelessly (either Bluetooth or Wi-Fi depending on the situation) so you have access to streaming music, notifications, messages, supported apps and more. There's also a touch sensor built into the right arm for doing stuff like controlling volume, pausing audio or dismissing Gemini. There's a physical button near the right temple for capturing images: A short press takes a picture while a long press records videos. However, the real lynchpin of the entire platform is Google's AI, which can be easily summoned via voice controls or by performing a long press on the touch panel.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, now i'll admit that i don't interact with gemini all that often when i'm using a phone or a laptop. When I already have access to a screen, a keyboard and all sorts of dedicated apps, so I find I can often perform tasks faster manually than asking an AI assistant to do them. If you want to respond to a text, get turn-by-turn directions or start some tunes, you can do all that hands-free with simple voice commands while keeping your phone in your pocket. But when wearing smartglasses, it's a whole different story. Granted, that is sort of table stakes for smartglasses these days, but being able to walk around with your head up while dodging traffic or other pedestrians can't be understated.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but it goes deeper, because thanks to gemini's intelligence and persistent memory between conversations, the ai in your glasses has a much deeper understanding of how to help you. Instead of constantly having to say a wake word all the time, you can have more natural back and forth dialogue. This allows you to get updates on your events, make adjustments to questions and pick up on previous queries even when they happen throughout the course of your day (you can specify how long you want Gemini to remember conversations).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, where things get really interesting is the combination of computer vision and ai, which allowed me to do things like pick up a physical invite card and simply ask gemini to add it to my calendar. It can even do rough estimates for how much of a certain food has been added, so if you're not worried about being super precise, you can leave your measuring cups in a drawer. No need to grab my phone, open up an app and add details like the time, date and location myself. I was also able to do things like simply look at a bunch of different ingredients and ask Gemini to make a smoothie from what was in front of me. And if you run out of certain foods, you can easily tell Gemini to add something to your grocery list.

Diungkapkan bahwa then there are other features like live translation, which feels kind of magical. The glasses are designed so that the mics are directed in a cone-shaped space in front of you, so that even in a room with other conversations going on, the glasses don't get confused. Not only does this let you switch speakers naturally just by looking at someone else, Gemini will even adjust the output of a translation to sound similar to the original speaker. This allows you to follow along in real-time almost as well as someone who speaks the language naturally.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that said, the thing that impressed me the most about these android xr glasses is the platform itself. This includes little touches like dedicated sounds when Gemini accesses your camera, when the glasses take a photo or video, when Gemini leverages external AI and more. Compared to some rivals where a lot of features feel like a work in progress, Google's OS feels much more mature. Google has done a pretty good job of translating a lot of the most important features you use on your phone to a medium without a screen.

Berdasarkan laporan, then there's google's approach to privacy, which looks to be a step up from the competition. Furthermore, Google says images and info sent to Gemini will stay on your device and will not be used to train AI or for ad targeting. That might not sound like much, but considering Google owns YouTube and generates billions from advertising, the simple act of leaving money on the table in favor of privacy is a welcome departure from Meta's glasses. In addition to each pair of glasses coming with an LED indicator that blocks you from taking pictures or videos when it's covered up or disabled, Google also isn't supporting features like livestreaming video directly from the specs. Those have always felt like they are meant to expand the reach of Facebook and Instagram.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the one caveat to all this is that you do have to buy into talking to and relying rather heavily on gemini. So while I'm still waiting for companies to deliver streamlined specs with built-in displays, these audio-first options feel like much more than a stepping stone towards that. They're surprisingly full-featured, and I don't think it's a stretch to say that compared to rival assistants like Siri, Muse and others, Gemini is the smartest of the bunch. I'm still not sure I'm 100 percent on board with that, but at least for me, these glasses make a better argument for always-on AI support than almost any other class of device I've used. So even if you primarily want these for playing music, keeping tabs on your schedule and getting occasional help from AI, Google's first batch of Android XR-powered intelligent eyewear feels like it's already jumped to the front of the pack.

Pre-orders for the new family of Android XR intelligent eyewear from both Warby Parker and Gentle Monster begin today with official sales slated for December 10.

#56. Jensen Huang’s exit puts Nvidia’s support for open source in question

📅 12 Nov 2026

Jensen Huang’s exit puts Nvidia’s support for open source in question

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/jensen-huangs-exit-puts-nvidias-support-for-open-source-in-question/

The open source community just lost one of its strongest advocates.

Sebagaimana diketahui, nvidia ceo jensen huang resigned thursday after he admitted to an affair with an alleged chinese spy, raising concerns about u. S. national security and the motives behind the executive’s support for softer chip export controls on China.

Sebagaimana diketahui, huang has been a staunch supporter of open source ai, framing the ecosystem as good for safety, innovation, diffusion, and sovereignty. And as frontier AI labs increasingly move to reduce their reliance on Nvidia and build their own chips, supporting open source is also a good way for the company to diversify its customer base by selling chips to nation-states, enterprises, and any organization that wants to own its own models.

Still, Huang’s resignation raises questions about whether Nvidia will carry on his legacy by continuing to support the open model community.

Jensen no longer being CEO would be very very bad for the open model cause in the US.

Sebagaimana diketahui, huang’s departure also comes as nvidia has yet to finalize a deal to acquire open source platform hugging face for $13 billion. Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue said in a post on X that the company would continue to fight for open source, whatever happens next.

Nvidia also agreed to pay $6 billion for a non-exclusive license for open AI coding startup Poolside’s technology.

Berdasarkan laporan, within nvidia, huang pushed for the development of the nemotron family of open-weight ai models built for long-running agentic ai systems and reasoning workloads — potential competitors to closed frontier models. One company insider told TechCrunch that they don’t expect a change in leadership to have an impact on Nemotron development.

Huang also backed companies that would make American open models more competitive, investing in startups like Reflection AI and Thinking Machines Lab.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, huang’s influence extended beyond nvidia’s investments and product roadmap. He also emerged as one of the most prominent voices pushing back against Washington’s efforts to restrict the open AI ecosystem.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, earlier this year, huang wrote an open letter signed by 25 companies, including microsoft, meta, ibm, and palantir, urging the u. S. government not to over-restrict open-weight AI models, many of which come from China.

Berdasarkan laporan, the impetus for that letter was washington’s debate over how the u. S. should respond to allegations that Chinese AI labs are stealing intellectual property from American counterparts like Anthropic and OpenAI, both of which have reportedly appealed directly to Washington on the matter, urging stronger protections.

That combination of Huang’s personal visibility and Nvidia’s market power made him the strongest counterweight to arguments from closed-model providers like Anthropic and OpenAI, which have advocated for greater restrictions on advanced AI models due to safety reasons.

Berdasarkan laporan, without huang, the concern among open source community members is that whoever takes over will be more cautious. Nvidia has named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. It’s not clear how Kress will approach the Hugging Face deal or support for the open model ecosystem, but founder-driven priorities tend to get a downgrade when leadership changes.

Huang’s exit could also strengthen the arguments of those in Washington who are arguing for tougher restrictions on Chinese AI companies, particularly as the scandal surrounding his relationship with Alice Huang, the Megaspeed executive and alleged spy, puts renewed scrutiny on his efforts to loosen chip export controls.

Restrictions on open-weight models from China could kneecap competition for American companies, the most powerful of which have kept their models closed.

Diungkapkan bahwa still, supporting open source isn’t simply a passion project huang pursued out of idealism. It’s increasingly central to Nvidia’s business strategy.

As some of Nvidia’s biggest customers, including Google and OpenAI, develop their own chips, Nvidia has an incentive to cultivate a much broader ecosystem of AI developers and customers.

More players training, fine-tuning, and running models mean more GPUs sold, and less dependence on a handful of frontier labs.

Berdasarkan laporan, huang may be gone, but nvidia still needs an open ai ecosystem. The question now is whether that commitment can survive without the man who made it a priority.

TechCrunch has reached out to Nvidia for comment.

This article has been updated with information from an Nvidia employee.

#57. Apple HomeView review: A versatile smart display and Siri-powered home hub

📅 12 Nov 2026

Apple HomeView review: A versatile smart display and Siri-powered home hub

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.engadget.com/2313999/apple-homeview-review/

The company’s smart screen debut heavily relies on an iPhone or iPad — for better and for worse.

Berdasarkan laporan, apple's entry into the smart display category was rumored for years. In true Apple fashion, it refused to rush new products just because most of the competition was doing it. By the time its debut home hub device arrives this week, the company will be nearly a decade behind its main rivals in the space. Now that the HomeView ($299) is here, Apple is hoping the iPhone faithful will like its mix of elevated design and newly expanded Siri capabilities.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, unlike smart displays from amazon and google, apple's approach relies on a companion device. You'll also need to have some smart home devices to make the most of the smart display and be willing to use Safari as your recipe box. That means you'll need either an iPhone or an iPad to mirror apps using technology similar to CarPlay. As you'd imagine, that means the HomeView's usefulness, like CarPlay's, is directly tied to how much you use Apple's core apps — things like Messages, Calendar, Photos, Reminders and others. If all of that is OK to you, and if you're willing to give Siri access to personal data inside some of those apps, the HomeView can quickly become a very versatile device with something for your whole family.

Berdasarkan laporan, i have fond memories of the imac g4. It was the first computer I used in a design lab in college, and I loved how I could reposition the display to suit the task at hand. The first time I saw the HomeView, those memories flooded back. Apple's smart home display doesn't exactly replicate the G4 styling, but it's close enough for a decent nostalgia hit for me.

Berdasarkan laporan, the homeview essentially consists of two parts: a cylindrical, domed base and a 7-inch liquid retina display. The wall-mounted option is just the screen, and you'll have to pay at least $59. 95 for a mount. Every version of the HomeView has two full-range drivers in the display itself. At least, that's if you get the tabletop version. The base houses additional components, like a down-firing woofer and a pair of force-canceling passive radiators for fuller sound with more bass than the wall-mounted models.

Berdasarkan laporan, that display has an led-backlit multi-touch ips panel that offers a 1,088 x 1,088 resolution at 200 pixels per inch. 3 nits — the lowest brightness ever on an Apple display. Apple says it also added an oleophobic fingerprint-resistant coating to cut down on grime from everyday use. If it's in direct sunlight, you can expect the maximum 500 nits, but at night, it can dial things down to just 0. There's an ambient light sensor that enables the HomeView to adjust both brightness and warmth as needed. The company believes this makes it perfect for a nightstand, if you're willing to have a camera pointed at or near your bed.

Berdasarkan laporan, the homeview's display has bezels like an ipad and the shape of a large apple watch. All of the interaction is done via swipes and taps on the touchscreen itself, or, as I'll elaborate on in a bit, with your voice. And unlike that iMac I'm nostalgic for, you can only tilt the display — you can't adjust its height. While that will suit most of your needs, I'm sure there are a lot of people who would've liked the ability to change the height or rotate the screen as well. Unlike either of those devices, though, it has no physical buttons for controls. Once you do adjust the way it tilts, a built-in accelerometer detects the new angle and alters the audio performance of the display's two drivers to match it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, another item to discuss in terms of design is the homeview's lone port. Around back, there's a single USB-C jack for power. Apple ships the standard version of the device with a USB-C to USB-C cable and a 30-watt power adapter. 99, you'll need to purchase the power adapter separately. If you opt for the USB-C wall mount, which already costs $59. The company offers a 40W dynamic power adapter (up to 60W max) for $39 while the minimum required power supply (20W) will cost you $19. Obviously, the AC wired and PoE (power over Ethernet) wired mounts won't need a power adapter.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and lastly, there's the matter of color. For the wall-mounted version, you can only pick between Silver and Space Gray. On those, the sides and back of the display match the base. For the standard (table or countertop) version of HomeView, you can choose from Silver, Starlight, Rose Pink or Space Gray options. And, just in case you need the reminder, both HomeView models are the same price ($299).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one of the homeview's most helpful traits is its ability to put siri ai front and center in your home. The smart device runs on Apple's A18 chip, the processor that debuted with the iPhone 16 line in 2024. The company is using it here for its Secure Exclaves which give it the ability to process camera and microphone feeds on-device in a manner that can't be accessed by Apple. The company explained that this enables the HomeView to recognize your face and voice, or that of other users in your home, without exposing any of the data to the operating system.

Berdasarkan laporan, that's important, because siri ai now has access to more of your personal data, like your conversations in messages, info from your calendar invites and other bits of "personal context" from various apps. Of course, you have to opt-in to all of this by enabling Apple Intelligence on your iPhone or iPad, and you can limit which apps Siri can index data from. If you do decide to use the system, I can attest that it works well on the HomeView, though it's merely another vessel for the larger AI system.

Sebagaimana diketahui, during a lengthy conversation about lighthouses in north carolina, siri gave me information about visiting a variety of locations in the state. It provided information that I didn't specifically ask for, like which ones were still active, and got more comprehensive when my follow-up query was a bit vague. For example, when I asked "Which lighthouse is the easiest to get to?" Siri responded with both a list of ones you can park close to and highlighted the one that requires the least amount of climbing.

Sebagaimana diketahui, siri was able to check my calendar to see if i was free to take the trip on a certain date and provided travel time from my house (including follow-up questions about the cities i'd pass through). I was finally able to stump the AI when I asked about "good hotels" near the Currituck Beach Lighthouse in Corolla, but even still, things felt more natural and conversational than interactions I've had with Siri in the past.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at times, siri showed text answers on the homeview in addition to reciting the info. What's more, I got a notification on my phone from the Home app letting me know Siri responded to a request for personal content. But it's important to remember that HomeView is just a conduit for Siri AI and its newly expanded abilities. When I asked about driving time or my schedule, a preview of the best route and the specific day on my calendar popped up respectively. These same things can be done on an iPhone or other compatible Apple devices, meaning you don't really have to spend $300 on a dedicated display for these tools.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one final note on security: since the homeview is heavily reliant on an iphone or ipad, those devices must be nearby and recently unlocked (and enrolled in the shared home) for siri to access personal data. The HomeView uses facial and voice recognition to know who's speaking, and to know when they walk away, so prying eyes can't see your texts if they rush over after you've been looking at Messages or other potentially sensitive apps. Guests or family members who don't have an iPhone or iPad can still use basic functions (control smart home devices, check weather, play music, etc), including asking Siri rudimentary questions.

Berdasarkan laporan, when i first spent time with the homeview last month, the feature i was most excited about was the recipe integration in safari. I'm happy to report that feeling remains, for the most part, but there's one caveat that does impact the overall experience.

Sebagaimana diketahui, let's back up for a second. Once the page loads, you'll see a cooking icon (a spoon and recipe card) in the bottom right corner. Tapping that will launch the HomeView's streamlined mode for the kitchen, which shows a recipe image with the dish's name, creator, cooking time and servings. On the HomeView, you can view a recipe link in Safari from your iPhone by holding it close to the display (just like you do to pass audio from your phone to a HomePod). There are two options underneath: Ingredients and Start Cooking.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the ingredients option gives you a checklist-style collection of what you'll need for the recipe. I had no trouble getting the AI assistant to add various ingredients to different shopping lists I have in that app (Costco, grocery store, etc). If you need to add things to a shopping list in Reminders, Siri can do that for you. The HomeView will show its work by displaying the new entry in the Reminders app, and a Live Activities shortcut at the top allows you to quickly get back to the recipe with a tap.

Diungkapkan bahwa once you hit start cooking, the recipe's steps are divided into swipeable slides with inline shortcuts for any timers you need. Or, at least that's how it's supposed to be. While testing the HomeView, I pulled in recipes from my go-to cooks, and while some of them worked just like Apple advertised, others did not. This isn't a massive deal breaker, as you can still read the recipe's steps, but once you've experienced the correctly formatted version, it's hard to go back.

Sebagaimana diketahui, going back means you'll get all of the steps on a single slide, requiring you to scroll instead of swipe. And if you ever need to peek back at that ingredients list, the properly formatted versions have an always-present shortcut in the bottom right corner. To be clear, the formatting isn't an Apple problem; it's entirely up to the creator or publisher to present their recipes a certain way. This is a long block of text, which can be overwhelming, especially compared to the short, easy-to-follow slides that alleviate some of the stress from following complicated instructions. I'm just pointing this all out to say Apple is advertising the ideal scenario, which is honestly an excellent experience, but you may not encounter it every time you cook with HomeView.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, another big piece of the homeview puzzle is its ability to act as a smart home hub. With the Home app and devices compatible with HomeKit and Matter, this display becomes the command center for your cameras, thermostat, lighting and more. There's a Home dashboard that shows everything you've connected to the system. You can then create scenes and automations, or ask Siri to handle those for you.

Diungkapkan bahwa we'll get to homeview customization in a bit, but it's important to mention two home faces here. Of course, you can always ask Siri to do things for you by summoning the assistant on the HomeView. The Home Modular face puts your favorite smart home devices on the same screen thanks to customizable widgets. These give you control over each connected gadget, including the ability to check a camera feed, without opening any apps on your phone. I'm sure Apple's AI is tired of adjusting my thermostat at this point, as that's what I've primarily been doing during my testing.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there's also a home camera face that's all video, all the time. Here, you can livestream up to nine feeds at once, giving you the ability to keep tabs on things wherever you have cameras positioned. If a visitor is detected, you can just tap on the HomeView to unlock a smart door lock (provided you have one of those, of course). We are a Blink household, though, and those aren't yet compatible with HomeKit, so I wasn't able to test any of Apple's camera features.

Diungkapkan bahwa if you have an icloud+ subscription, homeview works with compatible security cameras (again, homekit and matter) to detect people, pets, packages and vehicles. When any of those are seen, you'll get a notification and a live feed on the display. HomeView can also detect smoke or carbon monoxide alarms and send alerts to your iPhone, iPad or Apple Watch — even when you're away from home. That feature, known as Sound Recognition, is also available on the HomePod and HomePod mini.

Diungkapkan bahwa the homeview's speakers make it a solid option for music, podcasts and other audio entertainment. And unless you like watching your shows within a thin band that sits in the middle of a square display, flanked by thick black bars on the top and bottom, you, too, will find the video experience on HomeView underwhelming. I would love to see Apple bring F1 multiview to this display though, putting two small alternate feeds below the main broadcast. That's OK though, because right now, the only video app that's available on HomeView is Apple TV. But, despite its crisp, vivid display, the device is not well-suited for watching videos. Yes, they'd be tiny, but at least that's a better use of the space and eliminates the awkward black bars.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the homeview runs on the same platform as carplay, which is why the various video streaming apps you have on your iphone don't show up on this device. Apple says third-party developers are welcome to enable their apps for use on the HomeView, but doing so would also mean optimizing them for CarPlay. Only time will tell if developers are going to go through the extra steps of making that happen.

Berdasarkan laporan, when it comes to audio-only content though, the homeview is great. I'd classify the sound quality here as the midpoint between the HomePod mini and the larger HomePod. The system never loses other instruments either, as you can easily pick up the guitars in Anberlin's "Gravity. I've been reviewing the tabletop HomeView with a base, so I've enjoyed the added woofer and passive radiators, which balance out full-range drivers with extra bass. Across a variety of genres, bass is tight and punchy, and vocals cut through the mix clearly. " Switch to something more chill, like Sam Barber's "If I May," and the acoustic instruments lay a base for the singer's unique vocals. Drums are more subdued here, and the HomeView does well to keep them from overpowering the mix.

Diungkapkan bahwa i should also note the homeview can get pretty darn loud. I measured 87dB with my Apple Watch standing right in front of the device. But I should also warn you that it's not a comfortable listening volume if you're standing close to the display. It might be nice for a party, but you'll likely stay around 50 percent or less for the most part.

Berdasarkan laporan, spatial audio with dolby atmos is available on the homeview for compatible music, movies and shows. However, given the compact stature of the device and its limited sonic prowess, you're more likely to notice the excellent overall clarity and even-handed tuning more than any dimensional effects. While watching an episode of Masters of the Air, for example, I found the sound perfectly fine, but wouldn't classify it as very immersive.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, apple included a few more entertainment-related conveniences on the homeview that add utility. When listening to songs from Apple Music, you'll see animated album artwork if an artist has it, and lyrics are available with a single tap. For one, it works with the HomePod, HomePod mini and AirPlay-compatible speakers for multiroom audio, which allows you to play the same thing everywhere or pick specific songs for each room. And just like you can with your iPhone and HomePod speakers, you can handoff content from your phone to the HomeView just by placing your handset in front of the display.

Berdasarkan laporan, the homeview may look like an enlarged apple watch's screen, but the two devices also overlap in another area: faces. There's also an animated Snoopy face that updates based on the time of day, weather, holidays and sporting events. You can have it just be a clock, as there are three faces just for that purpose, or display your calendar or the weather. These screens are what you see when the HomeView is in what I like to call rest mode, when it's just sitting there not being actively used. Then there are the two Home faces that work with smart home devices that I already mentioned.

Diungkapkan bahwa those all have their purpose, but my two favorites are the photos and modular faces. You can opt for it to cycle through photos of specific events (Memories), people, pets or cities, for example, but you can also set up Shared Albums that it will source from. The Modular face is what I've used most, as its customizable collection of widgets puts the calendar, date, time and weather in one spot. The former makes the HomeView a digital picture frame and you can get specific about what shows up there. If you do that last one, new photos will automatically appear every time they're added to the collection. Of course, you can pick and choose what shows up here based on your needs or preferences, you're not forced to use the same combination I do.

Berdasarkan laporan, the best thing about faces is that you can easily switch between them by swiping horizontally on one. A long press brings up the face customization interface where you're free to fine-tune things like color and widgets (where available) to your heart's content.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one feature that apple has spent a lot of time showing off on the homeview is facetime. The smart display has a 12-megapixel Center Stage camera in its top bezel, which means you can conduct video chats without reaching for your iPhone. Of course, the Center Stage software will keep you centered in the frame as you move around, which will be handy if you need to take a call from the kitchen while you're cooking, for example. You can start FaceTime calls on the HomeView, or you can hand them off from your iPhone. I'll also note that you can take voice calls from the HomeView, and in general, the device works well for both types of chats.

Berdasarkan laporan, find my is also available on the homeview, allowing you to locate everything from your iphone to your airpods, or anything that has an airtag attached to it. The intercom feature from HomePods is on the HomeView as well, which comes in handy if you have multiple Apple speakers spread throughout your house. Of course, you can also use this to find family and friends who are sharing their location with you. It also works with the iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch, plus you can send and receive intercom messages from anywhere — not just inside your home.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, lastly, live activities displays real-time info for a variety of tasks on homeview. Live Activities on the HomeView are a bit limited though, only capable of showing active timers/alarms, FaceTime calls, Safari media playback and Now Playing controls for Apple Music or Apple TV. I found it also surfaced audio controls for my go-to podcast app Pocket Casts as well. Like it does on your iPhone, the feature puts your progress at the top of the display on a floating, tappable button. One thing that doesn't show up there that I wish it did is Live Activities from the Sports app. It would be great if the live scores for my favorite teams or an update on who's leading the F1 grand prix were available at a glance.

Diungkapkan bahwa apple is years behind the competition when it comes to smart displays. The company's two main rivals in this category, Amazon and Google, have been honing their products since 2017 and 2018 respectively. The premise has always been similar to Apple's: a combination display and speaker that's a conduit for each company's virtual assistant — or in 2026 terms, each company's AI.

Sebagaimana diketahui, amazon's current echo show lineup has six options, ranging from 5 inches up to 21 inches, with the largest models ditching the speaker base for a wall mount or stand. The most affordable, the Echo Show 5, is $100. Google's current slate of smart displays is much more modest, with only the aging second-generation Nest Hub and Nest Hub Max as the available options. Those are going for $100 and $229 respectively, and only the pricier of the two has a built-in camera for video calls.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, apple may have lagged behind the competition on introducing a smart display, but the homeview checks a lot of boxes that make it a very powerful option for iphone users. When you factor in the cooking assistance, smart home compatibility and FaceTime chops, the HomeView can easily become the command center for any household. The ability to automatically distinguish between different family members, and for Siri to pull in personalized context for each person, makes this a useful home hub. It's also more elegantly designed than all of its main competitors. Just be sure to keep your iPhone (or iPad) handy if you want to make the most of it.

Fossil Group posted quarterly results on Tuesday that could point to early signs of a turnaround for the legacy watchmaker.

The company's fiscal third-quarter earnings indicate the strategy is beginning to bear fruit.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the company said tuesday that it returned to profitability in the third quarter, posting operating income of $25. 7 million last year. 3 million, compared with an operating loss of $21. 4% to $271. Sebagaimana diketahui, for the quarter ended oct. 7 million, or 19 cents per share, compared with a net loss of $39. 1% to $137 million. 3, Fossil reported net income of $11. Diungkapkan bahwa fossil added that its key growth engine for the quarter was asia, where net sales grew 15. 1%. Fogliato said much of that growth was led by the India market.

Diungkapkan bahwa "priority number one is to grow our home market, and we're doing that," he said. "As retail is settling into a smaller, more profitable base, ready to grow again, we're entering 2027 with plenty of opportunities. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, fogliato said one key to growth was not trying to keep up with the smartwatch trend. While trying to make gains in the smartwatch space initially hampered Fossil's performance, it's now investing in analog watches again.

Sebagaimana diketahui, smartwatch sales came in under $1 million for the quarter, but sales for traditional watches — which make up around 86% of fossil's sales — grew 6. 4%.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "fossil is literally having a comeback, a strong comeback, a momentum, and we can see this," fogliato said. "And it comes not only through the numbers — it comes with the excitement we see in the stores, and we think we're just at the beginning. We have so much work to do. ".

“China wants Jensen out, so I want him in,” Luckey said last night, before Huang’s resignation was announced.

Diungkapkan bahwa mullenweg reposted an x post that followed his brief september ouster as ceo: “founder advice: if you don’t have a coup attempt every few years, you’re not hiring strong enough leaders. ” He said, “Just putting this back out there, for no reason whatsoever. ”.

Cook. ”.

#62. Apple TV 4K (4th gen) review: Still great, but drastically more expensive

📅 12 Nov 2026

Apple TV 4K (4th gen) review: Still great, but drastically more expensive

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.engadget.com/2314410/apple-tv-4k-4th-gen-review/

The $150 price increase is hard to swallow.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the apple tv 4k has been our pick for the best premium streaming device since the third-gen model arrived in 2022. In terms of pure performance, it was undoubtedly the best you could buy, thanks to the combination of picture quality, speed and features you wouldn't find on any of the more affordable competition. That was true four years ago and it's still true now.

Berdasarkan laporan, unfortunately, the global tech landscape has changed massively over the last two years. Nearly every device is more expensive, especially if it needs RAM or its own processor. Apple's streaming box didn't escape that fate. For the 4th-generation Apple TV 4K, Apple made big upgrades to performance and added a slew of new features, and of course, it carved out a more prominent place for Siri AI in your living room. The compact streaming box is a lot more expensive than the previous generation cost at launch, though, and the new $299 price tag certainly dulls its shine.

Berdasarkan laporan, if you were hoping for a new design, there are only subtle tweaks to report. The Siri Remote, however, is exactly the same size at 1. I'm talking 0. You'll be forgiven for not noticing. 24mm bigger in width and depth, and 3 grams heavier. 4 inches x 5. If you dive into the spec sheets, you'll discover the new model is slightly larger than the previous version. 4 inches x 0. The most evident is that Apple moved the light on the front of the box from the right to the center. 36 inches.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, apple upgraded the processor from the a15 bionic to the a19 chip. I don't have the tools to quantifiably check those claims, but I can tell you the device is super responsive, navigation is speedy and overall the UI is noticeably more fluid. The company says that the A19 chip is capable of 50 percent faster CPU performance and up to 2x faster GPU performance than the previous Apple TV 4K. In iPhone terms, that would be like going from an iPhone 13 to an iPhone 17, so the computing power increase here is significant. Plus, the A19 delivers a dedicated AV1 decoder for HDR rendering efficiency.

Berdasarkan laporan, of course, the a19 offers a boost to siri ai, which is playing a bigger role in the living room thanks to the new apple tv 4k. You can simply speak your queries while watching TV and Siri is off and running. For starters, the streaming box now has three far-field microphones built in, so you no longer have to use the remote to interact with the assistant. So when you want Siri to "play the show Jack texted me about," the assistant knows just what to do. But with Siri's recently expanded capabilities, it can now pull in personal context from Messages and other apps too. Like before, Apple's AI can help with finding and playing live TV, movies, shows and sports from your go-to apps. Additionally, audio captured from the far-field mics is processed within the Secure Exclave on the A19, so neither the apps, the OS nor Apple get access to any of the data.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the new feature that will get the most use at my house is precision finding for the remote in the find my app. And when I can't hear it, Precision Finding is better than the previous method for locating the remote with an iPhone. I have two kids who are constantly leaving the remote in undisclosed locations, so the added ability to play a sound has already greatly reduced the amount of time I spend searching for it. With the built-in mics for Siri though, a lost remote is much less frustrating since you can just tell the Apple TV 4K what to do.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there's also a noteworthy audio upgrade on the apple tv 4k. So you can have two HomePods in the front and two HomePod mini 2s in the back, which is the configuration I tested. Before, you could only use two HomePod or HomePod mini speakers as a stereo pair. The only additional requirement is that the two front speakers and two rear speakers have to match. Now you can use up to four of those, so long as they're second-gen HomePods or HomePod mini 2s, for a more complete home theater surround sound system. If you have four of the same speaker, that works too.

Sebagaimana diketahui, once you have all of the homepods in place, you'll hear a series of tones as the apple tv 4k locates the speakers and tunes the audio for the room. The HomePods provide the added bass needed for action scenes, or really just for a fuller soundstage most TV viewing will eventually require. I suspected that a combination of HomePods and HomePod minis is the ideal setup and my testing proved me right. I think having four HomePods would be overkill, not to mention expensive. The HomePod minis can't do that on their own, but they do well as rear speakers, providing dimensional backup to the larger speakers at the front. I also heard a four-mini configuration during a demo last month, and while it's certainly a boost compared to TV speakers, it's not nearly as potent as the arrangement I tested at home.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i'll also note that there's a feature called whole room audio that will be great for parties and gatherings. This allows for all four speakers to play the same sounds, rather than the fragments each might deliver in a surround sound setup. This ensures that everyone hears everything, from vocals to guitars, or even the commentators of an F1 race. Whole Room Audio is also easy to activate as it's accessible from the Speaker Mode option in the Control Center.

Berdasarkan laporan, like it has in the past, the new apple tv 4k can function as a smart home hub. Thanks to the HomeKit Secure Video, you can expect secure local processing on the streaming box, which encrypts clips before they're stored in iCloud. This allows you to control HomeKit and Matter accessories like cameras, locks and thermostats, and Apple says "thousands" of such devices are compatible. Apple Intelligence provides captions for camera feeds and you can control everything from the Control Center.

Diungkapkan bahwa siri voice control is available as well, as is the ability to run scenes from the home app in the control center. If someone rings the doorbell, you can also choose to be automatically notified on the display you're already looking at. If you have a HomeKit or Matter compatible camera (I don't), you can get a live view of those in the top right corner of your TV screen. If needed, you can chat with them and unlock the door without leaving your seat.

Berdasarkan laporan, my biggest complaint about the fourth-gen apple tv 4k is the price. However, even with rising memory and component costs, tacking on another $50 to the already inflated price tag is adding insult to injury. At $299, this model is $150 more than the equivalent version of its predecessor was at launch. Sure, Apple increased the price of the third-gen Apple TV 4K from $149 to $249 earlier this year, and a lot has happened since that model debuted in 2022. It especially stings when you consider the company actually decreased prices when it launched these models in 2022.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to pour more salt in the wound, apple got rid of the cheaper wi-fi-only option that also offered less storage space (64gb). Its original price was a drop from the $179 that the comparative version preceding it cost. If you'll allow me to dig even deeper into Apple TV 4K history, that $129 model was not only $50 cheaper than the W-Fi-only version before it, but even doubled the 32GB onboard storage. In 2022, that version of the third-gen Apple TV 4K launched for $129, though it eventually went up to $199 this year. Meanwhile, the fourth-gen Apple TV 4K only comes in one configuration and it has 128GB of storage; that's the same capacity as the priciest model of the previous generation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, after living with the apple tv 4k's new home theater setup with four homepods, i'm starting to question how many people will actually use it. When you consider one of the primary functions of a HomePod is to serve as a direct line to Siri, permanently putting all four in your living room seems like a waste. Not only does it require you to have four of Apple's speakers, but you'll also have to put all four of them in the same space. Not to mention you'll miss out on multiroom audio and features like Intercom, which are more helpful if your HomePods are spread around the house. After some testing, it seems to me like the quad-Pod speaker arrangement is a neat bonus — something you temporarily pull together for movie night or parties — rather than a substitute for a soundbar or traditional home theater setup.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i have another gripe that is more of a frustration with tvos as a whole, but it's worth mentioning as it relates to the new apple tv 4k. Even if you've added the streaming box to the Home app and assigned it to a room, the Home icon won't appear in the Control Center until you've either added a camera or created a Scene. So if you fire up your Apple TV and can't find your non-camera devices, that's probably why.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i appreciate the fact that camera feeds will be the most useful on a tv. I should also mention that tvOS doesn't have a dedicated Home app; everything to do with controlling your smart home requires digging into the Control Center on an Apple TV. " At the very least, I want there to be a shortcut in the Control Center for Rooms I've set up in the Home app on iOS, where I can then access individual devices if needed. But I think it's silly that I have to create a Scene (manually triggered saved settings) in order to see things like a thermostat or lights on a device that's advertised as a "smart home hub. Or, of course, you could fire up the full app on your phone.

Diungkapkan bahwa in terms of performance, the apple tv 4k remains the best streaming box you can buy. That's been true for a while now, and the upgrades the company made for this version only cements its position at the top of the premium heap. However, with the current state of global technology, specifically the price of anything that uses RAM or a chip like the A19, Apple's streaming device isn't as easy to recommend as it once was.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you're rocking with a third-gen model, i'd urge you to stay put. And if you're looking to invest in an Apple TV for the first time, try to hold out for a sale or catch one on the refurbished market. Heck, I'd even keep my eye out for a used third-gen model. Yes, you'll miss out on the newest features in that scenario, including the convenience of an always-listening Siri device that isn't a HomePod, but the core of what makes an Apple TV a great device is still there. And in late 2026, there's something to be said for saving significant money on a tech purchase.

#64. Evolving metal extraction processes

📅 10 Nov 2026

Evolving metal extraction processes

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11/10/1147726/evolving-metal-extraction-processes/

Rethinking how metals are extracted could unlock lower-emission production, make better use of mineral resources, and strengthen critical-material supply chains.

The metals industry has experienced transformational moments before: the Bessemer process, flash smelting, electric arc furnaces, and modern continuous casting all changed what was possible.

Berdasarkan laporan, yet, for more than a century, most extraction processes rely on techniques and pathways that would be familiar to metallurgists from generations ago. Processes have become larger and control systems smarter, but the fundamental science behind separating metals from ores has changed less than many realize.

Today’s materials challenges are different from those of the 20th century, but why are critical metals still produced using largely the same scientific foundations?.

EvoMaterials, a technology platform developed by Outokumpu—the global leader in sustainable stainless steel and the producer of ferrochrome with 67% lower carbon footprint than the industry average—is exploring that question by rethinking how metals can be extracted:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we decided to go beyond the current constraints and look fundamentally at what’s the best way to do this with the benefit of the scientific engineering knowledge and hindsight that we have today,” says caspar stinn, technical director for extractive metallurgy at outokumpu. “We’re looking at how we can reimagine metals production. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, as economies expand and the world becomes increasingly electrified, data and scientific models point to rising demand for many minerals, driven by technologies ranging from data centers to aerospace, water treatment, energy systems, and defence. According to Antoine Allanore, professor of metallurgy at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) this coincides with many Western economies having reduced their domestic processing capacity for the very metals those industries depend on.

Metallurgy is now strategically important, shaped not only by cost and availability but also by carbon footprint, geographic origin and supply-chain resilience.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that reality is particularly relevant for chromium and other specialty metals used in high-temperature and extreme environments. Chromium-based materials play a critical role in aerospace systems, power generation, corrosion-resistant infrastructure and defense technologies, where materials must perform under demanding conditions.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for decades, metallurgical innovation largely focused on improving yields, energy efficiency and process control. EvoMaterials is based on the idea that some metallurgical processes may benefit from entirely different chemical pathways.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the platform originates from research into sulfidation-based processing technologies, initially pursued to reduce carbon emissions associated with ferrochrome production. Laboratory work revealed broader potential.

Diungkapkan bahwa lab-scale trials demonstrated that these alternative process chemistries could potentially do more than lower emissions. They could recover valuable metals from lower grade resources and industrial side streams while fundamentally altering how separation processes are performed. The opportunity is to rethink how mineral resources are used and how much value can be extracted from them, bringing in greater resource efficiency and stronger industrial competitiveness.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, development of the technology began in the united states in 2021 for chromite from outokumpu’s kemi mine in finland, the only chrome mine in the european union and one of the few such operations across the western world. Since then, Outokumpu has evolved the technology through extensive research and development, combining new process chemistries with proprietary metallurgical expertise, supported in part by a non-exclusive patent license agreement from MIT.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the technology is a new application for separating metallic elements from materials,” explains allanore. Historically, that separation has been achieved using carbon- and energy-intensive approaches. The new method creates a different chemical environment that enables more efficient extraction with fewer losses and fewer unwanted by-products, recovering critical materials from resources considered waste.

EvoMaterials sits at the intersection of several scientific disciplines, a combination that strongly resonates with Stinn, who completed his PhD in Materials Science and Engineering at MIT, where his research focused on low-carbon metals processing and recycling technologies.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, modern materials innovation draws on a growing mix of chemistry, materials science, physics, computational modeling, and engineering. With advanced simulation tools and AI helping researchers identify promising directions, scientific discovery still depends on experimentation and testing in the lab—on getting your hands dirty and doing the hard work.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “science today is much more interdisciplinary than it was, and the collaboration across disciplines reveals new scientific opportunities,” says stinn. Engineering can translate those opportunities into more efficient and cost-competitive metals production.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a technically significant aspect of evomaterials is that it’s not a single process, but a technology platform. Allanore compares EvoMaterials to platform technologies in other industries, where a single scientific breakthrough can enable multiple downstream applications.

Sebagaimana diketahui, once a new extraction pathway has been mastered for one material system, the same scientific principles may be adapted to entirely different metals and mineral resources. The initial application becomes only the starting point.

“The future and the potential impact might be much broader than the original and current developments that are happening,” Allanore explains.

That possibility is increasingly important as industries seek secure supplies of nickel, chromium, molybdenum, and other strategic materials needed for advanced manufacturing.

Berdasarkan laporan, the broader implication extends beyond metallurgy. Companies that develop proprietary process technologies may create value through production but also through intellectual property and scientific expertise.

Based on Outokumpu’s technology leadership, that transition could create entirely new categories of value, enabling the production of high-value critical materials from ores and resource streams that previously appeared uneconomical or inaccessible.

The result would be a fundamental shift in how metals are manufactured, where sustainability, resource efficiency, supply security, and economic value become outcomes of the same technological architecture rather than separate objectives.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the next step for evomaterials is pilot-scale validation, with a pilot plant in new hampshire to begin operations in the first half of 2027. The facility will scale the proprietary technology from laboratory to one-ton production, providing a step toward industrial-scale deployment targeted for 2030. Beyond producing low-CO2, chromium-enriched ferrochrome and chromium metal, the platform could be adapted to other strategic materials, including nickel and molybdenum.

The work raises a broader question—how many of today’s metallurgical processes would look the same if they were invented from scratch? Or could those routes be designed differently today?.

The next revolution in materials may begin by rethinking how to extract the metals that society depends on.

Read more about this topic and hear more from Caspar Stinn and Antoine Allanore.
