#68. Rivian CEO says new R2 SUV, autonomy make 2027 an ‘inflection year’ as EV maker marks five years since IPO

📅 10 Nov 2026

Rivian CEO says new R2 SUV, autonomy make 2027 an ‘inflection year’ as EV maker marks five years since IPO

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/10/rivian-r2-autonomy-2027-rj-scaringe.html

It's been five years since Rivian Automotive celebrated its initial public offering with CEO and founder RJ Scaringe ringing the Nasdaq opening bell from the company's factory in Normal, Illinois, while the company's sleek vehicles sat outside the stock exchange in Times Square.

Berdasarkan laporan, it was a euphoric time for all-electric vehicle companies that has since diminished. And much like the EV hype, Rivian's stock price is down more than 80% since the Amazon-backed company debuted on the Nasdaq at $78 per share on Nov. 10, 2021. That includes a nearly 30% decline this year.

A host of internal and external factors have contributed to Rivian's stock decline, but the company continues to be the most promising EV maker to emerge during the early 2020s, as most of its peer group to go public during that time no longer exists.

Rivian founder and CEO RJ Scaringe acknowledges that not everything has gone to plan amid supply chain shortages, geopolitical tensions and slower-than-expected consumer EV adoption, but he said he believes the next year will prove to be a catalyst for the company and investors.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "2027 is really an inflection year for us," scaringe told cnbc during an exclusive interview. "I'm excited to start to really show what we believe so fully, the potential of the business. ".

Scaringe's bullishness comes as Rivian ramps up production of its midsize R2 SUV — meant to expand the brand to the mainstream market — and as the company continues to invest in its next generation of vehicle software and autonomy.

Diungkapkan bahwa scaringe said the r2, with an entry-level model at about $45,000, remains the core business to be able to showcase its newest technologies. Rivian delivered a record 19,248 vehicles in the third quarter of 2026, up 46% year over year, and said R2 was already its best-selling vehicle by volume, outselling both its R1 flagship products and its commercial van.

Diungkapkan bahwa "that's going to define the business. The path to profitability, the path to very significant growth in revenue is all built around R2, and then some of the variants that come following R2," Scaringe said.

For the most recent period, Rivian said the automotive cost of goods sold per vehicle improved by more than $12,000 quarter over quarter, helped by a higher R2 mix and better fixed-cost leverage.

Rivian also is in the midst of building a new multibillion-dollar Georgia factory that Scaringe has said is necessary to get the company to the volumes it needs to achieve net profitability.

Berdasarkan laporan, its sole factory in normal, illinois, is capable of producing 215,000 vehicles annually. That includes up to 155,000 R2s alongside R1 models and electric vans. Rivian said the Georgia plant will be capable of producing up to 300,000 units annually once the initial phase construction is completed in late 2028.

Of course, all of that means additional capital spending and pressure on the company to improve profits.

"We've made the decision to simultaneously work towards profitability … and deeply invest in our technology, and in particular in autonomy," Scaringe said.

Rivian's operating performance is improving, but several Wall Street analysts expect the company's investment requirements to rise significantly in 2027.

Rivian generated $176 million of consolidated gross profit in the third quarter, but its automotive business posted an $80 million gross loss, while its software and services unit generated $256 million of gross profit at a 42% margin.

Wall Street analysts broadly agree Rivian's R2 launch is showing encouraging early demand and lowering manufacturing costs, but they're concerned about whether that can offset rising autonomy spending, the Georgia factory buildout and continued cash burn.

Berdasarkan laporan, "funding has long been a key debate for rivian investors," deutsche bank analyst edison yu said in an oct. 30 investor note after the company reported quarterly results that exceeded Wall Street's expectations. "The notion of a multi-year (even if credible) path to cash flow breakeven will be less attractive to investors. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa rivian said during its late october earnings call that its total available future liquidity is expected to be about $13 billion when factoring in available credit and money from partnerships with volkswagen and uber as well as a $4. 5 billion U. S. Department of Energy loan for the Georgia plant.

Diungkapkan bahwa rivian said its cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments balance was $5. 5 billion to end the third quarter.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the company may still need to raise more capital. Scaringe said Rivian plans to be "opportunistic" about any additional capital raises, which have previously included equity deals with Volkswagen and Uber.

Berdasarkan laporan, "as we think about the environment looking out, we want to continue to position ourselves to be in a place to invest in the technology. And so that means we'll be opportunistic as it pertains to capital. But I want to be clear: We're like very focused on getting the profitability," Scaringe said.

The company has significantly upgraded the software capabilities and hardware on its vehicles to prepare them for autonomy technologies, or physical artificial intelligence, as Scaringe calls it.

The next step in that is releasing "point-to-point" driving capabilities, in which the vehicles can drive on their own from destination to destination with the driver acting as a monitor in case of any unexpected problems.

Diungkapkan bahwa u. EV leader Tesla is the only automaker to currently offer those features on its vehicles. S. Scaringe said Rivian plans to not only catch up to Tesla's capabilities but exceed them as it uses multiple sensor types to allow the vehicle to "see" better, especially in inclement weather.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "that's not like the finish line. Think of it as like the starting point where you suddenly have a more apples to apples comparison between Rivian and Tesla," Scaringe said.

The release of point-to-point over the coming weeks and months, first to employees and then to customers, is expected to be followed by autonomous vehicles with Uber by 2028.

Scaringe said he believes such technologies will become a differentiator for the company in the coming years.

Diungkapkan bahwa "i think it will go from a purchase consideration for maybe 10% of the buying public that's in the top five things considered in making a purchase decision to the no. 1 or No. 2 purchase consideration for the vast majority of buyers," Scaringe said.

Berdasarkan laporan, rivian plans to offer more details about its ai and autonomous plans during a second annual investor technology event on dec. 9.

"We view this as a likely positive catalyst as the event could set a path for AV features driving incremental vehicle demand & higher [software] revenue in 2027, building on 2026 growth," TD Cowen analyst Itay Michaeli said in an investor note last week.

Sebagaimana diketahui, rivian's stock is currently rated overweight with a $17. 70 target price, according to analyst estimates compiled by FactSet. That would be a roughly 26% increase from its Monday closing price but still a far cry from its IPO.

#73. The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity

📅 09 Nov 2026

The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity

Tanggal: 09 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11/09/1148194/the-backlash-about-data-centers-might-really-just-be-about-electricity/

Berdasarkan laporan, big tech sees a culture war over progress. But the real fault line is electricity: drawing it from the grid and generating it onsite provoke different kinds of backlash, neither easily solved by public relations.

Diungkapkan bahwa this story originally appeared in the algorithm, our weekly newsletter on ai. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here.

Diungkapkan bahwa as voters went to the polls across the us last week, i was in ashburn, virginia, part of what’s known as data center alley—the world’s largest data center hub. It’s also where the backlash now sweeping the country arguably first began taking shape.

Berdasarkan laporan, driving through it is surreal. Concrete monolithic buildings loom along every major road, with names like Skybox and CloudHQ.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it’s accepted wisdom in big tech that the war against data centers must be about something bigger than just data centers themselves. Two days after the midterms, OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer, Chris Lehane, wrote that data centers “have become a proxy for public unease about affordability, corporate power, and people losing control over their futures. ” It’s a culture war, in other words.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but spending a few days in data center alley left me wondering if it’s really the proxy that lehane describes. I came away convinced that the data center backlash is more about electricity than Big Tech admits. The industry can improve its image, but it can’t escape the physical consequences of its enormous appetite for electricity.

Sebagaimana diketahui, here’s why. There are two ways to power the sort of data center that AI companies want: connecting to the grid, or generating electricity onsite. In Virginia’s Loudoun County, where data centers are ubiquitous but have been built at a steadier pace than the breakneck expansion now underway elsewhere in the country, most are connected to the existing grid.

Berdasarkan laporan, one facility i went inside, operated by equinix, has massive diesel generators onsite for backup but gets its power from the local utility, dominion energy. Much of Dominion’s electricity is generated by natural gas (which is cleaner than coal or oil, but worse than renewables).

Sebagaimana diketahui, the average data center operating in this part of virginia today has a power capacity of 54 megawatts. That’s more than the power draw of the Denver International Airport.

Diungkapkan bahwa elena schlossberg, a prominent activist against data centers in virginia, told me she’s “always banging my head against the wall” when the industry paints the fight as a culture war. “It was always about power,” she says—that is, electricity.

Sebagaimana diketahui, some virginia protesters appear more animated by a broader anti-tech populism than schlossberg, to be fair. But it’s the particular consequences of drawing so much power from the grid that have done the most to shape how the backlash has played out.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, recent protests have led to new rules from the state that data centers must pay fully for the cost of new transmission lines to the grid and make sure they’re not spread among everyone else. Data center developers told me they’re preparing for new rules that would cut them off from grid power during peak demand. Schlossberg also worries about the downstream effects of a strained grid—for example, that data centers will run more diesel generators or that Dominion Energy will expand fossil fuel inputs rather than renewables to meet demand.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the overwhelming majority of ai data centers being built elsewhere in the country are not designed this way. Building there means bringing your own power (so-called “behind the meter” power), in the form of natural-gas-powered turbines. Companies also build diesel generators for backup. Anthropic, for example, has reportedly agreed to pay $3. The scale desired is so massive that companies are setting up in rural areas where there is virtually no grid infrastructure to connect to. 4 billion for gas turbines in what’s described as the largest power generation purchase by an AI company.

Sebagaimana diketahui, even if grids were nearby, they’d be unlikely to serve the amount of power demanded. The smallest data centers attractive for AI training are 300 megawatts. It’s a lot of power for one industrial site, but not unprecedented: One data center developer told me he’s eyeing a former steel mill already equipped to draw that much electricity from the grid.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but the ideal facilities are more like 6,000 megawatts. That’s the estimated draw of the city of Chicago, which is powered by more than 20 power plants within the city alone (and dozens farther out).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the notion of data center companies’ bringing their own power might seem attractive at first, because they wouldn’t be straining the grid. But generating electricity at this scale inevitably affects surrounding communities, and when public utilities build infrastructure of this magnitude, communities have traditionally expected a say in where it goes. Now, private companies are undertaking projects on a similar scale.

Diungkapkan bahwa natural-gas turbines of any scale release air pollutants. When diesel generators are used, it’s even worse. And in the unprecedented rush to get these facilities operating, companies have become horrible neighbors (recall that Elon Musk violated air quality laws when he set up dozens of turbines to power a data center in Memphis, according to the Environmental Protection Agency).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, big tech’s tendency to chalk the backlash up to a culture war obfuscates one simple fact: there’s only so pleasant you can make a small city of computers to live around. Sure, companies can pursue better deals that raise tax revenues, hire local workers, and get more community involvement, as the protests are leading them to do. But if a small town is asked to welcome a Walt Disney World, an international airport, a steel plant, and the power plants to run them all, should we be surprised by its trepidation?.

Diungkapkan bahwa again, that’s not to say this is the sole reason for opposition to data centers. Fears of job losses, existential risks, and concentrated corporate power all fuel the backlash, as does misinformation (most facilities use far less water than many people think). Nor is consuming enormous amounts of electricity inherently bad: Many of the advances that have improved modern life have required just that.

Diungkapkan bahwa but as one developer recently told me, industry insiders see their ambitions as constrained less by public opposition than by a lack of electricity. That should tell us something.

Sebagaimana diketahui, so what happens next? it’s possible that newly elected politicians’ actual stances on data centers won’t be as negative as the ones they campaigned on. That might mean the Permian Basin, where a network of natural-gas lines can be easy for developers to connect to and populations are sparse. But what seems true regardless is that if new data centers need their own power generated onsite, they’ll go where there are the fewest people able to resist them. Companies might also try their chances abroad; Google, in fact, announced the day after the elections that it will spend $15 billion on data center projects in Malaysia.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but there’s one place where big tech may find virtually no limits at all, as elon musk posted just hours after the midterms results came rolling in: “data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now. ”.

Ten years after AlphaGo’s match against Go champion Lee Sedol, today’s AI still isn’t tapping into the machinery that made that win possible.

#74. New York is forcing T-Mobile to stop putting data caps on low-income home internet plans

📅 11 Nov 2026

New York is forcing T-Mobile to stop putting data caps on low-income home internet plans

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.engadget.com/2314341/new-york-is-forcing-t-mobile-to-stop-putting-data-caps-on-low-income-home-internet-plans/

The company was throttling speeds for plans offered under the Affordable Broadband Act.

Diungkapkan bahwa new york's attorney general found that t-mobile was not following the state's affordable broadband act, which sets requirements for offering service to low-income residents. Under the ABA, eligible households must be able to purchase broadband at speeds of at least 25 Mbps for $15 a month or 200 Mbps for $20 a month without additional taxes or equipment fees. Providers are also required to make "reasonable efforts" to promote these low-cost options.

Berdasarkan laporan, the office of the attorney general discovered that t-mobile had placed monthly data caps on its aba plans. According to the press release, T-Mobile would throttle speeds to as low as 650 kilobits per second after a customer had used 50GB of data, which could happen in about four days of typical broadband use. The company was also only offering its ABA plans in areas where it had 5G wireless deployed and was preventing information about those plans on its website from being seen by search engines.

Following the investigation, T-Mobile will remove those data caps, make its ABA plans available in all places in the state where it offers home internet service, and will ensure that search engines can access details about ABA plans.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "reliable and affordable internet service is a basic need for all new yorkers, but t-mobile flouted the law designed to help vulnerable new yorkers access it," attorney general letitia james said. I encourage all eligible New Yorkers to enroll in a low-cost home internet plan through the ABA. "My office is committed to seeing the Affordable Broadband Act realize its goal of ensuring that New Yorkers in need are not denied access to affordable home internet. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in a statement shared with engadget, t-mobile the company said "we have a long history of helping customers in new york stay connected through low-cost broadband, and we're updating our plan to meet the state's requirements while maintaining the same low price. We've reached an agreement with the New York Attorney General that builds on that commitment, provides greater clarity around our offering and makes the plan available to more eligible customers. ".

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/11/ukraine-says-spacex-starshield-is-restricted-again-spacex-claims-it-isnt/

Report: Ukraine suspects speeds limits are intended to help Russia in peace talks.

Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said today that Starshield has again been disabled on fast-moving drones in Ukrainian territory occupied by Russian forces, and that the US has provided “very little” information about the return of the restriction.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we have detected speed restrictions on starshield on our ukrainian territory again, in the temporarily occupied parts of ukraine,” zelenskyy said in a speech at the 9th european political community summit in ireland. “The speed limit is back at 161 kilometers per hour—that’s 100 miles per hour. ”.

Zelenskyy’s allegation is that Starshield—the military variant of SpaceX’s Starlink satellite service—stops working on Ukrainian military drones when they travel above 161 kilometers per hour.

Sebagaimana diketahui, spacex today denied zelenskyy’s allegation. “This is false. There has been no change,” SpaceX’s media relations department told Ars today when asked if SpaceX has any response to Zelenskyy’s statement that Starshield is being restricted again.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, spacex has received multiple pentagon contracts to give ukraine access to the military-focused starshield. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said last month that any decisions on Starshield restrictions are made by the US government. The Pentagon inspector general’s office has since declined a request from US senators to investigate who ordered the restrictions.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ukraine officials reportedly said today that they believe the limit was reinstated to put pressure on ukraine in the latest round of peace talks with russia. Zelenskyy said in today’s speech that without satellite connectivity on its drones, Ukraine cannot intercept Russian drones that fly in from the occupied parts of Ukraine.

Berdasarkan laporan, it has often been unclear whether us and ukrainian government officials discussing the restrictions were referring to starlink, the civilian service that isn’t supposed to be used for offensive military purposes, or starshield, which relies on the same technology but is intended for military use. But today, Zelenskyy clearly stated that the current restrictions affect Starshield.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “this directly affects our ability to intercept russian jet-powered shahed drones,” zelenskyy said. “These drones come from those [occupied] areas, and because of the speed restrictions, we simply cannot catch up with them in time. And without the speed we need, shooting down these Shaheds becomes much harder. Only drone interceptors can operate there. This means more Russian strikes get through, and more of our people are killed, our civilians are killed, by Russia. Near the front line, we cannot use our aircraft. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, ukraine officials reported the first round of restrictions about a month ago, but the limits were removed by october 24. Zelenskyy said today that Ukraine doesn’t know why the limit is in place again.

Berdasarkan laporan, “we are trying to get the details from the american side, but so far we know very little,” zelenskyy said. If someone in America is making decisions that basically treat Ukrainian territory as if it is not Ukrainian, then this tells us where things are going. “But some things are very clear. We need to be clear and never recognize Russia’s occupation of Ukrainian territory in any way. ”.

A Financial Times article today described Ukrainian officials’ allegations that the Starshield limit was put back in place to influence peace talks:.

Berdasarkan laporan, senior ukrainian officials told the ft they believed the speed restrictions were imposed in an effort to pressure kyiv during the latest peace talks with russia, which just concluded in abu dhabi. US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, were in Moscow on Thursday to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin, after which they were set to travel to Ireland to meet Zelenskyy. One senior Ukrainian official said it appeared that Washington wanted to strengthen Russia’s position in the talks.

Berdasarkan laporan, “these are not random errors, but systematic speed restrictions,” zelenskyy said. “For us, this primarily means a significant complication in intercepting Russian jet-powered drones. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, musk last month accused ukraine of using the starlink commercial service for offensive drone strikes, which he said violates the terms of service. A Ukraine official denied Musk’s accusation and said previous limits imposed by SpaceX already prevented Ukraine’s military from using the commercial Starlink service in the way Musk described.

Berdasarkan laporan, as for the starshield military variant, musk has said that “starshield systems are owned and controlled by the us government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS. ” Trump denied making the decision to limit Ukraine’s satellite connectivity, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the administration had “no foreknowledge” of the slowdown.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we contacted the white house today and will update this article if we get a response. European Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier said that restrictions on Ukraine’s use of Starshield are unacceptable.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it is not the first time that ukraine is facing starshield disruptions. “SpaceX must have a consistent approach in sharing its services with Ukraine. These reports are deeply concerning and, if confirmed, unacceptable,” Regnier said at a press conference. Starshield services must be restored urgently for Ukraine to keep its soldiers connected, to protect its citizens, and to defend its territory. ”.

#79. United is restricting AI agents from booking flights

📅 11 Nov 2026

United is restricting AI agents from booking flights

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.engadget.com/2314121/united-is-restricting-ai-agents-from-booking-flights/

The airline believes AI poses security risks and may violate DOT and FAA rules.

Berdasarkan laporan, united airlines has announced it will change ticking policies to restrict ai agents' from booking flights through its website, third-party travel agencies and flight aggregators. The airline joins a growing number of businesses, including JPMorgan Chase and Amazon, which block agents from using their products to avoid the security and privacy issues associated with them.

Sebagaimana diketahui, giving something like your payment details or log-in credentials to an agent can expose sensitive information and lead to "unintended purchases, account changes or use of mileageplus miles," united says. Allowing an AI agent to complete a booking could also violate existing airline regulations from the Department of Transportation and Federal Aviation Administration. For example, United says only a human can acknowledge that their bag doesn't contain explosives during flight check-in.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, united would like to avoid association with any agent-based embarrassments, for instance when meta's muse leaked a user's address online. The Wall Street Journal reports that United CEO Scott Kirby has been open about the company's reluctance to jump into agentic commerce. "To be honest, I don't want to create another middleman," Kirby said at an event on Tuesday. Like other companies, it also wants to keep AI from getting in the way of its relationship with customers. Not every airline feels the same way: Southwest created a plugin so users can book flights with ChatGPT.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, luckily for united and other companies blocking ai agents, agentic commerce might not be taking off with regular people. During its recent third-quarter earnings call, Uber shared that it handled 320 million trips and deliveries during the week of Halloween; of those, AI agents were responsible for 500 Uber Eats orders and only four rides. Those aren't exactly industry-destroying numbers.

Berdasarkan laporan, handing an ai your credit card is very different from handing it your email login, and both are different from just asking it to send you a news summary every morning. Even if a large number of people are downloading apps like Muse, it seems like letting an agent shop for you isn't as frictionless or foolproof as it needs to be to catch on.

#81. SoftBank’s billion-dollar loss may have put a cap on AI’s natural gas ambitions

📅 12 Nov 2026

SoftBank’s billion-dollar loss may have put a cap on AI’s natural gas ambitions

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/softbanks-billion-dollar-loss-may-have-put-a-cap-on-ais-natural-gas-ambitions/

SoftBank might not be the first to invest in a hot trend, but when it does, it goes big.

Sebagaimana diketahui, witness its $30 billion bet on openai in early 2025 or its announcement in february that its sb energy subsidiary would spend $33 billion on a 9. 2-gigawatt natural gas power plant. If you can’t be first, be biggest, I guess.

Berdasarkan laporan, that philosophy apparently spilled over into procurement, where orders were also supersized. Starting about two years ago, SoftBank reportedly put down deposits on more than 13 gigawatts of turbines, almost 50% more than it needed.

The decision to over-order undoubtedly helped secure turbines and speed up SoftBank’s projects.

“SB Energy did not have a choice except to overbook turbines in the future if they wanted some turbines right away,” Peter Gardett, CEO of Noreva, told TechCrunch via email.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the energy world was caught off guard by the swiftness and magnitude of ai’s rising power demands. Queues for turbine orders now extend into the early 2030s. As natural gas was shaping up to be a go-to power source for the AI boom, CEO Masayoshi Son bet that by deploying his investment firm’s significant war chest, he could corner a portion of the market. If the AI world wanted power for its data centers, it would have to come to him.

Sebagaimana diketahui, now that bet appears to have fizzled. 1 billion quarterly loss on Tuesday, with over half of that stemming from losses related to power-generating equipment. SoftBank announced a $7. The investor had paid turbine manufacturers nonrefundable deposits to secure orders, and now it considered much of those worthless.

Diungkapkan bahwa the move was also a costly bit of price discovery, gardett said. Rather than overpay and potentially still be short of turbines, SoftBank overpaid and over-ordered.

“This charge is just that price discovery finally happening,” Gardett said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the magnitude of that misplaced bet — over $3 billion — reflects some of the electricity mania that has overtaken the ai world. Faced with years-long waits to connect to the grid, many hyperscalers and developers have turned to natural gas as a sort of energy security blanket, something that is proven and familiar.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as ai data centers spend more time in operation, their operators are getting a better feel for what’s required to keep them operating. Natural gas might seem like a safe bet, but there are still risks, including winter curtailments when supplies dip and demand spikes, Brent Nelson, senior managing director of markets and strategy at Ascend Analytics, told the Equity podcast Wednesday.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in light of that, nelson said the grid might still be their best bet. To make up for the shortfall, large batteries are a cost-effective choice, Nelson said. Most data centers would be best served by a grid connection, albeit a smaller one than they might normally request. They’d help shave peak loads or ride out requests from the utility to curtail electricity use.

Data center operators might be coming to that same conclusion, leading the natural gas market to develop more slowly than SoftBank expected.

Berdasarkan laporan, softbank’s natural gas-related losses are unlikely to have a domino effect, leading to mass cancellations of gas power plants. AI’s power demand appears to be too large for that. For now, natural gas is riding high, though SoftBank may have found its ceiling.

#83. How GM is trying to talk used car shoppers into buying new vehicles

📅 10 Nov 2026

How GM is trying to talk used car shoppers into buying new vehicles

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/10/gm-carbravo-used-car-shoppers.html

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, affordability challenges are pushing some buyers out of the new vehicle market. Many are choosing used cars instead.

In turn, automakers are looking for ways to compete with many of the online retailers grabbing market share in the used car market and trying to bring some of those customers back into a new vehicle.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, new vehicle sales tend to be more profitable for automakers, but reselling trade-ins as used vehicles is highly profitable for dealers. Used car prices are relatively strong, but newer online retailers such as Carvana and CarMax have made the market more competitive for dealers and other incumbent used car sellers.

"The internet and technology and apps on our phone have changed every aspect of retail, and probably one of the slowest areas of retail to have adopted to online and digital shopping has been the auto industry," said Ivan Feinseth, partner, chief investment officer and director of research at Tigress Financial Partners.

Berdasarkan laporan, general motors is a key example of automakers' attempts to address this shifting market. It's essentially an online portal through which Chevrolet, Buick and GMC dealers can list their certified used vehicles and make them available to customers all over the U. The automaker has revamped its certified used vehicle program, which now operates under the CarBravo name. S.

Sebagaimana diketahui, about 1,615 of gm's 3,700 dealers are enrolled in the program, according to the company. The only GM brand not involved is Cadillac, which maintains its own program.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "certified" used or "preowned" vehicles are used cars that have undergone a thorough inspection and reconditioning. They typically come with guarantees and warranties from the manufacturer.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, many automakers have certified used programs for their own cars. But GM, as part of its revamp, is using CarBravo to certify vehicles made by other automakers. A lot of those cars arrive at dealerships as trade-ins, and often dealers will sell them to wholesale auctions, said John Fitzpatrick, senior manager of the CarBravo program.

"Wholesaling doesn't bring nearly the revenue that selling it to a new customer does," he said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, gm has said it is planning to net about 250,000 sales in its carbravo program in 2026. Fitzpatrick said he doesn't expect that even half of those will end up being new car sales.

Diungkapkan bahwa but through carbravo, the customer gets access to gm's dealership network for service, something fitzpatrick says is a key differentiator between its program and growing online sellers. CarBravo vehicles come with various warranties, depending on the age and mileage on the car.

Diungkapkan bahwa gm said the program is driving more traffic into local dealerships, where purchases are typically finalized. That creates an opportunity to convert a used car shopper into a new car buyer. So far, the automaker said about 38% of the shoppers initially looking for used cars end up buying new.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a customer who wants to buy a full-size truck can look on the website and compare used chevrolet silverados alongside used ford f-150s and ram 1500s, for example. The buyer might settle on a used truck from any of those brands, but a conversation with a dealer can push them in a different direction.

"The customer picks up the phone, but in the back of their mind, they maybe always have been a traditional, more new car customer," Fitzpatrick said.

Berdasarkan laporan, "you've shown the customer, you're going to pay $500 [per month] for this used f-150, but you may pay $510 or $515 for this new chevy," he said. "And now all of a sudden the customer says, yeah, maybe I can do that because I'd rather have that new vehicle than the used truck. ".

While the average transaction price of a new vehicle is about $50,000, the average 3-year-old used car costs about $30,000 as of September, according to Cox Automotive.

However, industry analysts say customers base their purchasing decisions on the cost of the monthly payment more than on the sticker price of the car.

New cars often come with longer-term loan options than used ones, Feinseth said, which can result in lower monthly payments.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "on a 1- or 2-year-old car, you may be only stuck with a 3- or 4-year loan," he said. "On a new car, you can get a 5-year, 6-year loan. ".

The share of new car loans lasting 84 months hit a new record in the third quarter, at more than 1 in 4 loans, according to Edmunds.

Meanwhile, used car prices in some affordable segments have risen, according to Cox Automotive, and about three quarters of consumers express some interest in certified cars.

Berdasarkan laporan, but the key is building the relationship with the customer, he said. About 50% of the buyers GM has gained through the program appear to be new to the brand, meaning there is no record of them in any of the automaker's customer databases. About 70% had never visited the dealership they ended up purchasing from.

Berdasarkan laporan, "the goal is really to get that customer engaged with the store, give them the option of building a relationship with the dealer," he said. "The dealer can really help the customer figure out what works for their budget. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, it's a boon for dealers too: customers buying warranty-backed used cars often return to the dealership for service visits — which often account for about half of a dealership's profits. GM can also sell subscriptions to connected vehicle services, such as its OnStar, which provides safety, security and navigation services.

"That is a big part of General Motors' business going forward, is to sell the software and subscription services like OnStar and eventually to the cars that are enabled with Super Cruise," GM's advanced driver-assistance system, Feinseth said.

GM isn't the only automaker trying to use its certified preowned vehicle program to lure buyers.

Berdasarkan laporan, detroit rival ford motor also certifies vehicles made by other manufacturers through its ford blue advantage program. It is on track to do 450,000 total sales in 2026, more than GM's 250,000 target. It didn't specify how many of those buyers end up purchasing new vehicles.

Toyota told CNBC in an email that about 40% of its used car shoppers end up buying new instead.

Sebagaimana diketahui, honda didn't give specifics about its program. But Lance Woelfer, American Honda's vice president of automobile sales, said conversions happen "probably every day at dealerships throughout the country. ".

#85. Nancy Pelosi’s replacement is ready to regulate AI

📅 09 Nov 2026

Nancy Pelosi’s replacement is ready to regulate AI

Tanggal: 09 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11/09/1148182/nancy-pelosis-replacement-is-ready-to-regulate-ai/

Sebagaimana diketahui, scott wiener has made ai regulation a cornerstone of his political career. Now he’s headed to Congress.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as a california state senator, scott wiener authored legislation aimed at curbing the risks of advanced ai. Now, after winning a tight congressional race for former Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi’s open San Francisco seat, he could play a key role in setting federal AI policy.

Diungkapkan bahwa i spoke with wiener on friday, only a few hours after he had been declared the victor. But he was already thinking about AI risk. The previous day, the AI nonprofit METR had released a report that had been widely interpreted as evidence that Anthropic had achieved recursive self-improvement, a phenomenon in which AI meaningfully contributes to its own advancement and AI progress potentially spins out of control.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it’s very concerning,” wiener said, citing the report as evidence that we are quickly running out of time to regulate ai. “That does not appear to be happening. “It was my hope that Congress would take decisive action before [the end of] this year,” he said. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, wiener has been increasingly focused on ai in recent years, and he’s made many of the ai safety movement’s concerns his own: during our 20-minute conversation, he used the phrase “recursive self-improvement” half a dozen times, for example. “Because it’s moving very quickly, and we could sleepwalk into a disaster. “We need to slow this down,” he says. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, wiener has already had real influence on ai policy. SB 1047, a bill that he authored in 2024, was set to become the first real piece of frontier AI legislation in the country before it was vetoed by California governor Gavin Newsom; he then sponsored SB 53, a lighter-touch bill that Newsom signed. Both bills have inspired proposed federal legislation.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, wiener’s congressional campaign received over $3 million from public first action, a nonprofit in favor of ai regulation that receives substantial funding from anthropic. That contribution led opponents to criticize him for being too close to the AI industry, but Wiener says that couldn’t be further from the truth.

Diungkapkan bahwa “public first supported me because i was the first lawmaker in the country to introduce ai regulation and the first to pass it and get it implemented,” he wrote in a message after our interview. “The attacks on me for [Public First’s] support were shockingly cynical—literally attacking a candidate who actually regulated AI over Big Tech’s objection and falsely claiming the candidate is somehow too close to Big Tech. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa wiener says that if congress forms a select committee on artificial intelligence—something that democrats have discussed since september—he’d be eager to serve. And he’s enthusiastic about many of the policy ideas floating around Congress. “I think it’s really important to have a strong, empowered, nimble federal regulator,” he says, noting that Representative Ro Khanna, a fellow Democrat from California, has proposed legislation to establish such a regulator.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he also highlights the importance of whistleblower protections, testing and auditing requirements, and a kill switch requirement, and he wants to see congress leverage its oversight powers to hold the ai labs to account. “This is about the future of humanity, and we want to make sure that the public has a say and that the public knows what's going on,” he says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and as a longtime state legislator, he is opposed to broad federal preemption of state ai laws, which some of the proposed federal legislation would require. “States are, as Brandeis says, laboratories,” he notes. “You want the states to be able to continue to be nimble in ways that Congress sometimes is not. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, above all, wiener says, he wants congress to pass policies with real teeth. Once you’re in that realm, that really is potentially a recipe for total loss of control. That means taking seriously the possibility of AI catastrophe, something he discusses in the sort of language typically used by AI safety experts. “We’re in a moment that is very dangerous in terms of the risk of loss of control over AI,” he told me. “It’s critically important that when Congress acts, that we do so in a way that is truly meaningful and that meets the moment,” he says. “We need to deal with recursive self-improvement. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, he’ll have some allies in the fight against catastrophic ai risk. But there’s still a large gap between Wiener’s Bay Area, AGI-pilled perspective and the national mood on AI, which is anchored by opposition to data centers. Senator Bernie Sanders, for instance, has met with many of the AI safety movement’s most influential figures and has spoken repeatedly about AI and existential risk. The fact that voters approved 40 out of 41 anti-data-center ballot measures on Tuesday might seem to be a good sign for Wiener and others who support AI regulation, but Wiener says he sees this movement as far more tied to local concerns than to bigger questions about AI risk.

Diungkapkan bahwa “peoople who are really opposed to where ai is going—this is an area where they can actually do something about it,” he says. “But the data center revolt—to me, I think it’s more so that people are upset that there could be something like this in their community, with all the impacts near people’s homes, driving up electric bills and using water. I think that’s the bigger issue for most people, from what I can tell. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa wiener describes himself as only “cautiously optimistic” about congress’s ability to rein in ai, given its poor track record on regulating the tech industry. He also has concerns about the ability to get legislation past President Donald Trump, who called concerns about catastrophic AI risk a “hoax” in September and has demonstrated a stark unwillingness to collaborate with China, something that Wiener sees as essential to preventing the worst consequences of AI.

Berdasarkan laporan, but he says trump’s unpredictability provides  some measure of hope, though it’s a fraught kind of hope. And I hope if that’s what it does take—which, like I said, I hope it doesn’t—but if it does, I hope it’s as small as possible. “So far what we’ve seen are some problematic things, but not complete disasters,” Wiener says. “I hope that it doesn’t take a disaster to spur the president into acting. ”.

Ten years after AlphaGo’s match against Go champion Lee Sedol, today’s AI still isn’t tapping into the machinery that made that win possible.

#88. Phota Labs uses AI to turn everyday photos into professional-looking shots

📅 12 Nov 2026

Phota Labs uses AI to turn everyday photos into professional-looking shots

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/phota-labs-uses-ai-to-turn-everyday-photos-into-professional-looking-shots/

A new iOS app called Phota Labs gives users access to a personal AI photo assistant that turns everyday snapshots into images that look like they were taken by a professional photographer, all while preserving the authenticity of the image.

Rather than giving consumers yet another photo-editing tool, Phota Labs aims to use advances in AI to automate the editing process so it’s easier for anyone to get access to better photos.

The a16z-backed startup was founded by Cecilia Zhang and Zach Xia, who met at Adobe while working on computational photography products, including Project Indigo, Lightroom, and Photoshop.

Berdasarkan laporan, the duo saw a gap in the editing tools on the market and believed that although editing tools can be powerful for enhancing photos, they aren’t very effective at fixing a photo that wasn’t captured well in the first place. Phota Labs changes that by focusing on fixing the shot itself while preserving the natural appearances of those in the image.

Berdasarkan laporan, “phota is your personal photo assistant that can make great photos for any moment you want to keep before you even ask, which means that it’s a very proactive experience,” zhang told techcrunch in an interview. “Think of it almost like a photographer or virtual photographer who looks over your camera roll and tries to understand what’s happening and how they could have taken that photo for you on the spot for that scene. ”.

The idea is to use AI to transform photos, whether that’s turning a wide-angle group photo into a tighter portrait or transforming a selfie into a regular shot.

Users can choose from different photography styles that determine how AI transforms their images, ranging from subtle edits that preserve the original lens and composition to more dramatic transformations that introduce effects like fish-eye lenses, alternative angles, and entirely different perspectives.

While some people turn to ChatGPT and other generative AI tools to enhance or edit images, these tools can often alter a person’s appearance, especially when working with blurry photos because they don’t know what that person actually looks like.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “for phota, we built our own tech,” zhang said. ”We built this personalization technology that actually learns about people’s identity and is able to preserve them in any transformation we do to a photo. ”.

Images edited with Phota Labs feature invisible watermarks that identify them as altered by AI when shared on social platforms.

Diungkapkan bahwa the startup is initially targeting people who take tons of photos and like to share them on social media, but don’t want to deal with the tedious process of editing photos. Over time, the founders envision a broader audience, from retirees looking to create beautiful photos for their grandchildren to parents who want to share polished family albums with friends and relatives.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we have this obsession with authenticity,” xia said. That’s why we spend a lot of research into understanding personal context, into building this identity model because we want to make sure the photos are authentic. “I think there’s so much value in connecting AI with real moments and making sure those photos are not perfect, in a sense. They’re just better photos of the same moment, rather than saying, ‘Oh, this is an AI image’. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, xia said beta users were excited to see better versions of moments they had actually lived and saw the results as photos of real memories rather than ai-generated images. The founders discovered that users were taking more photos because they knew Phota Labs could enhance them later.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we’re turning something that’s unusable into something that people want to print,” zhang said. There’s so many cherished moments for photos, and we really want them to be actually meaningful and something that you can remember. So, I think that meant so much to us. “People who just love photos but never really got into editing can now experience professional quality that could never have been possible. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in terms of funding, the company raised a $5. 6 million seed round led by a16z last year.

Sebagaimana diketahui, phota labs is launching as a free app to build an initial user base before exploring a freemium model. The startup also plans to launch an Android app in the future.

Skydance is pulling back the curtain on how it plans to achieve at least $6 billion in cost savings in the next three years.

"By combining two global streaming services, two film and TV studio groups, two television portfolios, and overlapping corporate functions, we can reduce duplicative spend across an expense base of more than $50 billion," the company wrote in a letter to shareholders Monday as part of Paramount Skydance's third-quarter earnings release.

Sebagaimana diketahui, skydance, the company formed by the combination of paramount skydance and warner bros. Discovery, said it projects at least $2. 2 billion in cost reductions from eliminating "redundant back-office and corporate functions," including eliminating management layers and ramping the use of artificial intelligence. Those savings also account for "rationalizing" its office footprint.

Berdasarkan laporan, skydance expects at least $1 billion in savings from streamlining marketing and promotional spending. And around $1. 4 billion in savings will come from unifying its streaming businesses and broadcast architecture and integrating back-end technology.

Berdasarkan laporan, a final $1. 4 billion in savings will be tied to "optimizing third-party spend," eliminating overlapping expenses, and consolidating purchasing decisions to one centralized group, Skydance said.

Diungkapkan bahwa "we are confident in achieving these savings, drawing on our playbook from paramount," the company wrote. "That program is on track to achieve over $2. 7 billion in run-rate efficiencies by the end of 2026. ".

Some of that cost-cutting has already begun.

Sebagaimana diketahui, last month, skydance began offering voluntary buyouts to employees ahead of official layoffs. At the same time, the company adopted a five-day-per-week in-office policy. Additionally, last week saw the departure of eight executives — four from Warner Bros. and four from Paramount.

The company has previously said it plans to eventually merge the Paramount+ and HBO Max streaming services into a single platform.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on monday, skydance said it would take the first step toward that goal early next year, offering a bundle of the streaming services "at an even greater value. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, co-ceo ynon kreiz told investors during the company's earnings call that skydance is also looking for ways to optimize its content budget. The company spends more than $30 billion annually on shows and films.

"As one company, we can make smarter choices about how we distribute and monetize both new content and library content," Kreiz said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, skydance noted that it's expecting a $200 million headwind in the fourth quarter from theatrical underperformances at warner bros. studio related to already launched titles and upcoming releases.

The company will also utilize AI to speed up production and decrease costs to make films, co-CEO and chairman David Ellison said on the call.

"We think these tools will help unlock more original storytelling by being able to make the budget more digestible to be able to take that amount of risk," Ellison said.

Diungkapkan bahwa the updates came alongside third-quarter results for the legacy paramount skydance company that included revenue of $7. 04 billion, and adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of $1 billion, topping StreetAccount estimates of $913. 03 billion, which was roughly in line with StreetAccount estimates of $7. 5 million.

However, adjusted earnings per share of 45 cents were not immediately comparable to StreetAccount EPS estimates.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the results don't include the impact of the warner bros. Discovery acquisition, which closed after the end of the third quarter.

Skydance detailed business units of the combined entity, including studios, direct-to-consumer and TV, and said it will provide full-year guidance during its fourth-quarter earnings report early next year.

Berdasarkan laporan, "going forward, we will provide guidance on an annual basis, as we prioritize long-term value creation, which we believe will be more consistent with our strategic approach," the company told shareholders. "We will continue to provide quarterly updates, including certain forward-looking commentary where applicable, which will give investors visibility into our near-term progress of the business. ".

The school warned her parents and averted the danger after an internal system flagged a chat labeled “Funeral,” but Emma’s story stoked fears of parents joining protests not just in Durham, but also in Boston; Boulder, Colorado; Chicago; Los Angeles; New York City; and Portland, Oregon.

Emma’s lawsuit accuses Google of exploiting its dominant position in education technology and “sneaking” Gemini into Chromebooks, while falsely marketing them as safe.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “as a direct consequence of google’s choices, emma was baited by its defectively designed products into repeated, unmonitored, sycophantic ai chatbot interactions on her school chromebook without her parents ever knowing. Berdasarkan laporan, cassie creswell, executive director of ilfps, told ars that she’s been an advocate monitoring edtech issues for more than a decade. And even she was blindsided by Google’s AI moves.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i am aware of ai overviews when you search, which have a whole slew of problems, but i did not know that you really actually just have an interface where you can interact with gemini in the chatbot way on everyone’s chromebook still in chicago public schools,” creswell said. “And that’s so disturbing. ”.

Meanwhile, schools seem to be part of the transparency problem.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, creswell said that currently, the chicago school district “is telling us their official line is that kids don’t have access to generative ai tools and that we don’t need a district-level policy on generative ai because they have guidebooks. ” However, she’s reviewed Google’s CPS contracts, and they suggest that kids are interacting with generative AI and frontier models. Diungkapkan bahwa creswell told ars that parents are particularly upset that google is not transparent about how it processes and uses student data. She’s exhaustively researched Google contracts through Freedom of Information Act requests and told Ars that dozens of agreements she reviewed offer no indication of how CPS partners like Google—as well as Anthropic and OpenAI—are handling student data. Berdasarkan laporan, “any sort of transparency on what is actually happening in terms of the data that they collect and what they do with it, that is absolutely missing,” creswell said. And “it’s very unclear what data is being saved. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, to creswell and other advocates, it seems likely that kids’ data is collected no matter what, since “even if you do ‘-ai,’ and you don’t get a text summary, your search data and what’s being returned is all basically inside the generative ai model. ” Although Illinois law only allows commercial use of de-identified data, parents think Google should clearly explain what steps it takes to ensure data can’t be recombined to re-identify kids.

Berdasarkan laporan, ars reached out to google to see if the company could clarify if creswell’s read is accurate or if there’s any meaningful distinction between adding “-ai” to an individual query versus building a button that would automatically add “-ai” to every query. Google did not clarify, instead emphasizing that schools will control whether students can access the Gemini app, Gemini Notebook, and Search, with options to toggle each off individually, but no option to use Search without AI.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, emma doe’s lawsuit alleged that google has taken advantage of a dominant position it has held in schools since 2007 to push ai on kids and seize their data without meaningfully protecting them from the worst potential harms of its chatbot’s sycophantic design. Over the next two extensions of that contract, no updates were introduced to protect students’ privacy as AI advanced.

Diungkapkan bahwa currently, that policy specifies that “we receive customer data through the core services and process it according to the school’s (the customer’s) instructions. This customer data includes anything submitted, stored, sent, or received through Core Services by you or your school. ” Google collects that data on that activity, as well as account information “like name, email address and password” and location information, the policy said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the policy didn’t discuss gemini but noted that data from using core services helps maintain services, improve personalization, and increase security. Diungkapkan bahwa parents’ privacy concerns go beyond google, creswell noted. But since Google has “captured so much of the education space and so much of the education experience,” parents are focusing their energy on interrogating those AI systems in schools early on.

Diungkapkan bahwa in chicago, a recently re-elected cps school board member, karen zaccor, is pushing for an ai moratorium in schools after talking with city and community colleges about an allegedly noticeable decline in reading, math, and writing skills from students graduating from cps schools. Sebagaimana diketahui, at the google protest wednesday, parents waved signs that threatened to eject google from schools, with slogans like “no google + no ai = win/win. ” Many kids used favorite cartoon characters from shows like Beavis and Butthead and South Park to slam Google’s seemingly cynical approach to introducing AI in schools. Sebagaimana diketahui, “what about the future of our youth?” mackey said. “What about the future of our minds?”.

#96. Watch SpaceXs wildest test yet: A 22-hour flight and a historic return

📅 13 Nov 2026

Watch SpaceXs wildest test yet: A 22-hour flight and a historic return

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://mashable.com/science/spacex-test-two-catches-starship-ship-and-booster

SpaceX will try to catch both halves of its giant Starship in one launch, grabbing the booster minutes after liftoff and the ship nearly a full day later.

Diungkapkan bahwa no one has pulled off such a feat before. If both attempts work, the company says it will become the first to recover an entire orbital rocket for reuse. SpaceX has caught its Super Heavy booster three times before, but it has never tried to catch the the ship — the part that actually reaches orbit — until now.

Berdasarkan laporan, this test, known as flight 15, seeks to make a leap in progress and could launch as soon as friday, nov. 13. Starship's flight 14 test was the first to enter orbit, but controllers cut its planned nine-hour mission short. This time, SpaceX wants the ship to stay in space for about 22 ½ hours and land both pieces back at its Starbase launch site in South Texas, where huge mechanical arms will be waiting to snatch them out of the air.

Diungkapkan bahwa the stakes reach far beyond texas. NASA is counting on Starship as one of two lunar landers, along with Blue Origin's Blue Moon, to put astronauts on the moon as soon as 2028. China, meanwhile, aims to land its own crew on the moon before 2030. SpaceX can only fly that often if it reuses its rockets the way airlines reuse jets. To get there, Starship must refuel in orbit, which takes a series of fuel-hauling launches. And while SpaceX juggles the NASA contract, founder Elon Musk is laser-focused on his personal ambition of getting the rocket and ship ready to carry people to Mars and build a city there.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if starship lifts off when the launch window opens at 5:45 p. m. CT Friday, the final ship catch after reentry into the atmosphere would happen around 4:18 p. m. m. ET / 4:45 p. m. m. ET / 4:15 p. m. SpaceX will livestream the flight on its website and X, starting around 5:15 p. CT Saturday. ET / 3:18 p. CT Friday, or about 30 minutes before liftoff.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this spaceflight will stress starship like never before. The ship will circle Earth about 14 times and release 26 new Starlink internet satellites. It will fly for about 21 hours until its path lines up with Starbase. Then, its engines must fire again to bring it home.

Berdasarkan laporan, "relying on this engine to get us there for that final one percent of a historic return-to-launch-site mission is pretty scary," said lars blackmore, senior principal mars landing engineer, in a new company video, "go for orbit. ".

Want more science and tech news delivered straight to your inbox? Sign up for Mashable's Light Speed newsletter or get Mashable push alerts today.

Berdasarkan laporan, the trip back to earth brings a new kind of risk. Every earlier Starship ended its flight with a splashdown in open ocean. This time, the ship will cross parts of northern Mexico and southern Texas, steering around the region's larger cities. People in and around Cameron County may hear sonic booms, the loud bangs a vehicle makes when it outruns the speed of sound.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but things might not work out as planned. If anything looks wrong, they can ditch the ship in the ocean instead. Controllers will only bring the ship home if it passes a set of FAA-approved health checks. SpaceX built into the timeline ways to bail out near Hawaii and off the coast of Chile.

The video shared in the above X post is an animation of what the Starship catch should look like during flight test 15 if all goes as planned.

Berdasarkan laporan, the september test showed why those backup plans matter. During the climb to space, one of the ship's engines shut down early. The team first called off the trip to orbit, then pressed ahead, apparently after Musk questioned the conservative decision.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we had thought, like, 'hey, let's not proceed if anything goes wrong,'" said jeremy pedro, director of starship engineering, in the video. "And Elon really questioned the requirements and asked us, 'Is there anything actually prohibiting us from going forward?'".

The ship successfully released all of its satellites, but controllers brought it down early near Hawaii.

Diungkapkan bahwa "on launch day, we get risks from the engine team, from avionics, from the computers, from the propulsion system, from all the plumbing on the rocket. We get risks from the tower and the catch arms," said Shana Diez, director of Starship engineering, in the video. We get risks from the launch pad. "But the goal is always to take the risk in the place where you can learn the most, and that's the calculus that we're doing every day. ".

#97. How many SpaceX Starship rocket tests have failed?

📅 11 Nov 2026

How many SpaceX Starship rocket tests have failed?

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.engadget.com/2314045/how-many-spacex-starship-rocket-tests-failed/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in late september 2026, spacex's starship entered orbit for the first time, deploying 26 starlink satellites in what was heralded as a major step for spacex's cosmic ambitions. However, the celebration was cut short when a failed engine forced the mission to end shortly after reaching orbit. The malfunction prevented the intended six-revolution trek through Earth's orbit, falling well short of its 10-hour goal.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this result is typical for starship, as the company's "fail fast, learn fast" mindset recasts the program's failures — anywhere between four and 11 of 14 total launches, depending on how generous you are — as opportunities for growth. This has been true since its first test flight in April 2023, which exploded 65 miles short of its intended climb into Earth's atmosphere. As Musk tweeted after the fiery test, "Congrats @SpaceX team on an exciting test launch of Starship! Learned a lot for next test launch. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, given spacex's success to date, it is hard to argue with the company's logic. According to analytics firm BryceTech, SpaceX launched 85 percent of all spacecraft in 2025, including over half the world's orbital launches. To boot, Starlink's 9,800 active satellites currently account for over half of the world's total, according to satellite tracker Orbital Radar.

Berdasarkan laporan, the largest and most powerful rocket ever assembled, starship has a cargo capacity five times larger than spacex's falcon 9 rocket. This makes it essential for SpaceX's grander ambitions, including its million-satellite constellation, NASA's lunar missions and Musk's Mars colony dream. With another launch set for November 13, 2026, stakeholders will soon see whether the September launch represented progress or foreshadowed further additions to SpaceX's growing list of frustrations.

Sebagaimana diketahui, gauging the success of the starship project is difficult. And while it has yet to deliver a fully-reusable rocket capable of missions to "Mars and beyond," progress was always going to be incremental. Although some missions may fit within a binary success-failure matrix, most land somewhere in between. As such, its only fair to judge each mission against its own standards of progress.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, starship's start was turbulent. After its initial test combusted within minutes, its second flight saw the first-stage booster separate before the booster and vessel met fiery ends. Five months later, Starship's third test flight completed many of its objectives, reaching an altitude of 145 miles before disintegrating on its return. SpaceX then had two back-to-back successful launches, culminating in its launch tower successfully catching Starship's first-stage booster.

Berdasarkan laporan, unfortunately, another troubled period followed. The FAA launched another investigation after Starship's eighth test exploded in space, grounding planes across Florida. Test six saw SpaceX call off its lauded mechanical arm before crashing the Super Heavy booster into the Gulf of Mexico. Two months later, Starship 7 exploded over the Bahamas just eight minutes after takeoff, sparking investigations by both the FAA and the Turks and Caicos government. Starship 9 achieved minor improvements before spinning out of control, forcing SpaceX to cancel its planned deployment of 8 mock satellites.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, starship followed the disastrous run with a pair of its most successful tests. In August 2025, Starship released its first cargo of Starlink satellites. Two months later, SpaceX successfully launched and landed its 11th Starship rocket, fulfilling all major objectives.

Diungkapkan bahwa starship's twelfth test launched its upgraded starship v3 rocket. In July 2026, Starship 13 successfully deployed 20 of Starlink's new high-powered satellites before its first-stage booster failed to stick the landing. While it accomplished several objectives, engine failures caused it to crash into the Gulf, triggering yet another FAA investigation. Considering its scattershot history, Starship 14's semi-successful run is par for the course.

Sebagaimana diketahui, judging each mission against its stated objectives, most starship launches have failed to meet expectations. SpaceX, however, would likely claim that its willingness to learn from mistakes puts its true failure rate closer to zero. The better question is whether the program is learning quickly enough to keep pace with its own meteoric ambitions.

Diungkapkan bahwa if one takes musk's proclamations as a measuring stick, starship has underdelivered. And with the once-every-26-months Mars launch window closing this November, you can guess which side of the coin SpaceX landed on. In 2025, Musk predicted there was a 50 percent chance Starship would land on Mars in 2026. Of course, Musk is notorious for overpromising, so this is business as usual at Starbase.

Diungkapkan bahwa earlier this year, nasa announced that the program had fallen behind schedule by at least two years since the agency selected spacex's rocket to carry its artemis moon lander in 2021. With China aiming to reach the moon by decade's end, the pressure is mounting. NASA hopes to return to the moon in 2028; to do so, Starship must meet the Artemis III deadline in summer 2027.

Sebagaimana diketahui, beyond being musk's conduit to mars, spacex's most ambitious projects depend on starship to slash costs. SpaceX's proposed 1 million-satellite datacenter constellation Starmind, for example, is impossible without a high-capacity reusable rocket. " During the event, Musk said the mission was "more likely than not" to succeed. The November 13 test should provide another data point to judge SpaceX's progress, especially given its ambitions. In a Q3 earnings call, Musk stated that SpaceX will attempt to catch both the rocket and its booster, making it the  "first time that an orbital launch vehicle has been fully recovered. Starship's history may say otherwise.

Lee was later the chief product officer at crypto payments company MobileCoin and helped the World Health Organization launch its mobile app during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Diungkapkan bahwa in april 2023, lee was found bleeding in a doorway on an empty downtown san francisco street after being stabbed in the hip and heart. He managed to call 911 but died after being taken to a hospital.

Berdasarkan laporan, following the killing but before an arrest was made, some of big tech's loudest voices were quick to frame it in terms that supported their biases. #105. Innovating with AI in the special chemicals industry

Innovating with AI in the special chemicals industry

Tanggal: 09 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11/09/1147654/innovating-with-ai-in-the-special-chemicals-industry/

Connected data, AI, and advanced modeling are helping scientists accelerate research and develop more sustainable materials.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as companies look to accelerate innovation with artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and advanced modeling, the primary challenge is connecting new technologies to reliable data, scientific expertise, and the practical realities of bringing products to market. For specialty chemicals manufacturer Lubrizol, digital transformation is all about giving researchers the tools to test ideas faster, make better-informed decisions, and develop more sustainable materials without compromising performance.

Diungkapkan bahwa girish rao, vice president of information technology at lubrizol, says the company is building a digital foundation that connects business processes, modern data platforms, and cloud infrastructure to support its research and development (r&d) teams. Their goal is to combine decades of accumulated technical data with the deep expertise of chemists and engineers who understand customer needs as well as the physical constraints of their work. Data scientists can help identify patterns, test new hypotheses, and model possibilities before researchers conduct physical experiments. But, Rao emphasizes, “it's not about replacing scientific judgment; it is about giving our scientists better tools. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, scientists, data scientists, and it teams approach problems from different perspectives, prioritizing experimental validity, model performance, and platform security and scalability, respectively. By bringing these groups together in “fusion teams,” Lubrizol aligns them around shared objectives, starting with small pilots to build trust.

Diungkapkan bahwa "once the trust is built between the team members and they know what value they're about to create," rao says, "things go a lot better. " Cloud infrastructure also gives the company flexibility to access computing resources and modern tools without making the substantial investments required to build and maintain its own data centers.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, these capabilities could prove especially valuable in advancing sustainability. Digital modeling can help researchers evaluate more formulations, explore materials such as starch and corn-based alternatives, and assess trade-offs across a product's life cycle. Promising a material in a laboratory is only the first step. Scaling production while meeting performance expectations, regulatory requirements, and financial constraints is still a tightrope walk, but AI's ability to model multiple variables could help teams navigate those competing demands.

Sebagaimana diketahui, looking to the future, rao expects ai, automation, advanced modeling, digital twins, and connected data to converge as laboratories become more intelligent and manufacturing plants more efficient. The opportunity, he suggests, lies in bringing these capabilities together responsibly and at scale. “It's not just a single technology. I think it's the combination of all of these, and it'll be the ability to connect all these processes that are going to generate tremendous amounts of data. ".
