#153. A butterfly that fooled scientists for 200 years finally reveals its secrets

📅 12 Nov 2026

A butterfly that fooled scientists for 200 years finally reveals its secrets

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261110042556.htm

Diungkapkan bahwa a butterfly commonly seen throughout central and south america has been concealing a remarkable secret. For more than two centuries, scientists believed that the genus Colobura contained just one widespread species. Now, researchers have identified a third species that looks almost identical to its relatives, raising new questions about how these butterflies evolved and continue to live alongside one another.

Diungkapkan bahwa the newly identified species, named colobura cryptica, was described in the journal zootaxa by researchers led by anisha sapkota, a doctoral student at the florida museum of natural history. By combining DNA analysis with subtle differences in wing patterns and ultraviolet light reflection, the team uncovered distinctions that had remained largely invisible to scientists.

Sebagaimana diketahui, even more surprising, the three species occupy overlapping regions and can be found in the same places at the same time. Yet genetic evidence suggests they remain separate, with no detectable signs of interbreeding.

A Familiar Butterfly With a Hidden Identity.

Diungkapkan bahwa central and south america's tropical rainforests contain some of the greatest concentrations of biodiversity on the planet. Costa Rica alone supports approximately half a million species, roughly five times the number found across Canada, even though Canada's land area is about 200 times larger.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, despite this extraordinary diversity, certain plants and animals are especially recognizable throughout the region. In Canada's boreal forests, balsam firs are a familiar feature of the landscape. In tropical America, trees belonging to the genus Cecropia play a similarly prominent role.

Diungkapkan bahwa in 1888, german botanist andreas schimper described their importance, writing, "every naturalist who has been in tropical america will remember cecropia, belonging to the most conspicuous trees of those countries. ".

The butterflies of the genus Colobura are just as recognizable, according to Sapkota.

"If you go to the neotropics, Colobura is one of the first butterflies you see," she said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, these butterflies and cecropia trees share a close ecological relationship because cecropia leaves provide food for colobura caterpillars. Both groups occur across an enormous geographic area, from portions of the Andes Mountains and the Brazilian Amazon to the Atlantic Rainforest in Brazil and Paraguay. They are also widespread throughout Central America and the Caribbean Islands.

Berdasarkan laporan, such broad distributions are not particularly unusual in tropical ecosystems. However, the diversity within these groups presents an interesting contrast.

Berdasarkan laporan, scientists recognize 61 species of cecropia, many of which occupy relatively small geographic areas. Some grow only in the Andes, while others are confined to the Caribbean.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for colobura butterflies, the situation appeared very different. After Carl Linnaeus formally described Colobura dirce in 1758, scientists spent more than 200 years treating the genus as a single species, despite its extensive range.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that understanding began to change in 2001, when researchers formally recognized a second species. Now, an unexpected discovery in Venezuela has led to the identification of a third, described by Sapkota and her colleagues in Zootaxa.

Rather than providing a simple explanation for the group's evolutionary history, the discovery has introduced an even greater puzzle.

Diungkapkan bahwa "it's crazy to think about. These butterflies look almost exactly the same and are found in the exact same place at the same time. ".

A Butterfly Mystery Dating Back More Than 150 Years.

Berdasarkan laporan, distinguishing adult colobura butterflies is exceptionally difficult. In some butterflies, this stripe becomes a little wider. In others, it stays the same width. Their wings are nearly identical, with only slight variations in a gray stripe on the underside of the front wings. It may also extend far enough to meet a yellow band running across the wing, or stop short of it.

Their caterpillars offer somewhat clearer clues.

Sebagaimana diketahui, colobura caterpillars have velvety black bodies covered with prominent yellow projections that end in sharply angled barbs. These defensive structures send a warning to potential predators that could be interpreted as "leave me alone, or there will be unpleasant consequences. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, beneath those conspicuous spines are much smaller cream-colored markings. Depending on the species, these markings may resemble teardrops or rings, or they may be missing entirely.

The importance of these differences was recognized surprisingly early.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in 1852, dutch entomologist jan sepp proposed that caterpillars with different cream-colored patterns represented two separate species. Other researchers rejected his interpretation, arguing that the variations could reflect differences between males and females or simply natural variation within a single species.

That view remained dominant for approximately 150 years.

Diungkapkan bahwa in 2001, keith willmott and several colleagues revisited sepp's observations and formally described a second species, colobura annulata. Willmott is now a curator at the Florida Museum's McGuire Center for Lepidoptera and Biodiversity.

"We assumed that was the problem solved," Willmott said.

Berdasarkan laporan, he moved on to other research, believing the longstanding classification problem had been resolved. However, occasional observations continued to suggest that something was missing.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "i had a few indications that there was a third species, but i thought it was too implausible. ".

At the time, even the existence of two nearly indistinguishable species seemed remarkable.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "it's a very distinctive butterfly. It's hard to imagine there being two species in the same area that look alike because they're so different from anything else. ".

Roughly 25 years later, fresh evidence emerged when Willmott's colleague Andrés Orellana encountered a group of hungry Colobura caterpillars feeding on a young Cecropia tree in Venezuela.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the caterpillars were rapidly stripping leaves from the sapling. They possessed the familiar black body segments near the head and yellow spines characteristic of the genus, but one feature stood out.

Unlike the two recognized species, these caterpillars had no cream-colored markings at all.

Sebagaimana diketahui, orellana photographed the unusual insects and shared the images with willmott. The discovery provided a compelling reason to investigate whether a third species had been overlooked.

Sapkota had recently joined the Shirey lab at the Florida Museum and was eager to lead the investigation.

Working with her colleagues, she designed a study that combined genetic evidence with careful examinations of butterfly anatomy.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, first, she studied dna barcodes, short and highly variable genetic sequences that help researchers distinguish species. These sequences came from a long-running survey of butterflies and moths in Costa Rica led by study co-authors Daniel Janzen and Winnie Hallwachs.

Berdasarkan laporan, the investigation then expanded to older butterfly specimens collected across tropical central and south america. Sapkota sent these museum samples to Nick Grishin at the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center, where researchers sequenced both their mitochondrial and nuclear genomes.

The genetic results provided a way to test whether the butterflies represented genuinely different evolutionary groups rather than ordinary variations within a single species.

But the researchers also wanted to know whether there were physical differences that previous scientists had failed to notice.

An Invisible Clue Hidden in Butterfly Wings.

Sapkota spent hours examining preserved butterflies in museum collections, searching for consistent traits that might distinguish the suspected species.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at first, the effort produced few answers. Other than the slight differences in the gray wing stripe, the butterflies appeared remarkably similar.

Eventually, she noticed something unusual.

The undersides of some wings appeared to have a faint violet shimmer, and the intensity of that sheen seemed to vary between specimens.

This observation suggested that the insects might reflect ultraviolet light, which falls outside the range of human vision but can be detected by many butterflies.

"I checked it with a spectrometer and found that even though the butterflies didn't look violet to me, it reflected UV light," she said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the measurements revealed a striking pattern. All three species reflected ultraviolet light, but the wavelengths differed.

The researchers named the newly identified species Colobura cryptica, reflecting its previously concealed identity.

Although the visible differences were extremely subtle, the ultraviolet measurements, caterpillar markings, and DNA results told a consistent story.

The three species could be distinguished by the following features:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there is an additional complication with colobura dirce. It includes two subspecies with different ultraviolet reflectance values. Colobura dirce dirce reflects light at 362. 2 nm, while Colobura dirce wolcotti reflects light at 390. 6 nm. The 376 nm value represents the average for the species.

Berdasarkan laporan, beyond these minor wing differences, sapkota could not identify any other consistent anatomical distinctions. Even the male genitalia, which often provide some of the most reliable features for separating butterfly and moth species, appeared indistinguishable.

Nevertheless, the genetic findings were decisive.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, dna analysis identified three distinct evolutionary lineages, and those divisions matched the physical differences the team had documented. Together, the evidence confirmed that Colobura contains three species rather than two.

Three Butterfly Species Living Side by Side.

Identifying a previously unknown butterfly species is significant on its own, but the geographic distributions of these three species make the finding particularly intriguing.

All three occur in overlapping portions of Central and South America.

Diungkapkan bahwa colobura dirce has the widest distribution, extending from mexico to southeastern brazil. It occurs on both sides of the Andes Mountains and throughout the Caribbean archipelago.

Colobura annulata also occupies a large geographic area, although it is absent from the Greater Antilles.

The newly described Colobura cryptica has the smallest known range, stretching from southern Mexico to the foothills of the Andes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, these overlapping distributions raise an important evolutionary question. How did three species become genetically distinct while continuing to occupy many of the same regions?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, species often emerge when populations become isolated from one another. A mountain range, for example, might divide a population and prevent individuals on opposite sides from mating.

Sebagaimana diketahui, over many generations, the separated groups can accumulate different genetic and physical traits. If those differences become great enough, the populations may eventually lose the ability to interbreed, even if they come into contact again.

But geographic separation is not the only mechanism that can drive the formation of new species.

Researchers suspect that the Colobura butterflies might have developed different ways of using their shared forest habitats.

Berdasarkan laporan, "there could be vertical stratification between these butterflies," sapkota said. "Colobura dirce is typically found in the undergrowth and C. annulata are usually found in the canopy, but we do not know for sure because there have been mixed signals coming from different studies. cryptica and C. ".

In other words, one species may spend more time near the forest floor while the others favor the upper branches.

This kind of habitat separation could potentially help maintain differences between species living in the same geographic area.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, previous research has produced inconsistent observations. One reason may be that even experienced butterfly specialists have difficulty telling the three species apart.

How Do Nearly Identical Butterflies Recognize Each Other?.

An even more puzzling question concerns how the butterflies identify suitable mates.

Many moths and some butterflies use special scent glands to release pheromones, chemical signals that help individuals recognize members of their own species.

Berdasarkan laporan, that suggests visual information may play an important role in mate selection. Yet their nearly identical appearance makes it difficult to understand how they distinguish one species from another.

The newly discovered ultraviolet differences offer a possible explanation.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, although humans cannot see ultraviolet light, many butterflies can. Sapkota suspects that the different ultraviolet reflections from their wings might provide visual signals that help them identify members of their own species.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, similar mechanisms are known or suspected in other butterflies and moths. Garden whites, sulfur butterflies, and wood tiger moths possess ultraviolet-reflecting wing scales that researchers believe may contribute to mate selection.

Sapkota is investigating whether Colobura butterflies use comparable signals, but the results have not yet provided a clear answer.

Whatever mechanism they use, the butterflies appear remarkably successful at maintaining their separate identities.

Analysis of nuclear DNA found no evidence of hybridization among the three species, despite their overlapping ranges.

The findings suggest that the species have followed separate evolutionary paths without detectable genetic mixing.

A Familiar Butterfly Still Holds Many Secrets.

The discovery of Colobura cryptica demonstrates how much remains unknown about even widespread, conspicuous animals.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for generations, naturalists studied these butterflies without recognizing the full diversity hidden within the group. Only by combining detailed observations with modern genetic testing and ultraviolet measurements were researchers able to uncover the third species.

Yet some of the most important questions remain unanswered, including how the butterflies choose mates, whether they occupy different parts of the forest, and what originally caused their evolutionary separation.

For Sapkota, answering those questions will require observing the insects in their natural habitats.

Berdasarkan laporan, "someone has to go the field to find it out themselves. ".

Those interested in another unusual aspect of Colobura biology can explore the Biodiversity Heritage Library, which contains a whimsical account published in 1952 describing the poop perches that young Colobura caterpillars construct during their earliest developmental stages.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, goodyear tire & rubber co. announced Monday that CEO Mark Stewart would be stepping down from his role effective immediately.

Board member Roger Wood is taking over as interim CEO and president, Goodyear said.

The leadership change comes as the tire company is in the midst of a multiyear transformation plan.

Stewart was hired in January 2024 to lead the company, with the goal of revitalizing the legacy American business to make it more efficient and profitable.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the company has faced disappointing results thus far, reporting last week third-quarter results that saw net sales down 2. 3% year over year and an adjusted net loss of $31 million. Goodyear failed to reach a 10% operating margin by the end of last year, which was a major goal of the turnaround plan.

Sebagaimana diketahui, goodyear said it formed a special committee of the board earlier this year to conduct a "strategic review of the company's businesses and operations focused on identifying opportunities to strengthen performance and drive shareholder value. ".

It said Monday it will continue that work by evaluating strategic and operational initiatives that include further optimizing the company's business mix and footprint, improving efficiency and investing in new products and capabilities that support long-term growth.

"Goodyear has made meaningful progress in becoming a more efficient and focused company, and the board believes this is the right moment to transition leadership to accelerate that progress and capture additional opportunity," Goodyear Chair Joe Hinrichs said in a press release.

The company has faced headwinds from tariffs, higher raw material costs and increased competition from China.

Wood has been a member of the company's board of directors since July 2023 and was previously the co-CEO of Tenneco as well as CEO of Dana Holding Corporation.

The company will start a search for a permanent replacement as part of its strategic review.

Shares of Goodyear were down roughly 4% in early trading Monday.

#157. AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again

📅 12 Nov 2026

AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261110042553.htm

Diungkapkan bahwa artificial intelligence could help overcome one of the biggest challenges in restoring vision to people who are blind: getting a brain implant to produce reliable visual experiences. Researchers from three institutions, including UC Santa Barbara, have demonstrated that AI can improve how precisely an experimental visual prosthesis stimulates the brain and predicts what a person perceives.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the team used a deep learning system to develop electrical stimulation patterns for electrodes temporarily implanted in the visual cortex, the region at the back of the brain responsible for processing visual information. By analyzing the brain's responses, the technology gave researchers greater control over neural activity and helped them better anticipate the visual sensations produced by the implant.

Diungkapkan bahwa published online in the journal neuron, the proof-of-concept study represents progress toward more advanced visual prostheses, sometimes described as bionic eyes. These devices could eventually become more effective by learning how each person's brain responds to stimulation rather than relying on predetermined settings.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "building a model in the abstract is one thing," said michael beyeler, an associate professor of computer science and psychological and brain sciences at uc santa barbara. "Seeing it shape an experiment with a person is something else entirely. That ability to go from theory to something that may one day help people is what drives much of the work in our lab. ".

How Bionic Vision Could Bypass Damaged Eyes.

Berdasarkan laporan, for decades, scientists have worked to develop technologies capable of restoring some vision to people who are blind, although the results have generally been limited. Some experimental devices stimulate the retina, the layer of tissue at the back of the eye that detects light. Others attempt to activate parts of the visual system farther along the pathway that carries visual information to the brain.

Diungkapkan bahwa visual cortical prostheses work differently. This approach could offer a potential solution for people whose visual pathways have been damaged but whose visual cortex can still respond to stimulation. Instead of depending on the eyes or optic nerves, they deliver electrical signals directly to the visual cortex. Possible candidates include individuals who lost their sight because of strokes, neurodegenerative diseases, or traumatic brain injuries.

The ability to regain even limited vision could be especially meaningful for people who remember what it was like to see.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, beyeler highlighted those "who have been able to see for part of their life, but then, because of an inherited eye disease or an accident, have lost their vision," adding, "for those people, the desire may be very strong to get some vision back. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa the new findings build on earlier computational research supported by beyeler's 2022 national institutes of health (nih) director's new innovator award. The five-year, $2 million grant has supported his efforts to make artificial vision systems more accurate, predictable, and effective.

Scientists Test AI With a Brain Implant in a Blind Man.

Berdasarkan laporan, an important opportunity to test the technology came in 2024, when researchers from beyeler's bionic vision lab traveled to spain. Their goal was to determine whether their computer models could improve the performance of a brain implant already being used in an experimental study.

Diungkapkan bahwa at hospital imed elche, the team worked with a 27-year-old man who had become blind following a traumatic brain injury. He had received an implant containing 96 electrodes arranged in an array within his visual cortex. The device was intended to remain in place for six months before being removed.

Diungkapkan bahwa when researchers activated the electrodes using electrical current, the participant experienced visual sensations known as phosphenes. These can appear as spots, flashes, or shapes of light, sometimes resembling stars or fireworks.

Berdasarkan laporan, producing these sensations is possible, but making them consistent and predictable is much more difficult. The same electrical stimulation does not always trigger an identical response, and activating particular electrodes does not guarantee that the person will perceive a specific visual pattern.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to address this problem, the researchers trained a deep neural network, a type of ai designed to recognize complex patterns, to predict how the visual cortex would respond to different electrical stimulation settings. The model also considered the brain's resting activity immediately before stimulation, giving it information about the participant's current neural state.

Using these predictions, the researchers identified combinations of electrical signals that were most likely to produce particular patterns of brain activity.

Berdasarkan laporan, when the scientists tested the stimulation patterns selected by ai, the results were encouraging. The new approach generated the intended patterns of neural activity more accurately than the comparison methods while requiring less electrical current.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, another important discovery emerged when the team examined the relationship between brain activity and the participant's visual experiences. The patterns recorded directly from his brain were better predictors of what he perceived than the stimulation settings themselves.

Berdasarkan laporan, this distinction matters because activating the brain is not the same as knowing what a person will see. Even when researchers can produce a desired neural response, they still need to understand how the brain transforms that activity into a conscious visual experience.

Diungkapkan bahwa "engineers naturally want to treat phosphenes like pixels: stimulate more electrodes, and you should get a more complete image," beyeler said. The challenge is to learn more about that transformation. "But the brain does not work that way. Electrodes interact, neural responses fluctuate, and what we put into the brain is not necessarily what the person perceives. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the findings suggest that future visual prostheses may need to do more than simply deliver electrical signals. They may also need to monitor how the brain reacts and use that feedback to continually improve stimulation.

Teaching Brain Implants to Adapt to Each Person.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a key advantage of the implant used in the experiment was its ability to perform two tasks. It could stimulate the visual cortex with electrical current while simultaneously recording the resulting neural activity.

This allowed researchers to train their AI model using the brain's actual responses rather than relying exclusively on information about which electrodes were activated and how much current they delivered.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the participant also provided feedback about what he experienced. He reported whether he saw a phosphene and, during certain experiments, described its appearance, including its shape, size, brightness, and color.

Comparing these reports with the recorded brain activity revealed that neural responses contained more useful information about the perceived visual sensations than the electrical stimulation parameters alone.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the ai system also used measurements of resting brain activity to account for changes in the participant's neural state before each stimulation. This could be particularly valuable because the brain's response to electrical signals can vary over time, including from one day to the next.

By adapting stimulation to these changing conditions, future prostheses might provide more consistent visual experiences without requiring users to adjust to a rigid set of signals.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "a useful visual prosthesis cannot rely on a fixed recipe," beyeler said. "It has to learn how an individual brain responds and adapt the stimulation accordingly. Ultimately, the device should adapt to the person, not the other way around. ".

A Collaborative Step Toward Restoring Sight.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the research brought together scientists from uc santa barbara, eth zurich, and miguel hernández university (mhu). Beyeler described the effort as "a true collaboration. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, the project was led by co-first authors pehuén moure of eth zurich, jacob granley of uc santa barbara, and fabrizio grani of mhu. The supervising researchers were Beyeler, Shih-Chii Liu of ETH Zurich, and Eduardo Fernández of MHU. Their work forms part of a larger feasibility trial taking place in Spain.

Although the technology remains experimental and the participant's visual experiences were limited to flashes and shapes of light, the results demonstrate how AI could improve communication between artificial vision devices and the brain.

Sebagaimana diketahui, rather than treating every brain as if it responds the same way, future bionic vision systems could learn from each individual and adjust their signals accordingly. That personalized approach may prove essential to developing implants that can eventually restore useful vision to people who have lost their sight.

#159. Google pushes privacy angle as Gemini-powered smartglasses debut starting at $395

📅 12 Nov 2026

Google pushes privacy angle as Gemini-powered smartglasses debut starting at $395

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://arstechnica.com/google/2026/11/google-pushes-privacy-angle-as-gemini-powered-smartglasses-debut-starting-at-395/

The first Gemini smartglasses are a collab between Google, Samsung, Gentle Monster, and Warby Parker.

Berdasarkan laporan, smartglasses have always faced an uphill road to acceptance. Not only is propping a computer up on your nose an uncomfortable proposition, but the privacy aspect has been vexing people since the Google Glass days. Now, Google is ready to take another swing at “intelligent eyewear” for the Gemini era after previewing its plans a couple of times. The first glasses are up for preorder today from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, but they’re no impulse buy.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, these devices are a collaboration between google, samsung, and the aforementioned eyewear designers. Gentle Monster and Warby Parker have each designed a few different frames, with options for transparent and tinted lenses. Samsung is providing the computing hardware that fits inside them, and Google has the software covered.

Diungkapkan bahwa warby parker has designed three frames for google eyewear, called alden, reid, and wren (see above). They are available with both standard optical and sun lenses in Pine, Saddle, and Jet Black colors at $395 and higher. Warby Parker is only selling devices in the US. They come in dark red, pink, gray, and yellow colors and are available with clear, tinted, blue, or brown lenses. Gentle Monster has gone a bit further with six styles, but Google hasn’t told us any names for those yet. The Gentle Monster styles start a little higher at $449, and they will be available in the US and South Korea.

Berdasarkan laporan, google says the frames all weigh about 41 grams, which is not terrible but is definitely near the top for glasses generally. That will also determine the final pricing. They will, naturally, weigh much more when you account for lenses. So far, we only have the starting prices for these devices, including non-prescription lenses.

Berdasarkan laporan, the setup here is similar to the ray-ban meta glasses we’ve seen for a few years. There are no screens in the lenses, but you can interact with the AI system via voice or by activating the integrated camera. The experience should be similar to using Gemini Live on your phone, but it will be a lot easier to fire up the AI. You can say “Hey Gemini” or tap a touch-sensitive area of the frame to start interacting with the robot.

Credit: Gentle Monster Credit: Gentle Monster.

Sebagaimana diketahui, since this is the same chatbot that operates across the google ecosystem, it has access to your data and preferences. The glasses use custom open-ear speakers to limit distractions for those around you. You can ask questions and get personalized answers, have Google Maps guide you by voice, or just talk with the AI to kill time. Google notes the directional microphones should not pick up speech from other people, either.

Sebagaimana diketahui, adding the camera feed is where things get interesting. Google suggests asking Gemini for recommendations when looking at a bookshelf or glancing at an event poster to have the AI add it to your calendar. When the AI can see what you see, it has the potential to do more work on your behalf. The glasses will also support Gemini Guided Vision, which provides conversational audio descriptions for people who are visually impaired.

Berdasarkan laporan, the utility of these devices hinges on gemini. In fact, it can be frustratingly fallible at times. I would be remiss not to point out that Gemini, like all AI systems, is not infallible. The chatbot still regularly screws up simple things like adding calendar appointments or identifying objects in an image in my testing, and when you don’t have a screen to verify the AI’s output, it may be harder to trust it. These devices will really only make sense if you can rely on Gemini to do things right, and that’s still not a guarantee.

Diungkapkan bahwa all the gemini-powered glasses from gentle monster and warby parker feature a 12 mp wide-angle camera capable of shooting photos and video. Google says it has implemented a number of features and limitations to ensure people don’t do creepy things with its intelligent eyewear, and that it doesn’t do creepy things to you—Google claims its approach respects privacy on “both sides of the lens. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa for starters, there’s a recording light that is on whenever the camera is active. Like the Meta glasses, Google’s eyewear will detect if the light has been covered up or modified in any way that would prevent it from illuminating. In that event, the glasses will refuse to activate the camera. All Google-powered glasses will have a physical off switch, too.

Credit: Warby Parker Credit: Warby Parker.

Berdasarkan laporan, on the user privacy side, google says it will not save any images or videos captured by the glasses in your gemini history. Your voice interactions with Gemini via the glasses are, as with all other Gemini endpoints, not guaranteed the same level of protection. Additionally, none of that data will be used for training AI models or targeting ads. You can delete your chats from the Gemini history, though.

Berdasarkan laporan, data on the glasses is encrypted, and it remains that way during transit to the cloud. However, it’s not encrypted on Google’s servers. The company does note that it’s working to bring Private AI Compute to glasses, which will isolate data during processing so not even Google can access it.

Credit: Gentle Monster Credit: Gentle Monster.

Sebagaimana diketahui, anyone looking to get gemini on their face and test google’s privacy promise can preorder the glasses from the gentle monster and warby parker websites. On the Android side, you’ll need a Pixel 7 or newer or a Samsung Galaxy S or Z series device running One UI 9 or later. Devices should ship and appear on store shelves on December 10. They will work with all iPhones from the 13 Pro onward. Importantly, support for these devices is a bit narrow at launch. If you’ve got a cheaper Samsung Galaxy or a device from another OEM, you’re out of luck at the moment.

After all, you don’t need to know everything, only what’s important.

#164. Earth's fiery birth may have created hundreds of oceans' worth of water

📅 12 Nov 2026

Earth's fiery birth may have created hundreds of oceans' worth of water

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261110042549.htm

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, earth may have created a substantial amount of its own water as the planet was forming, rather than relying entirely on comets, meteorites, or other objects to deliver it from space. New research published in Nature Geoscience suggests that chemical reactions between rocky pebbles and the hydrogen-rich atmosphere of the young Earth could have produced enormous quantities of water.

Berdasarkan laporan, the discovery offers a new explanation for how our planet acquired one of the most important ingredients for life. It also raises the possibility that other rocky planets throughout the universe could generate water through similar processes, potentially making habitable worlds more common than previously thought.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, researchers at the university of new mexico investigated this possibility by recreating some of the extreme conditions that existed during earth's formation. The study was led by graduate student Susmita Garai, along with Zachary Sharp, professor and director of Earth and Planetary Sciences, and Peter Olson. Their experiments examined what happens when rocks containing iron react with hydrogen at extremely high temperatures.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "previous ideas about the source of water to earth rely on an external source, such as comets or meteorites. Dr. Garai's efforts paid off mightily, as she found that water is produced in just minutes in the high temperature environment of the Early Earth's atmosphere. Here we show that virtually any Earth-sized planet should have water by this newly identified mechanism," explained Sharp. "In order to evaluate the possibility of 'pebble' rain' being a source of water, we needed to construct and execute some very challenging high-temperature experiments. ".

A New Explanation for the Origin of Earth's Water.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for decades, scientists have debated where earth's water originally came from. One prominent theory suggests that much of it was transported to the developing planet by icy material originating in the colder, more distant regions of the early solar system.

Sebagaimana diketahui, according to this explanation, water-rich objects, including small icy pebbles, traveled inward and eventually contributed to earth's water supply. However, researchers have struggled to fully explain how enough of this material could have reached our planet from such great distances. There are also unresolved questions about whether this delivery process accounts for Earth's chemical composition.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the new study investigates a different route by which water could have appeared. Instead of arriving already contained in ice or other materials, water may have been produced directly through reactions involving the rocky ingredients that built Earth and the gases surrounding it.

Diungkapkan bahwa during the planet's earliest stages, countless small pieces of rock gradually came together to form a larger body. Scientists refer to this growth process as pebble accretion. As Earth gained mass, it could have accumulated a dense atmosphere containing large amounts of hydrogen, with temperatures and pressures far higher than those found on the planet today.

Sebagaimana diketahui, under those conditions, rocky pebbles falling through the atmosphere could have triggered a remarkable chemical reaction. Hydrogen in the surrounding gas would react with iron oxide inside the silicate rocks, transforming the iron oxide into metallic iron while releasing water vapor.

Experiments Reveal Water Can Form in Minutes.

Berdasarkan laporan, to determine whether this process could actually occur, the researchers exposed samples of silicate rock to temperatures ranging from 1,200 to 1,400 degrees celsius. They conducted experiments using flowing hydrogen gas and repeated the tests with helium to provide a comparison. Each experiment ran for between 15 minutes and three hours.

Diungkapkan bahwa the results provided strong evidence that the proposed reaction works under these extreme conditions. When the rocks were heated in hydrogen, almost 80% of their iron oxide was transformed into metallic iron, with water vapor produced during the reaction.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in contrast, the researchers did not observe the same reaction when helium was used instead of hydrogen. This difference confirmed that hydrogen played a crucial role in generating the water.

Diungkapkan bahwa the speed and scale of the reaction were especially striking. Although the scientists had expected some water to form, the results suggested that the process could have been far more productive than anticipated. When they extended their experimental findings to conditions on the early Earth, their calculations indicated that the mechanism might have generated hundreds of oceans' worth of water.

Diungkapkan bahwa "we had suspected and hoped that we would produce iron metal and water in our reduction experiments, but we really had no way of knowing how fast and how much. We were quite surprised to find that extrapolation of our work suggests that hundreds of oceans' worth of water were likely produced in this way. Looking out over a large body of water, it is hard to imagine that that water may have been produced 4 ½ billion years ago in a hell-like atmosphere, but it very well may have," said Sharp.

Earth's Fiery Beginnings May Have Helped Create Its Oceans.

Diungkapkan bahwa these findings suggest that the conditions of earth's formation may have actively contributed to its water supply. Rather than being entirely dependent on water delivered from elsewhere in the solar system, the growing planet may have possessed the ingredients needed to manufacture water through its own chemical reactions.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the implications extend well beyond earth. If rocky planets around other stars develop similarly hot, hydrogen-rich atmospheres during their formation, they might also produce substantial amounts of water as rocky material accumulates.

Berdasarkan laporan, this possibility could have important consequences for understanding how common water is across the universe. A process that naturally occurs during the formation of Earth-sized planets would mean that obtaining water might not require the right icy objects to arrive from distant regions of a planetary system.

Could Other Earth-Like Planets Make Their Own Water?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the research also adds to growing interest in pebble accretion as an explanation for how planets form. Although the concept has gained attention relatively recently, it has already helped scientists address several longstanding questions about planetary development.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the idea of pebble accretion is still relatively new. "And now we see that it also can explain why our planet is habitable. But it seems to solve many problems that exist with the existing paradigm for planet formation," Sharp said. It's only been around for the last decade. By extension, it is reasonable to expect that other Earth-sized bodies circling other stars would also have water and possibly life. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, there are still important uncertainties to resolve. While the experiments show that rocky material can generate water when exposed to hydrogen under conditions resembling those of the early Earth, they do not establish how much of our planet's present water supply was actually produced this way. Additional research will be needed to determine the contribution of this mechanism compared with water delivered by comets, meteorites, and other sources.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, nevertheless, the findings reveal a potentially important process that may have shaped earth billions of years ago. They also suggest that the ability to produce water could be built into the formation of rocky planets themselves, opening new possibilities for understanding where water, and perhaps life, might exist beyond our solar system.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, juicier chicken tenders. Revamped sauces. Richer and creamier Frosties.

Across the restaurant industry, chains are turning their focus back to their food in the hopes that better quality will win back diners.

Berdasarkan laporan, over the last two years, consumers have dined out less frequently and grown pickier about where they choose to eat, based on data from black box intelligence. In that time, "value" has been the buzzword du jour for restaurant executives, who have explained to analysts and investors that the word encompasses more than menu pricing alone.

Berdasarkan laporan, now, industry ceos are turning to their corporate chefs to try to beat rivals on quality and taste, as they look to expand their definition of value. Discounts and one-off promotions can lift traffic for a time, but the actual product still matters for restaurants' long-term growth, as well as franchisee profitability.

From Wendy's to Chipotle Mexican Grill, chief executives touted new or upcoming improvements to menu items on their quarterly earnings conference calls in recent weeks.

"We think the product's improved and even better," Chipotle CEO Scott Boatwright told analysts on the company's call in late October, referring to the burrito chain's brisket, which returned to menus for a limited time Thursday.

For some chains, better food is a key step in ambitious turnaround plans.

For example, "quality food at real value" is one pillar of Wendy's five-part turnaround strategy that the chain unveiled on Thursday.

"We're also rebuilding our food offerings and have begun testing improvements to quality and craveability of our core items, including thicker, crispier bacon, a richer and creamier Frosty, whole leaf lettuce on sandwiches and improved salads," Wendy's CEO Bob Wright told analysts on the call Thursday.

Diungkapkan bahwa that same day, the company reported its seventh straight quarter of same-store sales declines and publicly rejected a $1. 4 billion takeover bid led by Nelson Peltz's Trian Partners. Wendy's said the proposal did not take into account the potential value that its turnaround plan could unlock.

There is precedent to suggest that better-tasting food can contribute to higher sales.

Diungkapkan bahwa in 2009, domino's pizza changed its recipe, swapping out its sauce, adding garlic to its crust and switching to shredded mozzarella with a hint of provolone. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, now, some of the same team that led the domino's turnaround is copying the playbook at burger king's u. S. restaurants.

Sebagaimana diketahui, part of the burger chain's multiyear comeback plan has focused on revamping its core menu items. #170. NASA’s Hubble Offers Cosmic Sampler of Targets for Roman

📅 12 Nov 2026

NASA’s Hubble Offers Cosmic Sampler of Targets for Roman

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://science.nasa.gov/missions/hubble/nasas-hubble-offers-cosmic-sampler-of-targets-for-roman/

A gallery of gravitational lenses captured by NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope showcases the diversity of this cosmic phenomenon and lays the groundwork for follow-up observations by the new Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.

Berdasarkan laporan, gravitational lensing, first predicted by albert einstein, occurs when the gravity of a massive foreground object, such as a galaxy or cluster of galaxies, bends, warps, and magnifies the light from a more distant background object. The effect is similar to that of a giant lens in space that allows astronomers to view objects much farther away than any telescope could see on its own.

The lenses in this image formed from the precise alignment of a distant background galaxy with the mass of a foreground galaxy, creating distorted and magnified images of the background galaxy that appear as arcs around the foreground galaxy.

Berdasarkan laporan, astronomers will use these observations of a large and varied population of gravitational lenses to construct lens models that will help determine how much mass is in the lensing system’s foreground galaxy – and potentially prove or dispel a theory about dark matter. Astronomers study the amount of distortion of the lensed background galaxies to determine the quantity and distribution of mass in the foreground galaxy, including its invisible dark matter.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, hubble views the cosmos primarily in visible and ultraviolet light with some infrared coverage, providing a comprehensive, high-resolution view of individual objects. While Hubble gets a better view of individual lenses, Roman will be able to capture more lenses with its wider field-of-view. Roman sees primarily infrared light and some visible, over a much larger field of view to create panoramas of the universe. If Roman finds a particularly interesting lens, researchers may use Hubble to take follow-up observations using its visible and UV prowess for individual objects.

Berdasarkan laporan, with hubble's high-resolution imaging and precise models, researchers should also be able to detect small imperfections in these gravitationally lensed galaxy arcs that would indicate the presence of small clumps of dark matter. Researchers could use these previously undetected clumps to confirm the cold dark matter theory, which predicts the existence of many small dark matter clumps of between a million to a billion solar masses. In contrast, the dark matter halo of our Milky Way galaxy is around 1. 3 trillion solar masses.

Diungkapkan bahwa by studying hubble lens images in detail, researchers intend to build a super-intelligence tool to efficiently search similar arcs in the upcoming roman images. The Hubble images are expected to both yield their own results on dark matter and pave the way for analysis of Roman’s larger sample of lenses.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the unique lenses in this image display some of the different characteristics researchers will see as they collect a diverse and numerous assortment of lenses to test in their models. Panel A is an example of an arc-counterarc configuration, in which the lensed background galaxy appears as a duplicated pair of arcs. The lensed galaxy is being magnified by a pair of foreground galaxies whose combined mass bends the light of the background galaxy around them.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, panel f is an einstein ring, in which the alignment of the background galaxy and approximately spherical mass of the foreground lens are so perfectly situated that the lensed galaxy almost fully encircles the foreground galaxy. Panel I shows a quadruply lensed galaxy, in which the background galaxy is replicated four times, appearing as smeared dots around the foreground galaxy. Panel C also shows a quadruply lensed galaxy, with double knots that are most likely strong star-forming regions in the background galaxy.

Berdasarkan laporan, some of the magnified and warped background galaxies appear blue and some appear red. These bluish arcs indicate young stars, while reddish arcs indicate older stars. Roman and Hubble will explore these differences to better understand how galaxies evolved earlier in the universe.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, most of the foreground lensing galaxies are elliptical galaxies, which are older, denser, and more compact. Lensed images of background galaxies only occur when the mass density of the foreground galaxy reaches a critical point.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but not all of these foreground galaxies are ellipticals, and researchers can use these differences to explore the evolutionary paths taken by these galaxies. In panel G, the foreground galaxy appears elongated, which may be true or a trick of perspective, and in panels B and F, the foreground galaxies appear to have spiral arms.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, panel d’s foreground galaxy has a visible dust lane, which is rare in a lensing galaxy and the kind of detail that hubble’s sharp, visible-light vision excels at revealing. The lensed background galaxy could be an Einstein Ring, with the dust lane “breaking” our view of the ring. Because infrared light is less obscured by dust, future Roman infrared observations could help determine whether the arcs form a more complete Einstein ring.

Berdasarkan laporan, these strong lenses were first detected with the dark energy spectroscopic instrument at kitt peak. Images like these are an example of the kinds of collaborative efforts that routinely take place between NASA’s Great Observatories to build a comprehensive picture of the cosmos. Hubble subsequently observed them, and Roman will take further observations. As Roman joins the family of large space observatories that includes Hubble, the Chandra X-ray Observatory, and the James Webb Space Telescope, a new window opens onto the universe, revealing sights previously hidden while expanding our cosmic knowledge for all of humanity.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, claire andreolinasa's goddard space flight center, greenbelt, mdclaire. andreoli@nasa. gov.

Since its 1990 launch, the Hubble Space Telescope has changed our fundamental understanding of the universe.

NASA's Hubble and Roman space telescopes will work together to broaden our perspective of the universe.

Hubble and Webb observations complement each other, providing us with a broad view of the universe.

#173. NASA reveals Earth's ozone hole has grown to a size not seen in a decade

📅 11 Nov 2026

NASA reveals Earth's ozone hole has grown to a size not seen in a decade

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261110042546.htm

Sebagaimana diketahui, unusual weather patterns over antarctica caused the ozone hole to expand dramatically in 2026, reaching one of its largest sizes on record. Despite the striking increase, scientists from NASA and NOAA say Earth's protective ozone layer is continuing its gradual recovery and remains on track to heal later this century.

Diungkapkan bahwa the 2026 antarctic ozone hole ranked as the seventh-largest in 48 years of observations, based on its average seasonal area. Scientists attributed the expansion primarily to an exceptionally strong polar vortex, a large circulation of winds that influences atmospheric conditions over Antarctica. They also emphasized that international efforts to reduce harmful chemicals have prevented the hole from becoming even larger.

Berdasarkan laporan, between september 7 and october 13, 2026, when ozone depletion was at its seasonal peak, the hole covered an average of approximately 9. 6 million square miles (25 million square kilometers). Scientists closely monitor ozone in the stratosphere because it serves as Earth's natural "sunscreen," protecting living organisms from dangerous solar radiation. That is more than twice the size of the United States. Unlike this beneficial layer high in the atmosphere, ozone near Earth's surface is a pollutant frequently associated with human activities.

Antarctica's Ozone Hole Reaches Its Largest Size in a Decade.

Berdasarkan laporan, the ozone hole reached its maximum extent on september 18, spreading across 10. 5 million square miles (27. 1 million square kilometers). This was approximately 90% of the size of the largest ozone hole ever measured, which occurred on September 9, 2000.

Berdasarkan laporan, "the annual ozone hole has been forming later in the season in recent years, which tells us the ozone layer is healing," said paul newman, a senior scientist at the university of maryland and longtime leader of nasa's ozone research team at the agency's goddard space flight center. "But an unusually powerful polar vortex has extended ozone depletion in the Antarctic this season, allowing the hole to grow to proportions we haven't seen in a decade. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, although the hole expanded to an extraordinary size, the results also demonstrate the benefits of decades of international environmental protections. Without reductions in chemicals known to destroy ozone, the affected area could have been substantially greater.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the 2026 ozone hole is large but could have been 1 to 2 million square miles (3. 5 million square kilometers) larger if ozone-depleting substances were as prevalent in the atmosphere today as they were at their year 2000 peak," Newman said.

How a Powerful Polar Vortex Accelerates Ozone Loss.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ozone depletion begins with chemicals released through human activities, particularly compounds containing chlorine and bromine. Atmospheric circulation transports these substances into the stratosphere, where ultraviolet radiation breaks them apart. The released chlorine and bromine atoms then participate in chemical reactions involving particles in Antarctic stratospheric clouds, leading to the destruction of ozone.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a major factor in this process is the stratospheric polar vortex, a seasonal band of strong winds that circles antarctica. This circulation traps extremely cold air over the region, allowing the formation of the special clouds that help trigger ozone destruction. When the vortex becomes unusually strong or expansive, conditions favorable for ozone loss can persist across a larger area.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in 2026, atmospheric disturbances that would normally weaken the vortex were unusually subdued. This allowed the circulation to remain powerful and helped create a broader region where ozone could be destroyed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the polar vortex was unusually large this year in part because planetary-scale weather systems that typically well up from the lower atmosphere and break up the vortex were especially weak in august and september," said amy butler, a research scientist at the noaa chemical sciences laboratory. "That weak wave action kept the strongest polar vortex winds further from the South Pole by several degrees of latitude, creating a larger area for conditions ideal for ozone depletion to occur. ".

NASA and NOAA Measure the 2026 Ozone Hole.

Despite its exceptional geographic size, the 2026 ozone hole did not experience the same extreme levels of ozone loss observed during record-breaking events 10 or 20 years earlier.

Sebagaimana diketahui, to measure ozone concentrations, noaa researchers launched instruments attached to weather balloons from the south pole baseline atmospheric observatory. They also collected readings using the Dobson Ozone Spectrophotometer, an optical device designed to measure atmospheric ozone. Their observations showed that ozone levels directly above the South Pole fell to their lowest reading of 2026 on October 17, reaching 105 Dobson units.

Berdasarkan laporan, the dobson unit is the standard measurement used to describe the total amount of ozone above a particular location. To illustrate the scale, 100 Dobson units would produce a layer of ozone just 1 millimeter thick, approximately the thickness of a dime, if all the ozone in the atmospheric column were compressed to standard temperature and pressure at sea level. The lowest ozone concentration ever measured over the South Pole was 92 Dobson units in October 2006.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, satellites provide another essential source of information. Since 1979, spaceborne instruments have helped scientists observe changes in the ozone layer and track its condition over time. The 2026 measurements included data from NASA's Aura satellite, NOAA-20, NOAA-21, and the Suomi National Polar-orbiting Partnership satellite, a joint NASA and NOAA mission.

Why Earth's Ozone Layer Is Still Recovering.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, scientists say the latest observations reinforce evidence that international restrictions on ozone-destroying chemicals are working. Much of that progress can be traced to the Montreal Protocol, a global agreement adopted in 1987 to phase out substances responsible for damaging the ozone layer.

Berdasarkan laporan, under the agreement, countries committed to replacing harmful compounds such as chlorofluorocarbons with alternatives that pose less danger to atmospheric ozone. According to Stephen Montzka, a senior scientist at NOAA's Global Monitoring Laboratory, chlorine concentrations in the Antarctic stratosphere associated with ozone-depleting chemicals have declined by approximately one-third compared with their peak levels in the 1980s.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, these reductions are significant because chlorofluorocarbons and other ozone-depleting compounds were once common in refrigerators, air conditioning systems, building insulation, and other everyday products. Although many of these substances have been phased out, they can remain in the atmosphere for decades. Additional emissions can also occur when older equipment, materials, and landfill waste release chemicals that were manufactured years ago.

Berdasarkan laporan, because these compounds break down so slowly, repairing the ozone layer takes many decades. Nevertheless, continued monitoring by NASA and NOAA indicates that the long-term recovery is progressing. Even with unusually large seasonal ozone holes such as the one observed in 2026, scientists expect the Antarctic ozone hole to recover by the 2070s.

Diungkapkan bahwa the latest findings illustrate how exceptional atmospheric conditions can temporarily produce severe ozone depletion without reversing decades of environmental progress. They also highlight the lasting impact of international cooperation in protecting Earth's atmosphere.

After disrupting the soda category with Poppi, founders Allison and Stephen Ellsworth are now taking aim at hydration with their new brand, Jetty.

Starting Monday, Jetty drinks and ready-to-mix electrolyte packets will be on shelves at Whole Foods grocery stores and available online at Target and Amazon.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the new, self-funded venture directly pits the ellsworths against pepsico, which bought poppi for $1. S. Pepsi owns Gatorade, which dominates the U. 95 billion in 2025. sports drink category with about 60% market share, according to Numerator data.

Berdasarkan laporan, poppi shook up the soda category with prebiotic fiber, low calorie and sugar counts and its fun marketing aimed at generation z and millennials. Jetty looks to upend the hydration category through a similar strategy. To do so, it will face off not only against Gatorade but also a swarm of other upstarts looking to get in on the electrolyte-fueled trend.

Diungkapkan bahwa for decades, gatorade and other sports drinks have pitched their products to athletes who need electrolytes and fluids after an intense workout, although many consumers drink them every day without even sweating. Jetty is aimed at people who need a hydration boost, but not the same level of electrolytes or sugar as a traditional sports drink.

Berdasarkan laporan, "no one has really created a product for just everyday hydration — literally everyday hydration for normal people," allison ellsworth, jetty's chief brand officer, told cnbc. "Like I woke up this morning, I didn't run a marathon. ".

Following Poppi's sale to PepsiCo, Ellsworth stayed on as an advisor to the brand, although she said she is no longer involved in the day-to-day operations.

Diungkapkan bahwa after 10 years building poppi, ellsworth said, she finally had free time. As Ellsworth tells it, she went to the doctor for the first time in a decade. She started using a GLP-1 medication and lost 60 pounds.

Ellsworth's husband, Stephen, now CEO of the new brand, noticed she wasn't hydrating, even when she came back from the gym.

Diungkapkan bahwa glp-1 medications such as ozempic and mounjaro can make people less thirsty. But because staying hydrated can also help mitigate some of the drugs' side effects, such as nausea and headaches, it can become more important.

"I physically struggle getting liquid into my body," Ellsworth said.

Diungkapkan bahwa plain old water is often less appealing to consumers, even dehydrated glp-1 users, but more flavorful options with added benefits can be tempting. About 44% of GLP-1 users report consuming more functional beverages, according to EY-Parthenon's third annual survey of more than 3,600 current or former GLP-1 users.

Ellsworth sees a broader appeal for Jetty, too.

Diungkapkan bahwa "our core audience is going to be millennial moms and gen z," she said. "Gen Z just isn't relating to these old school brands, the legacy of the Gatorades and the Powerades. They're just not cool. ".

Consumers broadly have become more interested in staying hydrated.

Sebagaimana diketahui, dollar sales of hydration and electrolyte products climbed 20% to $2. 6 billion over the 52 weeks ended Oct. 4, based on data from SPINS, which tracks new universal product codes, or UPCs. The category also has a strong repeat buyer rate of 62%.

Berdasarkan laporan, however, the ellsworths aren't the only ones to notice the potential in hydration. Big food and beverage companies have been looking to hydration, too.

Berdasarkan laporan, kraft heinz debuted capri sun juice pouches and kool-aid packets with electrolytes this spring. In April, Pepsi unveiled an overhaul of the Gatorade brand, focused on making it more appealing to a wider swath of consumers, with more potential occasions like a "fresh morning start" or an "afternoon walk. " And Electrolit is a top performer for its distributor Keurig Dr Pepper, with 40% retail sales growth in the company's third quarter.

All of that means more competition for shelf space and consumers' "share of throat," an industry term for beverage market share.

To increase Jetty's visibility across the grocery store and to maximize convenience for shoppers, Jetty will be available in both powders and bottles.

Berdasarkan laporan, single-use electrolyte mixes are growing at a much faster clip than the ready-to-drink category, ellsworth said, thanks to unilever's liquid i. and smaller upstarts like LMNT. V. On Amazon alone, powders are a $1 billion category, according to Ellsworth.

Berdasarkan laporan, the ready-to-drink, or rtd, sports beverages are a much larger market, but the category's sales are shrinking as consumers reach for other hydration options instead. And Coca-Cola has written down the value of BodyArmor by more than $1. 7 billion after buying control of the brand for $5. Unit sales of sports drinks have fallen 9. 1% from 2022 to 2026, according to Numerator data. 6 billion in late 2021.

"Me and my husband know how to do RTD," Ellsworth said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, jetty will launch with five flavors, including watermelon, orange mango, fruit punch, black raspberry and white cherry. All of them contain 100 milligrams of sodium, 310 milligrams of potassium and 100 milligrams of magnesium in a 15. 2-ounce bottle or 15-gram packet.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in addition to electrolytes, jetty products also contain b vitamins, 3 grams of fiber and 6 grams of sugar. It doesn't use artificial sweeteners or dyes, its founders say.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for comparison, a 20-ounce bottle of traditional gatorade thirst quencher has about 270 milligrams of sodium and 80 milligrams of potassium, plus 34 grams of sugar. The sports drink brand is also phasing out artificial colors and promoting lower-sugar versions.

"What's really interesting about this product and this opportunity is we now can capture all those lapsed drinkers — or that generation that didn't even ever drink it in the first place," Ellsworth said.

Poppi's new owner knows about Jetty and the market it is trying to capture, too.

Berdasarkan laporan, "i don't think [pepsi] gets it, but what they do get is that the movement is changing, and they think that just by taking dyes out or doing 90% less sugar, they're going to capture this audience," ellsworth said. "But that is very big corporate thinking. ".

She added that she believes Pepsi has missed the mark on advertising to Gen Z consumers across its portfolio, such as in its campaigns for Sprite competitor Starry.

Perhaps as an extension of that, Poppi's performance has been underwhelming under PepsiCo's ownership.

Diungkapkan bahwa the food and beverage giant now estimates the fair value of potential performance-based payments to poppi's prior owners is $12 million, pepsi said in a regulatory filing in october. At the time of the deal, Pepsi promised an additional payment of $300 million if Poppi hit certain targets by the third quarter of 2027. The Ellsworths declined to comment on the filing to CNBC.

Berdasarkan laporan, this time around, with one successful brand under their belts, jetty's founders say they have learned from past mistakes. Those lessons should help Jetty as it launches at a much larger scale than Poppi did.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, three different claims lawyers have signed off on jetty's packaging, according to ellsworth. Poppi paid $8. 9 million to settle class-action litigation alleging false advertising over its "gut healthy" claims.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for now, jetty is entirely self-funded with $2. 5 million, although Ellsworth said that the brand will likely raise money in 2027. This time, though, she said investors will probably look less like traditional venture capitalists.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "i want to bring in investors that bring value," ellsworth said. Instead of a venture capitalist who is willing to invest $15 million, Jetty would rather consider investors who can only write a check for $1 million but have access to celebrities. "So then you're getting access to talent on a cheaper level and people that are invested in the brand. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, and jetty has also learned a few lessons from gatorade. For example, the brand is already at work on a lemon-lime version — the original flavor of Gatorade.

Berdasarkan laporan, "we'll eventually do it," ellsworth said. "But it was really important at the beginning just to stick to flavors that we love, for it to taste good. ".

#176. ‘Heartland’ Review: Jessica Chastain Rocks a Stetson and a Swagger for a Soapy Nashville Noir

📅 13 Nov 2026

‘Heartland’ Review: Jessica Chastain Rocks a Stetson and a Swagger for a Soapy Nashville Noir

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://variety.com/2026/film/news/heartland-review-jessica-chastain-1236946587/

When a young relative goes missing, a jaded former country star returns to the industry that chewed her up in 'Country Strong' director Shana Feste's thriller, which can be gaudy fun, but eventually peters out.

Berdasarkan laporan, misty jones keeps her grammy in the fridge, alongside a near-empty tupperware of chicken broth and, well, not a whole lot else: a former country superstar turned burnt-out rural hermit, she more or less lives off what once was, but her memories don’t exactly nourish her. Related Stories 'Nobody Wants This' Season 3 Opens With 6. ” So does Jessica Chastain‘s surprisingly brash, beery performance as Misty, whose no-bullshit demeanor serves her well when she must turn amateur detective, investigating the disappearance of a relative who happens to be a rising country star herself. Peculiar details like these enliven “Heartland,” a missing-person mystery that returns writer-director Shana Feste to the Nashville milieu of her 2010 sophomore feature “Country Strong. 2 Million Views in Four Days Netflix’s 'Haunted Hotel' Renewed for Season 3.

Sebagaimana diketahui, fusing southern-fried noir atmospherics with the sequinned kitsch of a music city backstage melodrama, “heartland” often hits the same undemanding guilty-pleasure groove as “country strong” — or indeed the six-season run of tv’s “nashville” in the 2010s. What it isn’t, at nearly any point, is an effective thriller. Feste’s thin screenplay is heavily reliant on Chastain’s brio to sustain a quest that only narrowly makes sense on a moment-to-moment basis, and never gathers much intrigue — since the villains are all glaringly identifiable as such from the get-go, while Misty’s rough-diamond integrity is never in doubt. The result is diverting straight-to-Netflix fare, sparkly and disposable as a rhinestone, though its star commits as though it were something more.

Diungkapkan bahwa “there’s no such thing as good girls,” says misty early on in proceedings. And she comes out, quite literally, all guns blazing: In the film’s opening minutes, she feuds with a neighbor on the remote Georgia pecan farm where she’s settled, eventually taking a shotgun to the woman’s windows. It’s not entirely true — the character hides a kind, true heart beneath a gruffly embittered exterior — but it’s a solid pointer for Chastain, always at her most interesting when playing characters who are either morally off-base (“Dreams,” “A Most Violent Year”) or at least a little prickly and defensive. It’s our first taste of the hot temper that cost her a mainstream music career years ago — they called her “the cunt of country,” she says with some relish — though she rarely wields it against someone who doesn’t deserve it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s that hard-headed quality that her brother donny (paul sparks) calls upon when he comes to her for help. His 20-something daughter Charlie (singer Carter Faith, in her film debut), herself a buzzy new talent on the Nashville country scene, has recently gone missing, and he suspects shady showbiz machinations at play — something Misty knows plenty about, even if she left that world behind long ago. And so she turns gumshoe, with an oversize felt Stetson instead of a fedora, and a lineup of men to question that range from Charlie’s too-slick-by-half manager Roy (Garrett Hedlund) to an obsessed incel stalker.

Diungkapkan bahwa there are other, hidden reasons for misty to take on a job that isn’t really in her skill set, though they’re not quite satisfyingly addressed, as feste’s script toggles awkwardly between the procedural and the personal. Certain key relationships — notably that between Misty and Donny, brittle with shared secrets — are fleshed out in single scenes, never to be readdressed; elsewhere, the film dawdles on less pivotal connections, though there’s a lovely, wily supporting performance from Sugarland frontwoman Jennifer Nettles as a past friend-turned-rival, culminating in an onstage duet between her and Chastain that’s the highlight of the film’s original and on-the-money country song score. Where characters are sketchily drawn, casting is often more considered: Stalwarts like Hedlund, John Hawkes and Norbert Leo Butz all bring flickers of intelligence and eccentricity to fleeting or one-dimensional roles.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, still, this is chastain’s show, and she’s clearly enjoying it, often daring to play things quite broad and blustery, which rather suits the occasional tackiness of the material; at other points, she convincingly locates a quiet seam of deep-set pain in the protagonist, a casualty of an industry that, it is suggested here, often takes young female talent for a ride. Misty seems vaguely inspired by the enduring mystique of Bobbie Gentry, the prodigious Nashville singer-songwriter who, after a few years at the top, retired from music and checked out of the public eye entirely. Yet the film’s somewhat half-baked mystery tends to distract us from more dramatically probing questions about Misty herself, a curious character in search of a more curious character study.

#177. Hundreds of streaming services and nothing to watch

📅 12 Nov 2026

Hundreds of streaming services and nothing to watch

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/11/hundreds-of-streaming-services-and-nothing-to-watch/

Most viewers wish there was a TV Guide for streaming.

Bruce Springsteen famously said those words during a concert and later in a song in the 1990s about the number of TV channels seemingly growing disproportionately to the availability of enjoyable content.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, within a few years, there would be hundreds of tv channels and still, some would argue in hyperbolic frustration, “nothing to watch. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the advent of streaming services was poised as a potential solution to this problem. It granted viewers easy, on-demand access to thousands of movies and shows, which, theoretically, could ensure that viewers could always find something to watch.

According to a survey from Nielsen’s Gracenote, though, that’s not exactly the case today.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, gracenote, a nielsen-owned content data business, surveyed 3,000 video streaming users in the us, brazil, france, germany, mexico, and the uk who were at least 18 years old for its “2026 state of play: amid fragmentation frustrations, ux is the future of streaming” report. It found that many struggle to find something to stream. However, this is not necessarily because there’s nothing good on, but rather because they find it difficult to home in on good content on streaming services.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for example, over 51 percent of respondents said that “the abundance of content and [streaming] services is making it harder to find something to watch. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, further, 19. 2 percent of respondents said that, on average, they either “always” or “often” don’t know what to watch, can’t find anything, and then decide to do something else. And 27. 4 percent of respondents said that, on average, they either always or often try to watch a specific program but end up not watching it because they couldn’t find it on streaming.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “through the lens of catalogue size and streaming usage, connecting the 83. 4 percent who don’t always know what they want to watch should be fairly straightforward, especially as companies increasingly use customer data to create personalized experiences that foster long-term engagement and loyalty. Audiences, however, aren’t finding what they’re looking for, and content discovery challenges are mounting,” the report reads.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, forty-seven percent of participants said they spend more time looking for something to watch than they did a year ago. The average amount of time spent is 12 minutes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in recent years, numerous streaming services have paid large sums to air live events, including sports, to grow their advertising businesses. However, “nearly” 52 percent of streaming users that Gracenote surveyed said they “frequently don’t know which channel or service a specific sports event is on. ”.

“Sports events that are behind subscription paywalls are often hidden from traditional search, which inhibits discovery,” the report notes.

Berdasarkan laporan, and in an example of streaming users yearning for experiences most closely connected to traditional, broadcast television, gracenote reported that almost 35 percent of respondents spend more time watching free ad-supported streaming television services, such as tubi or the roku channel, because subscription-based alternatives, such as netflix and disney+, have “become overwhelming. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the on-demand nature of streaming services has degraded the need for live/virtual and print-out tv listings, such as a tv guide. But challenges in finding content on streaming services are apparently leading many streaming viewers to yearn for that classic form of guidance.

Diungkapkan bahwa in gracenote’s survey, 72. 3 percent of respondents said they want “a consolidated guide to the programming available across all of the streaming services that they use. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, streaming service providers and analysts i’ve spoken with have pointed to content discovery as a streaming challenge for years. Some, like Netflix and Amazon Prime Video, have turned to AI to help people search for content by using casual terms or to analyze viewing habits to make new recommendations. Others, such as Tubi, have turned to user-generated content playlists and recommendations.

Berdasarkan laporan, however, there is apparently still a deficit when it comes to good and accessible streaming recommendations, as 31 percent of survey respondents said they have yet to find a “good source of recommendations for their personal taste and preferences. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, despite there being hundreds of streaming services—as analysis this month from research firm parks and associates this month states—many would agree with springsteen that it still feels like there’s “nothin’ to watch. ”.

After all, you don’t need to know everything, only what’s important.

Diungkapkan bahwa endeavour was escorted by nasa armstrong’s f/a-18s and an f-15, which carried the photo and video teams in the back seats. Diungkapkan bahwa endeavour helped begin assembly of the international space station by delivering its first components to orbit and went on to complete 25 missions. The space shuttle will soon be seen, along with some of the images from the final flight, in its permanent home inside the new Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center at the California Science Center in Downtown Los Angeles.
