#179. A massive new simulation reveals how the universe emerged from darkness

📅 12 Nov 2026

A massive new simulation reveals how the universe emerged from darkness

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261110042534.htm

A powerful new computer simulation is allowing scientists to explore one of the most mysterious periods in cosmic history, when the universe emerged from darkness and the first stars and galaxies began to transform the cosmos.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, developed by researchers at mit, harvard university, and other institutions, the simulation, called lumina, recreates the evolution of the early universe across a region roughly 1. 6 billion light-years wide. It follows 2 billion years of cosmic history, revealing how galaxies formed, how radiation spread through space, and how the universe gradually became transparent to light.

The research, published in the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society (MNRAS), provides an unusually detailed picture of events that unfolded billions of years before our solar system existed.

How the Universe Entered Its Cosmic Dark Age.

Diungkapkan bahwa the story begins with the big bang, when the universe existed in an extremely hot, dense state filled with electrons and other subatomic particles. This primordial plasma, described as initially smaller than a single atom, expanded rapidly and cooled as the universe grew.

Berdasarkan laporan, eventually, particles slowed enough for electrons to combine with atomic nuclei, producing electrically neutral hydrogen. Around 380,000 years after the Big Bang, the universe entered a period known as the cosmic "dark age. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, although the universe had become transparent to much of the radiation left over from the big bang, stars had not yet formed to illuminate the cosmos. Neutral hydrogen filled space and could absorb certain types of radiation, including the ultraviolet light that would later emerge from the first stars.

Lumina allows researchers to investigate how this early environment evolved, eventually giving rise to the galaxies, stars, and other structures that helped bring the dark age to an end.

How the First Stars and Black Holes Transformed the Universe.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the simulation covers an immense region measuring 500 megaparsecs, equivalent to approximately 1. 6 billion light-years. Within that volume, Lumina follows dark matter, gas, stars, and radiation (such as photons), capturing both the behavior of matter across enormous distances and the formation of individual galaxies.

One of its most important achievements is recreating two major changes in the early universe: hydrogen re-ionization and helium re-ionization.

Diungkapkan bahwa hydrogen re-ionization began as the first stars and galaxies produced increasing amounts of ultraviolet radiation. This energetic light removed electrons from neutral hydrogen atoms, a process called "re-ionizing" the gas. As more hydrogen became ionized, the universe became increasingly transparent to ultraviolet light, allowing radiation to travel across much greater distances.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this transformation helped clear the widespread neutral hydrogen that had dominated the early cosmos. Lumina reproduces the process in remarkable detail, showing how radiation from the first generations of stars gradually changed the conditions throughout space.

The simulation also follows helium re-ionization, which requires substantially more energetic radiation to strip electrons from helium.

Diungkapkan bahwa the results point to different sources driving these two transformations. Early stars and galaxies appear to have been primarily responsible for ionizing hydrogen, while actively feeding supermassive black holes supplied the intense radiation needed to ionize helium.

This is the first simulation to capture both processes together, offering a more complete view of how the early universe changed.

"Lumina does everything from small-scale star and galaxy formation to large-scale reionization of hydrogen and helium, in a volume that is 100 times larger than previous best simulations," says study author Mark Vogelsberger, a professor of physics at MIT.

Diungkapkan bahwa the researchers are making lumina available to other scientists, allowing its predictions about early cosmic structures to be compared with observations from existing and future telescopes. Such comparisons could help researchers better understand the events that shaped the first galaxies and stars.

Building a Virtual Universe With Half a Trillion Elements.

Berdasarkan laporan, lumina gets its name from the latin word meaning "lights. " Its underlying technology builds on IllustrisTNG, an earlier simulation developed by scientists at MIT and other institutions, including members of the Lumina research team.

IllustrisTNG models how galaxies form and evolve by following the interactions of dark matter, gas, and other physical processes from the Big Bang to the present day.

Berdasarkan laporan, to create lumina, researchers upgraded the existing software so it could reproduce galaxy formation in comparable detail across a much larger region of space. They also incorporated a radiation transport model that calculates how light, including ultraviolet radiation, travels through the universe and interacts with surrounding matter.

Together, these improvements allow the simulation to track both the formation of galaxies and the enormous changes that radiation produces across cosmic distances.

Diungkapkan bahwa the resulting model contains approximately half a trillion individual elements, including particles of dark matter and cells representing gas. It provides roughly 30 times the resolution of IllustrisTNG while covering a region 100 times larger in volume than previous leading simulations.

Berdasarkan laporan, recreating billions of years of interactions across so many elements requires extraordinary computing resources. The researchers used Frontier, one of the world's most powerful supercomputers, located at Oak Ridge National Laboratory in Tennessee.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "at peak scale, the calculation brings together the equivalent of more than 100,000 cpu cores and around 15,000 gpus," says xuejian (jacob) shen, an mit co-author of the study. "Making all of those processors communicate efficiently while continuously evolving trillions of interacting pieces of information is itself an extraordinary feat of computer engineering. ".

Watching the First Galaxies Emerge From Darkness.

Lumina begins approximately 45 million years after the Big Bang, during an era when neutral hydrogen dominated the universe.

Berdasarkan laporan, researchers initialized the simulation using conditions based on scientists' understanding of that period. They then allowed the model to calculate how gas and dark matter interacted throughout its half a trillion elements as cosmic time progressed.

At the same time, Lumina tracked how radiation appeared, spread, and interacted with matter, including the ultraviolet light produced by emerging stars.

The result is a virtual universe that scientists can explore at dramatically different scales, from the arrangement of matter across enormous cosmic distances down to the development of a single galaxy.

Berdasarkan laporan, on the project website, the researchers have released videos showing these processes in action. One offers a "zoom-in" from the entire simulated region to an individual disk-shaped galaxy. Another presents a time-lapse of the complete volume, showing how hydrogen re-ionization spreads across the universe over 2 billion years.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "on the one hand, it's evolving dark matter as well as the gas in the universe, and on the other, it's also tracking how radiation travels," zier explains. Zooming in more, we see this is where the first galaxies form. And the first stars form in those first galaxies. And when we zoom in, we can see gas is falling into these dark matter haloes. The simulation then tracks that radiation, and we can zoom way out to see how that radiation travels out from stars, through the universe, until at some point it ionizes some neutral hydrogen. Those stars then create radiation. "We see dark matter and gas start to clump in these over-densities. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, this ability to move between vastly different scales is one of lumina's defining strengths. Researchers can examine the formation of individual galaxies while also observing how their combined radiation affects the universe on a much larger scale.

Berdasarkan laporan, "other simulations cannot zoom in as far as this," vogelsberger notes. "The difference between the smallest and largest scales that we simulate is larger than in any other simulation. ".

A New Way to Explore the Universe's Earliest History.

Berdasarkan laporan, the research team plans to use lumina to investigate the large-scale arrangement of matter in the early universe. The simulation could also help predict the patterns of gravitational waves generated by ancient galaxies and black holes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, another major opportunity will come from comparing lumina's virtual universe with real observations. New and upcoming telescopes are expected to collect increasingly detailed information about enormous numbers of distant galaxies, providing scientists with fresh ways to test their understanding of the early cosmos.

Because Lumina simulates such a large volume of space, it can generate extensive populations of galaxies that can be directly compared with these observations.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "one of lumina's major advantages is its sheer size," shen says. "It produces enormous populations of simulated galaxies, finally allowing us to make comparisons with the very large galaxy samples that upcoming surveys will observe. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, by bringing together detailed galaxy formation, dark matter, gas, and the movement of radiation, lumina offers researchers a powerful new tool for reconstructing the universe's earliest chapters. It may help explain not only how the first galaxies took shape, but also how their stars and black holes transformed the surrounding cosmos.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the study's mit authors include mark vogelsberger, xuejian (jacob) shen, and teodora-elena bluichi. Other contributors include first author Oliver Zier (a former postdoc in the Vogelsberger Lab), Rongrong Liu, Sonja Koehler, and Lars Hernquist of the Harvard and Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics; Aaron Smith of the University of Texas at Dallas; Rahul Kannan of York University in Canada; and Volker Springel and Rüdiger Pakmor of the Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics in Germany.

Berdasarkan laporan, the research received partial support from nasa and the national science foundation. S. It also used computing resources at the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, which is supported by the Advanced Scientific Computing Research programs within the Office of Science at the U. Department of Energy.

#181. ‘Pop Pop’ Dives Into Radicalization and Male Fragility in the Digital Age. Its Creator Says It’s “More Topical Every Day” – and Urges Us to Join Hands.

‘Pop Pop’ Dives Into Radicalization and Male Fragility in the Digital Age. Its Creator Says It’s “More Topical Every Day” – and Urges Us to Join Hands.

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/pop-pop-film-manosphere-trump-age-tallinn-2026-interview-1236752826/

Writer-director Dylan Stephen Levers' debut feature is a cinematic parable, premiering at Tallinn, that was partly shot at alt-right marches and is full of memes and indie spirit.

Berdasarkan laporan, u. S. filmmaker Dylan Stephen Levers’ (this is a film about tom and maddy) debut feature, Pop Pop, is a cinematic parable that hits us not only with unusual and memorable visuals and sounds, but also hits us hard with all sorts of queasiness-inducing questions for our age of virality, digital nihilism, the manosphere and radicalization.

Diungkapkan bahwa in true independent spirit and pop art fashion, the movie is a cinematic mash-up of meme culture, trips into cyberspace and alt-right protests that explores toxic masculinity, cancel culture and a sea of identity crises without any apparent lifeboats. Related Stories TV "Evil All Along": How Russell Brand Got Caught Business Around 10-15 Percent of SAG-AFTRA Membership Wants AI Blocked, CEO Tells Web Summit.

Berdasarkan laporan, pop pop gets its world premiere on sunday during the 30th edition of the tallinn black nights film festival (pöff) in estonia. And it only seems fitting that it debuts in the fest’s Rebels With a Cause Competition program.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, written and directed by levers, pop pop stars cashton tate rehklau, trevor jonathan lown and lena kutscher, along with austin davis, djuna knight, kevin confoy and marta kotzien. Rehklau and Lown are Dustin and Dibz, best friends who survived their senior year of college and now share an apartment in New York and an Internet series. But where do they go from here? Well, they end up taking very different paths.

Diungkapkan bahwa dustin becomes immersed in an increasingly radical worldview, focusing on attracting attention and a following via provocative online posts. Dibz finds meaning in social justice activism and his first crush on a man, forcing him to reconsider his identity. The film mixes fictional scenes with footage shot during real-life protests and psychedelic animations that take the audience into the digital world, including the manosphere.

Berdasarkan laporan, pop pop is a body by lulz films production, co-produced by grease nyc. The cinematographer is Consuelo Althouse, while Josh Coll handled editing. W. Ian Ross, Levers and Althouse produced Pop Pop, with Stefanie Abel Horowitz, Josh Bierne-Golden and Erin Magill serving as executive producers.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in a director’s statement, levers says he began writing pop pop in 2016, “as angry white men were gathering online, sharing extremist ideas about immigrants, islam, women, and the supposed destruction of the ‘white race. ’ What the media dismissed as a fringe movement soon became a significant political force. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the filmmaker decided to explore what it means to be a man today. S. Ahead of its world premiere, Levers talked to THR about Pop Pop, his inspirations and hopes for the film, and how the U. , and the world, may be able to be less divided – or at least divided with less rage.

When and how did the inspiration to create Pop Pop hit you?.

Berdasarkan laporan, i started writing this many, many years ago. , there were things coming out like Girls and Frances Ha that so many of my friends were really identifying with because they talked very eloquently about young womanhood and graduating from being a girl to an adult. We would get together every six months with a group of actors and just hammer away at the script and make it better and better. The coming-of-age tale is evergreen in film and TV. S. Especially in the U. I come from a theater background, so this was developed like a new play. In February of 2020, it felt ready to go. But I thought, “Well, where’s the conversation around men?” I started convening groups of people for little sessions and just writing things here and there. And three weeks later, there was COVID, and the world shut down.

Diungkapkan bahwa it felt a little dead on arrival. But throughout that summer of 2020, a lot of the things that were already present as narrative came to the forefront even more. The film is set in the middle of the 2016 election cycle, but issues around masculinity, what it means to be a man, what it means to be in community with other people, whether that’s digital or otherwise, almost felt like they were on steroids now. It’s become, strangely, more and more topical every day.

Diungkapkan bahwa since you mentioned the election that first made donald trump u. S. President, I want to ask you about political marches that we see in Pop Pop. It looks like you actually shot during real protests…did you?.

Berdasarkan laporan, i had done all this research in 2019 about these alt-right protests, and i had been to a bunch of them. It felt very fringe and very contained, but if you were there, you felt, “Oh my god, we can’t turn away. This is just going to get bigger and bigger. Famously, there was one in the Boston area called the “Straight Pride” protest, and the parade marshal was Milo Yiannopoulos. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa and the filmmaker part of me felt it just saw such amazing production value in this horrible protest. So, how do we recreate that on screen? And our cinematographer, Consuelo Althouse, because she’s a genius and has an amazing background in doc filmmaking, said one of the things that we could do was shoot in some of these protests. So we did.

Diungkapkan bahwa [a consultant on the political things on the film] told us that the protest that we really should be going to was in d. 6. And so it ultimately functioned as the dress rehearsal for Jan. It ended up being in December of 2020, three weeks before Jan. 6. , which was a “Stop the Steal” protest led by this guy Ali Alexander. C. And as we were watching the news that day, we were like, “Oh my God, that guy’s in our footage! That guy’s in the footage! And that guy!”.

How did you approach or think about filming inside those protests, especially sending in your actor who plays Dibz?.

Berdasarkan laporan, consuelo and i had a lot of conversations about the ethics of shooting in an event that had its own purpose and was not being staged for the purpose of being on screen. We made a pact to take this one character, Dibz, and let the action unfold around him. We were not going to try to affect any part of the proceedings of that day, but let’s try to see if we can really catch those colors, those textures, the craziness of the day, which, even if we had millions of dollars for production design, would not have looked as authentic as what you see on screen.

Sebagaimana diketahui, trevor, who plays dibz, is such an amazing and brave actor. So we had precautions in place. In no way was I willing to traumatize any crew or cast members by making this film, and in no way were we trying to put anybody’s lives in physical danger. We said if anything sketchy happens, we’d regroup at a meeting point. But it was definitely always safety first. There were a couple of people, as we were shooting throughout the day, who were like, “Why do you have such a large camera? What are you guys doing?” And we just said, “Oh, we’re an independent outlet,” and they loved the idea that we weren’t the corporate media.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in pop pop, we see some modern-looking scenes in the cyber sphere but also an older-looking computer with its loud typing sounds and retro-feeling pop-up windows and the like. Can you explain how important it was for you that the technology side of the story of the film was reflected by the visual experience?.

Diungkapkan bahwa i always love to ask what the organizing principle of a story is. I thought of this computer screen almost as a character to start priming the audience for the rules of that kind of existence. The idea was to put this device into this story that’s a deeply digital one.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, and the digital space is a mix of stuff that we made up and actual memes. There are memes that would have been popular in 2016. My biggest dream for this movie is, and I’ll know I have made it then, that somebody writes a listicle called “25 Memes That You Can See in Pop Pop. There’s a Drake dancing, there’s Obama, they’re flying over what’s called the political compass, which is a meme that lets you self-locate where you are politically, and then there are some more obscure gems. ”.

Since you just mentioned the title again, how did you choose that?.

Berdasarkan laporan, to me, it was about the feeling of everything breaking apart. My generation in the States grew up with this idea that institutions were healthy and that there were certain social contracts that would never be broken. But we have seen in the past 12-plus years that there’s been a giant pickaxe that has been taken to that version of reality. So, the title is in reference to that breaking down and that combustible tinderbox energy of everything just sort of blowing up.

Berdasarkan laporan, but it is also that this is pop filmmaking, which is about swallowing everything and metabolizing it so it becomes this different thing. Here’s all this imagery – let’s put it through the wringer and talk about it, interrogate it, and see where we land. So it’s a little bit of an accidental double entendre.

Sebagaimana diketahui, you say double entendre, so i need to ask you about that great double act that your two leads are. These brilliant young actors are giving incredible performances. I cannot wait for people to see them. And Lena and the others give it all a real ensemble vibe. I really hope that we can introduce people to them. They are amazing. I am so excited for people to see them for the first time.

I assume you didn’t have a huge budget and didn’t win the lottery?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, no, i worked to pay the bills and keep the lights on, producing big events for brands [and things like that as a day job]. A. telling people to use circular Legos, not the square ones. I was doing crazy shit, including following a giant Bath & Body Works candle around the Eastern Seaboard or going to the Grove in L. I just kept Tetris-ing every single job I possibly could into my schedule without going absolutely insane. I also got really lucky in that my collaborators were really down and kept coming back to this project time and time again.

Berdasarkan laporan, i think this was true indie filmmaking. The hope and dream is that, as we watch in our industry all of these conglomerates sell to each other and combine forces, what happens is a healthier indie undercurrent, so that films like this and filmmakers who have ideas that are a little bit more out there can get their films made with less strife than five years of Tetris-ing so many jobs together.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the “thank you” section of the credits, i saw the name zazie beetz. Is that THE Zazie Beetz?.

Yes, she and her now-husband David [Rysdahl] did some very early development on this film.

Diungkapkan bahwa after i watched pop pop, i felt motivated to try harder again to keep in dialogue with people who may not always share my political or other ideas or hopes. What’s your hope for audiences of Pop Pop?.

Diungkapkan bahwa i hope it causes massive fights and wrecks entire families. No, I’m kidding! (laughs) I really set out to make a movie about people who are right when they’re wrong and wrong when they’re right and what it means to be morally three-dimensional in a world that provides us with not many great options for being a good person.

Berdasarkan laporan, so, yes, i wanted to ask how we deal with other people who we potentially don’t agree with, but we still have to be in community with. It’s really about thinking seriously about community building and coalition building. I think one of the things that this country has to do is to figure out how we can build coalitions, and part of that is joining hands with people that we don’t necessarily always agree with and figuring out what is still left in the concentric circles between us.

Berdasarkan laporan, it’s my hope that folks can utilize the film as a jumping-off point to talk about their own struggles. A lot of us are about to go home for Thanksgiving and have anxiety-inducing political conversations around the family table. Perhaps, once you see this movie, instead of pointing to your uncle with whom you disagree, or fighting with your mother, you can look at these characters and use them as ciphers to have discussions instead of pointing fingers.

I’m hungry for other filmmakers to go out there and make films that really are responding to and rising to meet the moment, and I want to meet them.

Sebagaimana diketahui, starship consists of two elements: a huge booster known as super heavy and an upper-stage spacecraft called starship, or ship for short. Both are designed to be fully and rapidly reusable — a first in the world of orbital spaceflight.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, spacex has already caught super heavy, pulling the feat off on three previous starship test flights. But it has never tried to do so with Ship, which flies farther and faster than the booster and is therefore a more challenging vehicle to recover.

So today's flight is a pretty big deal for SpaceX.

"If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket," the company wrote in a Flight 15 mission description.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the action will unspool over two days, if all goes to plan. Super Heavy will return to Starbase for a touchdown just 6. 5 minutes after launch, but Ship will continue on to low Earth orbit.

Diungkapkan bahwa the upper stage will deploy 26 of spacex's next-gen starlink v3 satellites, during a 42-minute stretch beginning about 35 minutes after liftoff. This will be just the second batch of V3 spacecraft to reach orbit, after the 26 that went up on Flight 14 on Sept. 28.

Berdasarkan laporan, ship will then stay aloft for nearly a full day. The mission plan calls for the upper stage to return to Starbase for its chopsticks catch on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), about 22. 5 hours after liftoff.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there's no guarantee things will go according to plan, however. SpaceX will call off a Ship catch if the vehicle experiences any issues during Flight 15. If something crops up, the company will steer Ship to a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean, either near Hawaii or off the coast of Chile.

Sebagaimana diketahui, so it'll be a busy weekend for spacex, and for space fans who want to keep tabs on the mission. And we can help you out there, with our Flight 15 updates page.

#185. Scientists discover a giant 66-pound rodent that lived 34 million years ago

📅 11 Nov 2026

Scientists discover a giant 66-pound rodent that lived 34 million years ago

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261110042532.htm

Sebagaimana diketahui, an ancient rodent of extraordinary size has been identified from fossils uncovered in a mine in southern thailand. The discovery, made by an international team of paleontologists that includes scientists from McGill University, provides new evidence that giant rodents appeared much earlier and in more parts of the world than previously believed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the researchers found "remarkably large" fossilized teeth belonging to a previously unknown species called yakamys sirindhornae. This prehistoric rodent lived approximately 34 million years ago, during the middle of the Paleogene period. Its remains, consisting of a lower second molar and a lower incisor, were recovered from the Bang Mark Pit at the Krabi lignite mine in Thailand's Krabi Province.

Diungkapkan bahwa although only two teeth have been identified, they offer valuable clues about rodent gigantism, the evolutionary process through which rodents develop unusually large bodies. The discovery suggests that Southeast Asia played a more significant role in the early evolution of giant rodents than scientists had recognized.

Giant Rodents Have a Much Older History Than Expected.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "today, the largest living rodent is the capybara, but very large rodents are not restricted to recent ecosystems," said virginie millien, a biology professor at mcgill university and co-author of the study. "Giant rodents evolved repeatedly during the later history of the group, mostly in South America. This discovery suggests that Southeast Asia also played an important role in the early evolutionary history of large-bodied rodents. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, the newly identified animal's name reflects both its impressive size and its connection to thailand. Yakamys combines "yak," the Thai word for giant, with "mys," the Greek word for mouse or rat.

The second part of its scientific name recognizes an important supporter of scientific research in Thailand.

"The species name, sirindhornae, honors Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn, in recognition of her longstanding support for science and paleontological research in Thailand," Millien said.

How Big Was This 34-Million-Year-Old Rodent?.

Berdasarkan laporan, to estimate the animal's size, the research team applied seven established methods that use tooth measurements to calculate body mass. Their results suggest that Yakamys sirindhornae weighed approximately 30 kilograms, making it about twice as heavy as other known rodents from the same period, including Hulgana.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that would have made the newly discovered species exceptionally large compared with its contemporaries. However, the researchers emphasize that determining an extinct animal's weight from a small number of fossilized teeth involves considerable uncertainty.

"This is only a ballpark figure, as there is substantial uncertainty associated with fossil body-mass estimation," Millien said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the limited fossil evidence also makes it difficult to reconstruct how yakamys evolved or what its life was like. Additional discoveries will be needed to better understand its physical characteristics, ecological role, and evolutionary relationships.

International Research Uncovers Thailand's Prehistoric Past.

Diungkapkan bahwa the fossils were identified through an ongoing international collaboration investigating ancient mammals in thailand's krabi basin. The project brings together scientists from McGill University, Thailand's Department of Mineral Resources, and French research organizations, including CNRS and Université de Poitiers.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, by revealing evidence of an unusually large rodent in southeast asia 34 million years ago, the discovery expands scientists' understanding of where and when rodent gigantism emerged. Future fossil finds could help establish how these ancient giants lived and how their evolution relates to the enormous rodents that appeared elsewhere in the world.

The research received support from CNRS, Université de Poitiers, Université de Montpellier, McGill University, and the Department of Mineral Resources of Thailand.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “lois was a dream choice, and we couldn’t be more thrilled to have her. ”.

“Outside of Cleveland” also stars Alex Wolff, Brooklynn Prince, Jim Gaffigan, Sarah Wayne Callies and Michael Ian Black.

As pointed out by West, at the 2017 Gotham Awards, Prince and Smith were among the youngest and oldest nominees ever for “The Florida Project” and “Marjorie Prime” respectively.

“Years later, they end up in the same movie,” he enthused.

Sebagaimana diketahui, west’s film, selected for the u. in Progress co-production forum at Poland’s Tauron American Film Festival, is produced by Brain Scratch Productions, 1515 Films and Sub_Sequential Pictures. S. His previous, “Linoleum,” premiered at SXSW.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the cast always hinged on max’s character, so that’s where we started. Alex Wolff was an immediate choice as not only is he an incredible musician, he can also convey both the world-worn weariness of adulthood and the spark of adolescence, often within the same scene,” he said.

Diungkapkan bahwa “from there, since the story moves fluidly between two timelines without relying on gimmicks, i needed actors who could make the family feel lived-in from the first frame. Jim, with whom I’d worked before, and Sarah possess that warmth and humor, and Brooklynn brings an honesty and maturity that’s rare at any age. Lois ended up being the final key to that family dynamic and I was thrilled to see it all come together seamlessly. ”.

West isn’t hiding that the story he’s telling is very personal.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it’s always hard to put that much of yourself on screen, and there were days on set in ohio that almost felt a little too close to home. My art team had asked my parents for items, and it freaked me out, but also brought a smile to my face. When I entered Max’s room after our production design team had finished with it, I saw actual items from my own childhood. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, he added: “making any form of art should always be part exploration and part excavation, and this was the perfect combination of the two. I see home. Once I stopped trying to hide from the personal, the film became more relatable and honest. And I am deeply indebted to my team for making that happen. When I watch it, I see the Ohio that I know and love. ”.

#187. Review: Apple's M6 iMac is pricey, but it's still a good choice for a clean desk

📅 12 Nov 2026

Review: Apple's M6 iMac is pricey, but it's still a good choice for a clean desk

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://arstechnica.com/features/2026/11/review-apples-m6-imac-is-pricey-but-its-still-a-good-choice-for-a-clean-desk/

Apple’s M6 keeps the iMac current without shaking things up much.

The Apple Silicon iMac got its fourth refresh this month.

Every other Apple Silicon Mac has found a way to move forward over the last half-decade—we’ve gotten a more Pro design for the MacBook Pro, a mini-er design for the Mac mini, and a Mac Studio that has finally made Apple admit it doesn’t want to make the Mac Pro anymore.

Berdasarkan laporan, but the apple silicon imac has always been more interested in looking backward. It’s a clean and pretty desktop computer, one I see all the time in small offices and on TV shows that depict small offices. It’s the thin, screen-on-a-stand iMac design by way of the original Bondi Blue G3 iMac. We’re long past the days when it was Apple’s primary workstation computer.

Diungkapkan bahwa so i wanted to write about this new imac from the perspective of that entry-level imac buyer, who chooses the imac because it’s simple and then uses it until it breaks. What does a new iMac get you if you’re stepping up from the M1 model or comparing it against an older refurbished M4 model? Without any real external updates, what makes this iMac iteration interesting?.

If you haven’t used an Apple Silicon-era iMac before, here’s a brief primer.

Berdasarkan laporan, the new imac is much thinner than the older aluminum intel models. Its front is mostly one big 24-inch screen, surrounded on all sides by a relatively thick white bezel (I still wish black were at least an option, but Apple apparently doesn’t agree).

Sebagaimana diketahui, white bezel aside, it’s by far apple’s most colorful computer. The iMacs ship with color-matched fronts, backs, stands, keyboards, mice, trackpads, and cables. Apple has tweaked the color offerings and changed the tints of each specific color a few times over the years, but the M6 iMac uses the same six color tints (plus silver) that the M4 iMac did.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the basic $1,499 imac is essentially a macbook air in terms of ports—it has two thunderbolt ports on the back and a headphone jack on the left side. Choosing this model also locks you into a lesser version of the Apple M6 with 10 CPU cores and 10 GPU cores instead of 12 of each, a maximum of 24GB of RAM, a minimum of 256GB of storage, and a maximum of 1TB. Its default keyboard doesn’t have Touch ID support, and the only way to get it is to buy the version with the built-in number pad, an $80 upsell.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the $1,699 version is the one to get if you still intend to use the imac as a workstation. This version also includes four Thunderbolt ports on the back for connecting additional accessories. It includes the full-speed version of the M6 with all its CPU and GPU cores intact (though there are performance caveats here we’ll talk about later), plus options for 32GB of RAM and up to 2TB of storage. Both available keyboards on this version have Touch ID.

Diungkapkan bahwa a 2. 5 gigabit Ethernet port can be added to any iMac for $30. This port is located on the desktop’s power brick rather than the iMac itself, an elegant solution that keeps even a wired Internet connection hidden beneath your desk with the other cables. All iMacs also offer a VESA mount adapter option in place of the default stand at no extra charge.

Berdasarkan laporan, i still really like the effect created by the color-matched keyboard, mouse/trackpad, and cables—even the white bezel complements the white keycaps and mouse. Just know you’re paying quite a lot for how the desktop looks. The $899 Mac mini is $800 cheaper than the iMac with the same chip, the same amount of RAM, and the same amount of storage. Sure, it would cost something to add a nice-looking 4K monitor, but not $800, even if you go for extra frills like a high refresh rate.

Diungkapkan bahwa it’s fine that the imac upcharges you for style and convenience. That’s the point of the computer. Just make sure that’s what you want to pay for.

Here are the basic specs for every entry-level iMac Apple has shipped, going all the way back to the last of the Intel models.

Diungkapkan bahwa the imac’s evolution has been slow and gradual during the apple silicon era. The computer has never gotten a base storage upgrade, and the base M4 and M6 models still only support a single external display (the upgraded models support two external displays, finally surpassing the old Intel model).

Berdasarkan laporan, if you have any kind of apple silicon imac and you’re happy with how it’s performing and you’re not hankering for more ram or more displays, i don’t think the m6 model really adds anything worth upgrading for. It’s definitely faster, but even six years on, the Apple M1 remains perfectly serviceable for daily use, especially when it’s attached to 16GB of RAM.

Berdasarkan laporan, and if you’re in the market for an imac now, i think the m4 model still gets you the best bang for your buck if you can find one refurbished or on sale. That one still gets you a minimum of 16GB of RAM, Thunderbolt in all four ports for the four-port model, the 32GB RAM option, the nano-texture display option, and support for multiple external displays (again, in the four-port model).

Sebagaimana diketahui, the m6 imac builds on that, and it comes with real performance benefits (more on that shortly). But the brightest dividing line in the Apple Silicon iMac model history is between the M3 and M4 model, not the M4 and M6 model. And that’s true despite the two-generation silicon upgrade.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a quick recap on the m6: a total of 12 cpu cores (two super cores, four performance cores, six efficiency cores), either 10 or 12 gpu cores, 16/24/32gb ram options, and a doubled neural engine npu with 32 cores instead of 16. For the iMac, the M6 also introduces some of the architectural tweaks introduced with the Apple M5, including the addition of neural accelerator hardware to the GPU cores. This boosts the speed of some kinds of local AI workloads compared to the M4, including MetalFX upscaling and frame generation in games.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the m6 in the mac mini and the m6 in the 14-inch macbook pro both perform similarly within a roughly 28 w sustained power envelope. The version with 16GB of RAM will perform slightly worse in games and other workloads sensitive to memory bandwidth—the 16GB M6 offers 153 GB/s of memory bandwidth, and the 24GB and 32GB versions offer 170 GB/s. But that’s a pretty minor difference.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the imac is slower than either of those two macs, particularly in multi-core cpu benchmarks and graphics benchmarks, and the handbrake video encoding test shows the likely culprit. The iMac’s M6 consumes an average of 18 W of power under sustained heavy load. It won’t throttle its speeds as aggressively as a MacBook Air because the iMac still includes an active cooling fan, but the reduced power envelope does mean that the Mac mini or MacBook Pro are 5 to 8 percent faster than the iMac in heavy multi-core CPU tasks and about 8 to 12 percent faster in graphics benchmarks.

One benefit of the smaller power envelope is that the iMac’s chip is even more power-efficient than the regular M6 and the iMac’s version of the M4, using much less power to do the same amount of work.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that still makes it a solid upgrade over the m4. The iMac’s M6 is 15 to 20 percent faster in our single-core CPU benchmarks, between 20 and 30 percent faster in multi-core CPU benchmarks, and between 20 and 40 percent faster in graphics benchmarks (the Blender GPU benchmarks do even better—they seem to like the neural accelerators in the M5 and M6 GPUs). Especially with 24GB or 32GB of RAM, it’s perfectly capable of being the heart of a multi-monitor workstation setup or a light photo/video editing rig.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the m6 imac changes almost nothing about who the imac is for, its position in apple’s lineup, or what it’s technically capable of. It’s a box-ticking upgrade, and the box being ticked is “keep the insides up to date. ”.

That means today’s iMac is best for the same kinds of computer users it was good for in 1998: people who don’t want a laptop, people who need a friendly and approachable kiosk or office computer, and people who just want something pretty that doesn’t require a lot of fussing with screens or cables.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that’s the main thing i miss about being an imac user. I like how my current Mac Studio desktop works, and I need flexibility and complexity in my specific setup to get the Mac and a gaming PC connected to all the same stuff. But despite my best efforts, the cable situation has always been a barely managed mess.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if someone you know has a cable management problem and doesn’t need the complexity, congratulations, you’ve found someone the imac is for. I just wish Apple would use these kinds of pretty, saturated colors in a laptop or desktop that meets my needs, you know?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ars technica has been separating the signal from the noise for over 25 years. With our unique combination of technical savvy and wide-ranging interest in the technological arts and sciences, Ars is the trusted source in a sea of information. After all, you don’t need to know everything, only what’s important.

#188. How to Rob a Bank review: This eat-the-rich thriller from Amazon has the psychological depth of a kiddie pool

📅 13 Nov 2026

How to Rob a Bank review: This eat-the-rich thriller from Amazon has the psychological depth of a kiddie pool

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://mashable.com/entertainment/how-to-rob-a-bank-review

Diungkapkan bahwa earlier this year, i reflected in my review of how to make a killing that cinema has been riding a wave of eat-the-rich comedies since 2019, when parasite and ready or not made class conflict into ghoulish fun. Since then, we've seen the good (Triangle of Sadness, The Menu, Send Help, I Love Boosters), the bad (How to Make a Killing), and the truly awful (The Running Man reboot).

So, how does How to Rob a Bank, the latest from David Leitch, stack up? Oh, very poorly, and that's actually shocking at first glance.

Sebagaimana diketahui, let's consider the talent behind how to rob a bank. For starters, the production is helmed by David Leitch, who's directed such compelling action movies as Atomic Blonde, Deadpool 2, and The Fall Guy. The original screenplay comes from Mark Bianculli, a writer who worked on Hunters, an intense drama about a group that hunts down Nazis. The ensemble cast boasts Nicholas Hoult, Anna Sawai, John C. Reilly, Zoë Kravitz, and Pete Davidson.

Berdasarkan laporan, all this suggests that a bank robbery thriller centered on class warfare might feature explosive action, challenging ideas, and rich emotional moments. Instead, How to Rob a Bank is a flashy, brainless mockery of the great American bank robbery movie. However, produced and distributed by billionaire Jeff Bezos' Amazon MGM Studios, this eat-the-rich movie never dares to get that deep. Who could guess why?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this thriller gets off to a kinetic start by pitching the audience into a band of charismatic bank robbers; they wear animal masks and document their crimes in a youtube web series that encourages others to follow in their footsteps. Through voiceover narration, their dashing leader Ryan (Hoult) delivers some rapid-fire statistics about the American wage gap, arguing that robbing a bank offers a better chance of financial security than banking on the system playing fair.

Sebagaimana diketahui, exactly which system ryan is referring to is left vague in bianculli's screenplay. These robbers explain that banks bleed lenders dry, steal homes, and essentially kill people who can't afford medical care. These arguments are delivered in bullet-point form, as are the scraps of character development of their central anti-heroes. There will be glancing critiques about the mistreatment of military veterans, healthcare under capitalism, and immigration reform, but the focus here is on banks. That makes it hard to feel invested in either.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, instead of delving into the robbers' lives, the movie cuts to the fbi agent (reilly) who's cajoling a bitter hacker (kravitz) to give him her batman-level stalker tech to track them down. While this setup has promise, she eats junk food and cracks meh jokes while he furrows his brow to unmask these robbers. She agrees reluctantly between bong hits, which make up about 40% of her character, and they set off on a wonky buddy-cop adventure. It's far from the sparks and fun of Lethal Weapon or Beverly Hills Cop.

Diungkapkan bahwa by the time how to rob a bank has set up this could-be cat-and-mouse dynamic, the actual exploration of who these thieves are feels like an afterthought. To Hoult's credit, he and his onscreen wife, Emi (Sawai), manage to muster engaging intimacy in some thin scenes. But all of these backstory scenes reek of tropes and stereotypes.

Diungkapkan bahwa for instance, hugo (rhenzy feliz) lives in a crowded apartment building, where he provides for his spanish-speaking grandmother, who we learn later is undocumented. Meanwhile, Ryan and his wife live in a decaying house, where pictures of their deceased child provide an unspoken motive. And then there's Pete Davidson's Vince, who lumbers into a treacly scene singing a lullaby to his child, while his wife, Skyler (Tati Gabrielle, who is given nothing to do), looks on smiling.

Berdasarkan laporan, they aren't characters but figures propped up by cliché and half-hearted politics the movie has no real interest in. It's never really clear what Ryan's big plan is between the robberies and his social media campaign. Is he just seeking revenge? Or is he earnestly pushing for revolution? And if so, what kind? Hoult is given plenty of rabid monologues for the gang's YouTube audience to enjoy. But who Ryan is behind his wolf mask remains ambiguous, and frankly boring.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in american cinema, bank robbers have a dubious place of honor alongside gangsters. These anti-heroes expose the broken system of American capitalism and its corrupt government, and then suggest that their crimes are a defiant middle finger to it all. They are the flip side to the white hat-wearing cowboy, who fights for the good of all by going outside the rules of a polite society. To them, they must break the laws to achieve their American dream.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in movies like dog day afternoon, set it off, and the town, audiences are urged to identify with the robbers, who are average folks making extraordinary choices to combat their bad fortune. Their hopes, fears, and pain become our own. In each of these films, a great director explores the bank robbers' psyches and their worlds, so that we, the audience, can relate. So, when they inevitably suffer a deadly loss in their pursuit of this twisted American dream, we hurt too. And then we're left to wonder what it means about our world that we can root for armed thieves to topple some aspect of it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, how to rob a bank gestures to this classic arc. To Leitch's credit, the film feels firmly set in Pittsburgh, where long-standing brick buildings, towering yellow bridges, and rolling hills strewn with weathered houses give a distinct look that speaks of America's promise and decline. He also embraces vibrant color, which adds pizzazz to the robbers and their online videos. But when it comes to creating complex characters who can make an onscreen death hit hard, he falls absolutely flat.

Berdasarkan laporan, sure, there's that scene where one of the gang will inevitably be slain by stone-faced police. But this time it won't hit, because How to Rob a Bank's characters all feel like gestures to a point of view, be it disillusioned, revolutionary, apathetic, or dedicated to the status quo. They don't feel real enough to move us, because How to Rob a Bank is in such a rush to plop in action set pieces.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and how are those action set pieces? underwhelming. Sure, there's gunfire, car chases, motorcycle races through untamed woods, and street-level mayhem. None of it is all that memorable. As someone who fell hard for the jaw-dropping stunts and awesome battles of Atomic Blonde, I take no joy in telling you that it feels like Leitch is phoning it in here.

Sebagaimana diketahui, to the ensemble's credit, they do seem committed to making the most out of thin characters, stale jokes, and nattering political rhetoric. But they can't elevate a script that is juvenile in its politics and devastatingly uninterested in challenging its audience.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the end, how to rob a bank adds nothing to the conversation about the wealth gap. Instead, the movie callously steals markers from online political discourse to use as flair, which is haphazardly flung upon a subgenre framework meant to stir up an audience and then haunt them with a film's final moments. Then it delivers an ending that's senseless and pointless. This gutless knockoff gives no thought-provoking turns or heart-wrenching reveals. Simply put, this movie could have been a meme.

#189. Scotland’s Flow Country

📅 12 Nov 2026

Scotland’s Flow Country

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/scotlands-flow-country/

Blanket bogs in the Scottish Highlands store vast amounts of carbon.

Berdasarkan laporan, compared to ecosystems in many other parts of the world, the blanket bogs of the flow country in northern scotland are unassuming—soggy, treeless landscapes dominated by hummocky mosses, grasses, and heathers. Yet, to ecologists, the seemingly desolate areas are nothing short of extraordinary.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the bogs store tremendous quantities of carbon. That’s because their soils are so waterlogged that microbes cannot fully break down dead plant material, a process that would otherwise release carbon dioxide. Instead, partially decayed plant matter accumulates into thick layers of spongy, crumbly, carbon-rich material called peat.

Diungkapkan bahwa the unusual ecosystems, also called blanket mires and featherbed bogs, only occur in places with abundant rainfall, poor drainage, and low levels of evapotranspiration. These types of bogs cover just 120,000 square kilometers (46,000 square miles) globally, less than one-tenth of one percent of Earth’s land surface. The image above, captured by the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 8, is centered on blanket bogs in the Scottish Highlands, home to the largest such ecosystem in Europe. This peatland is also the first of its type to be inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the peat bogs of northern scotland, home to more than 30 species of sphagnum moss, are spread across some 1,900 square kilometers (730 square miles) of the country’s highlands region. The light green area on the right side around Thurso is farmland. The darker green geometric patterns in the center are conifer plantations. In this image, boggy areas appear dark brown and are sprinkled with lakes. The image was captured in the spring, the part of the year when the land surface is most waterlogged and peat bogs begin to accumulate large amounts of new biomass.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, while forests store most of their carbon in living trees—which eventually release it back into the atmosphere when they burn or die—peat bogs often store carbon for many thousands of years. Some parts of the Flow Country have been accumulating peat for more than 9,000 years, building deposits exceeding eight meters thick, according to UNESCO. Overall, scientists estimate that all of the world’s peatlands cover just 3 percent of Earth’s land surface but store more than 600 gigatons of carbon—about twice as much as all the world’s forests combined.

Sebagaimana diketahui, nasa earth observatory images by michala garrison, using landsat data from the u. S. Geological Survey. Story by Adam Voiland.

#191. Why heart attacks can still happen even when bad cholesterol is low

📅 10 Nov 2026

Why heart attacks can still happen even when bad cholesterol is low

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261109205415.htm

Diungkapkan bahwa researchers at chalmers university of technology in sweden have uncovered new clues about why some people develop heart disease even after lowering their bad cholesterol to recommended levels. Their findings point to biological processes involving other fat-carrying particles in the blood that may contribute to cardiovascular damage in ways that go beyond cholesterol buildup. By identifying these previously poorly understood mechanisms, the research could help pave the way for more targeted strategies to prevent heart disease and potentially save lives.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, heart disease remains one of the world's leading causes of death. Coronary heart disease develops when fatty deposits containing cholesterol (cholesterol) build up inside the arteries that supply blood to the heart. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), cardiovascular diseases kill nearly 17. 9 million people worldwide each year, with heart attacks and strokes responsible for more than 80% of those deaths. If left untreated, the condition can eventually cause a heart attack.

Sebagaimana diketahui, reducing ldl cholesterol, commonly known as "bad cholesterol," is a proven way to lower the likelihood of a heart attack. However, bringing LDL cholesterol into the recommended range does not eliminate the danger. Some patients continue to develop coronary heart disease despite successful treatment, suggesting that other particles transporting fats through the bloodstream play an important role. Until recently, the biological reasons behind this remaining risk were not well understood.

"For this study, we wanted to understand what happens beyond the accumulation of cholesterol in artery walls, whether different fat-carrying particles can damage the blood vessels differently and why the remaining risk of heart disease still occurs," says Jakub Morze, lead author and a postdoctoral fellow at Chalmers University of Technology, in Sweden.

Berdasarkan laporan, cholesterol is a substance similar to fat that circulates in the bloodstream. The body needs it to build cells and manufacture certain vitamins and hormones. Problems can arise when too much cholesterol accumulates in blood vessel walls, creating deposits called plaques.

Berdasarkan laporan, these plaques can narrow arteries and interfere with blood flow. If a plaque ruptures, a blood clot may form quickly and completely obstruct the affected vessel, potentially triggering a heart attack or stroke.

Diungkapkan bahwa because cholesterol and other fats cannot travel through the blood on their own, they are transported by specialized particles known as lipoproteins. When too many of these particles circulate in the blood, they can deliver excess cholesterol into artery walls. The cholesterol they carry is commonly referred to as "bad cholesterol. Three major classes of these particles contain a surface protein called apolipoprotein B (apoB). ".

Diungkapkan bahwa to investigate these unanswered questions, the scientists used proteomics analysis to examine how three types of fat-carrying particles (ldl, trl and lp(a)) affect the body and may contribute to heart disease. This approach allowed the team to investigate biological changes associated with the particles rather than focusing exclusively on the cholesterol they carry.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, all three types can contribute to cholesterol deposits inside artery walls, although ldl, which stands for low-density lipoprotein, is the most common. In a previous study, the same research group found that counting harmful lipoprotein particles was the most effective way to predict future heart disease risk.

Diungkapkan bahwa the researchers also identified two particularly important contributors beyond ldl: triglyceride-rich lipoproteins, or trl, and lipoprotein(a), known as lp(a). Their earlier findings suggested that each of these particles poses a greater risk individually than an LDL particle. As a result, TRL and Lp(a) are considered major contributors to the cardiovascular danger that can persist even after LDL cholesterol has been successfully reduced.

Proteomics is the systematic, large-scale examination and measurement of proteins within cells, tissues, or body fluids at a particular point in time.

Sebagaimana diketahui, while genomics investigates a person's relatively stable dna, proteomics focuses on proteins, which are constantly responding to changes inside the body. These molecules help construct tissues, process food, transmit hormonal messages, and defend against infections.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, because protein patterns shift in response to factors such as diet, stress, aging, and disease, analyzing them can provide a snapshot of current biological activity. Proteomics can help researchers identify biomarkers, diagnose medical conditions, and track how patients respond to treatment.

Blood Proteins Reveal Hidden Heart Disease Risks.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the new investigation focused on proteins, which perform countless essential functions throughout the body. Unlike genetic information, which remains largely unchanged, protein levels and activity can respond to diet, stress, aging, and illness. Studying these changes can therefore provide valuable insights into the body's current biological condition.

Berdasarkan laporan, researchers analyzed measurements of nearly 3,000 proteins found in blood samples and compared the results with genetic information and long-term health records. This combination helped them identify protein patterns associated with different lipoprotein particles and provided clues about how those particles might contribute to damage inside the arteries.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one of the most striking discoveries involved trl and lp(a). Although these are distinct types of particles, their associated blood protein patterns showed substantial similarities. Those overlapping patterns also appeared to be linked to the later development of heart disease.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the researchers found that these particles carried proteins capable of attracting immune cells, potentially encouraging inflammation and changes in the structure of blood vessel walls. This suggests that TRL and Lp(a) may contribute to cardiovascular disease through some of the same biological processes, rather than simply depositing cholesterol in the arteries.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ldl showed a different pattern. Its associated proteins were primarily connected to cholesterol accumulation in artery walls, highlighting an important distinction between the ways these three types of particles may contribute to heart disease.

Berdasarkan laporan, "the overlap for trl and lp(a) is one of the most interesting findings," says morze. This could help identify targets for more precisely directed prevention in the future. "It suggests that these particles may affect some of the same inflammatory and vascular processes. ".

How LDL, TRL, and Lp(a) Affect Heart Health.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the three types of lipoproteins examined in the study, ldl, trl, and lp(a), transport different amounts of cholesterol and other fats through the bloodstream. Each contains the structural protein apolipoprotein B, or apoB.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, all three can contribute to atherosclerosis, a condition in which fatty material accumulates inside blood vessel walls. As these deposits develop, they increase the risk of coronary heart disease.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ldl: low-density lipoprotein transports most of the cholesterol circulating in the blood. An LDL cholesterol measurement indicates how much cholesterol is contained within these particles.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, trl: triglyceride-rich lipoproteins transport cholesterol along with triglycerides, which the body uses as an important energy source. As triglycerides are removed from these particles, the remaining fragments can deposit cholesterol inside artery walls. In this study, the TRL measurements primarily reflected liver-produced particles called VLDL and the remnants they leave behind.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, lp(a): lipoprotein(a) resembles an ldl particle but contains an additional protein known as apolipoprotein(a). Higher levels of Lp(a) are already recognized as an established risk factor for coronary heart disease.

Could the Discovery Lead to Better Heart Disease Prevention?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, by identifying biological pathways associated with cardiovascular risk beyond ldl cholesterol, the findings offer researchers new possibilities for developing more personalized prevention strategies. In particular, the shared inflammatory and blood vessel effects linked to TRL and Lp(a) could become promising areas for further investigation.

Berdasarkan laporan, however, the research did not evaluate a new treatment or establish a blood protein test ready for routine clinical use. Additional studies will be needed to determine whether measuring these biological processes, or developing treatments that target them, can improve protection against heart disease.

Diungkapkan bahwa "lowering ldl cholesterol remains a cornerstone of prevention," says clemens wittenbecher, who led the study and is assistant professor of precision medicine and diagnostics at chalmers. "Our findings point to biological processes that may help explain some of the risk that remains beyond LDL. The next step is to establish whether measuring or targeting these processes can improve prevention alongside existing treatments. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, the results reinforce the importance of controlling ldl cholesterol while revealing why cholesterol reduction alone may not address every source of cardiovascular risk. Understanding the additional ways blood particles affect arteries could ultimately help scientists develop more precise approaches to protecting heart health.

The study, "Apolipoprotein B-containing lipoproteins: distinct roles in atherosclerosis revealed by plasma proteomic profiling," was published in the European Heart Journal.

#193. Paper Tiger review: Adam Driver, Miles Teller, and Scarlett Johansson enter a tense love triangle

📅 13 Nov 2026

Paper Tiger review: Adam Driver, Miles Teller, and Scarlett Johansson enter a tense love triangle

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://mashable.com/entertainment/paper-tiger-review

Berdasarkan laporan, marriage story stars adam driver and scarlett johansson reunite in writer/director james gray's paper tiger. But don't expect a desperate rehash of Noah Baumbach's divorce drama.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for one thing, gray is a filmmaker less drawn to such wall-punching theatrics, as evident through films like two lovers, ad astra, and armageddon time. For another, Driver and Johansson are not lovers in this film, though they are in a love triangle of sorts, with Miles Teller at the center.

Diungkapkan bahwa gray gives driver, johansson, and teller some unexpected roles, allowing each a place to display their range. But make no mistake, this is Driver's movie.

Berdasarkan laporan, set in 1986 new york city, paper tiger unfurls the story of a jewish family from queens that gets on the wrong side of the russian mob. In a cozy home in Elmhurst, Irwin Pearl (Teller) raises his two sons, Benjamin (Roman Engel) and Scott (Gavin Goudey), with his dedicated housewife Linda (Johansson).

Diungkapkan bahwa far from the cocky persona teller forged through performances in the spectacular now, whiplash, and the divergent film series, the 39-year-old actor now oozes doofy dad energy. Teller's signature smirk is swapped for an aw-shucks smile, and a patronizing eyebrow raise that insists, "Father knows best. " A pair of oversized eyeglasses completes the look; it's is such an evocative detail of the era that the title card reading "1986" might be deemed egregious.

Diungkapkan bahwa as irwin, teller is guileless, relishing every chance to play with his boys or annoy them with dad jokes. Still, he yearns for their respect, and wilts when his eldest huffs they only have "crappy" stuff because Irwin, an educated engineer, isn't bringing home bank like their uncle, Gary (Driver).

Diungkapkan bahwa a former nypd officer turned security consultant with city hall connections, gary pearl is flashy, rich, and successful in a way his younger brother can only envy. He wears tailored suits and a debonair smile. He drives a luxury car, and brings Peter Luger Steak House takeout to family dinner. So, when Gary promises Irwin a business opportunity to make $10,000, his brother is practically drooling at the possibility.

Berdasarkan laporan, gary wants to create a consulting firm with irwin that would advise russian immigrants who own property alongside the gowanus canal on how to meet the city's building codes. The elder brother insists this legit business shouldn't run them afoul of the Russian mob, but an overeager Irwin makes a misstep that puts all of the Pearls at risk.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, at first, irwin seems the protagonist of paper tiger, but gray's clever script steadily shifts focus to gary and linda. Once Irwin has earned the ire of the Russian mafia, it's up to his brother and wife to fix it, because this family man with zero street smarts is incapable. And in this battle to protect Irwin (and the rest of his household), Gary and Linda become unexpected rivals, in part because they deal with Irwin the same way.

Berdasarkan laporan, paper tiger becomes a story about the things we can't say to the person we love. For Gary, he tries to maintain a breezy exterior, promising Irwin he'll work it out with the mob. But in the meantime, thugs creep into the Pearl home and intimidate them by taking Polaroids of the parents and boys, defenseless in their beds. Whether because we don't want to hurt them or we want to protect them, some truths are just too terrible to utter. It's only when Irwin finds these pictures that he finally admits to Linda what's going on.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, she's understandably furious, but she's got a big secret of her own: a fatal diagnosis she can't bring herself to share. With the mob threatening his life, Gary and Linda are in a similar situation: with an uncertain amount of time left to set Irwin up so he and the boys will be okay. But wife and brother are not allies, and so their paths lead in different directions, while Irwin spirals in impotent plans of his own.

The tragedy of the film is not so much what happens to Irwin's family, but that — as smart as he is — he can't see the troubles mounting before his very eyes.

Diungkapkan bahwa gray's ensemble overall is strong. But Driver dominates the film, committing body and soul. When he reprimands his onscreen brother with love and radiant frustration, he evokes Al Pacino's Michael Corleone, specifically when he kisses the traitor Fredo. The swagger he employs as Gary schmoozes cops and crooks alike is beguiling, recalling James Caan as Sonny Corleone in The Godfather. But in moments when that veneer cracks, Driver's fear is so sparking the screen itself might catch fire. The masculinity and the heartache swell to a violent expression of love.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but gary isn't as direct as michael, and so irwin gets to remain smugly self-righteous, unable to recognize his brother's sacrifices for him. The bravado that carved his career at the start comes into play in the third act as a shield that Irwin carries to distance himself from his own failings. Teller is smartly cast in this role. He is a beloved fool whose smile shocks the audience, because it displays his blissful ignorance.

Diungkapkan bahwa playing the desperate and dying housewife linda, johansson is urged by gray to go into a space of melodrama the cool blonde has rarely tread. Big bouncy curls, thick eyeglasses, and a raspy Queens accent attempt to scrub the movie star glamour from Johansson's appearance. That might have more firmly grounded the Pearl family's blue-collar identity, and by extension, Linda's grit-teeth determination to secure their future. As weary and mumsy as the costuming of housecoats and made-up eye bags tries to make her, the role of Linda might have been better realized by an actress with a mug, not the face of numerous luxury beauty brands. But it is a futile effort. Johansson tries, but her ache and ire ring hollow.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, driver's performance recalls '70s gangster cinema, where toxic masculinity roared with a debonair allure. Teller's jolly blend of ego and ignorance makes his '80s dad a believable buffoon. But Johansson's (perhaps impossible to dim) glamour makes Linda feel like she's from a '50s melodrama, so beautiful and so sad! In this context, as grounded as she aims to make Linda, it still feels heightened, a performance of wifely limitations rather than a portrait of them.

Sebagaimana diketahui, still, even with this tonal collision, paper tiger is a thoroughly engaging drama. So, with each moment, in words spoken and unspoken, a labyrinth is built, daring the characters to escape it. Gray's dialogue shrewdly builds not only characters, but the barriers of what they can and won't share with each other. Like Conclave, Paper Tiger becomes as much about what's talked around as what's talked about. And rather than calling us to relate to Irwin, the good guy and family man at the film's center, Gray urges us to share in the frustration of those who love him until the bitter end.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in this way, paper tiger is a uniquely thrilling and purposefully infuriating family drama. Because as we watch a final moment unfold that is undeniably sweet and tender, we are haunted by what lies beneath it. Gray challenges us to take that trembling awareness home, and look to our own families, lives, and lies.

Diungkapkan bahwa paper tiger was reviewed out of the new york film festival, where it was the opening night selection. 13. The film will open in theaters on Nov.
