#195. Cosm rides premium moviegoing wave with more immersive screenings and a wider library

📅 07 Nov 2026

Cosm rides premium moviegoing wave with more immersive screenings and a wider library

Tanggal: 07 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/07/cosm-immersive-movie-screenings.html

The next big thing in premium large format theatrical viewing takes inspiration from the stars.

Sebagaimana diketahui, cosm, an immersive entertainment technology company, got its start programming planetariums — its name a combination of "cosmos" and "colosseum. " The company's massive, domed screens first offered guests a view of the universe, now they mimic courtside seats at sports venues around the world and drop film fans into some of Hollywood's most iconic sets.

Diungkapkan bahwa at a time when the theatrical industry is seeing its biggest growth from the sale of premium large format, or plf, tickets, cosm seeks to offer a fresh take on an elevated viewing experience. And it's quickly expanding both its footprint and its content library.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, since 2024, cosm has opened four theaters — near los angeles, dallas, atlanta and detroit — with a cleveland hub set to open in 2027. These experimental venues have garnered the attention of sports fans, screening live matchups in an arena-like environment. Showings often sell out, according to Cosm.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, more recently, cosm has partnered with hollywood studios like warner bros. , now a part of Skydance, to bring the likes of "The Matrix," "Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory," "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" and "It" to its locations. Cosm recently signed a deal with Universal, which will bring "Shrek" to its domes in December.

The agreements mark a lucrative new chapter for the privately held Cosm, expanding its audience reach and viewing opportunities beyond timed, live events.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as a privately held company, cosm doesn't disclose its financials. Tickets cost anywhere from $18 for a matinee to around $70 for prime seats or in-demand showings. That doesn't include added fees for concessions or items from special, themed menus tied to screenings.

Sony invested $100 million in the company in June, taking a minority stake and placing Sony Pictures Entertainment Chairman and CEO Ravi Ahuja onto its board of directors.

Cosm also counts among its investors Cosm chairman Steve Winn's firm, Mirasol Capital; former Milwaukee Bucks co-owner Marc Lasry's Avenue Sports Fund; Rocket Mortgage co-founder Dan Gilbert's Rock; and David Blitzer, managing partner of the New Jersey Devils and Philadelphia 76ers, who invested through his firm Bolt Ventures.

Berdasarkan laporan, "cosm is really early in its growth trajectory at the moment, and we saw an opportunity to partner with the company at, what i would say is at, a very important stage in its development," jay levine, chief strategy and business operations officer at sony, told cnbc. And the real reason why we did it was it gave us a lot of exposure to a growing distribution and what we deem an experiential platform that we think has long-term potential. "They have about five locations with the goal of a pretty significant rollout. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, sony has made several plays in the theatrical space in recent years. It bought Alamo Drafthouse in 2024 and entered a long-term lease to reopen and restore the iconic Cinerama Dome in Los Angeles in July of this year.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "our experiences strategy is around tech, it's around fandom, and it's around new and innovative approaches to content distribution," levine said. "For us, we're all about these differentiated experiences. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, cosm's 87-foot-diameter, concave screens drop viewers into the middle of the action, whether it's an nfl game or inside the world of "the matrix. " The company's forthcoming Cleveland location will have an even bigger dome, at 100 feet in diameter.

The experience is akin to that of the Sphere in Las Vegas, which has garnered headlines since opening in 2023 for hosting high-profile concerts and events.

Diungkapkan bahwa "people absolutely love to live out what they love in fandom, just like wearing a sports jersey," alexis scalice, head of cosm studios, told cnbc. "And I love that I'm seeing that same behavior happen with cinema. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa stadium-style seating is nestled within each cosm dome, with booths and tables set on each level. The dome's width is such that it fills much of the viewer's periphery, giving the sensation that they are part of the on-screen environment.

Diungkapkan bahwa the los angeles and dallas locations have capacity for around 350 seats each, while the newer domes in atlanta and detroit have up to 500 available seats. Cosm has not shared how many seats the Cleveland location will have, but with its larger screen it is expected to have a larger number of seats.

For live sports events, Cosm has specialty cameras mounted in arenas that broadcast back to the dome, creating the illusion of being on the field of play.

For theatrical features, the film is played in a large rectangle in the center of the dome and the background is transformed to extend the scene.

In Cosm's presentation of "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone," for example, during the iconic scene where thousands of Hogwarts acceptance letters flood through the fireplace and into a living room, the background is swarmed with animated envelopes.

Diungkapkan bahwa cosm has partnered with experiential production company little cinema and creative studio makemake to create the visuals and environments for each scene of a film released in the dome. From storyboarding to post-production, this process can take up to a year as Cosm, the participating studio and the visual effects artists craft and render each moment.

Berdasarkan laporan, "we really work hard not to take away from the story, so the film remains the hero in the narrative," scalice said. and our creative partners to make sure that we're not detracting too much from the story, but we're enhancing those moments for more elevated emotional response. "Working very closely with Warner Bros. ".

With the exception of "It," which was released in 2017, Cosm's theatrical offerings thus far have been films that were released decades ago and that typically have long-established fan bases.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that helps cosm leverage what scalice called "that nostalgia factor" — "parents coming in that. grew up on this, and they want to share it with their children. ".

"We can reinvigorate these legendary films," she added.

Berdasarkan laporan, cosm has dabbled across genres — horror, fantasy, science fiction — and also demographics — family-friendly and r-rated. "Shrek," set to debut Dec. 16, will be its first foray into animation.

"The thing that's so incredible about it is everybody thought initially it's just going to be working for sports, and when you look at what they've done, a lot of the titles with 'Harry Potter,' with 'Shrek,' and some of the other ones, I mean, the fill rates are actually incredible," Sony's Levine said.

Studios and theatrical exhibitors alike are looking for innovative ways to showcase Hollywood's product to moviegoers, especially as major shifts in viewing habits have disrupted the business.

In the post-pandemic era, the cinema space has been defined by fewer screens and fewer moviegoers, but those declines have been masked by higher movie ticket prices, particularly for PLF experiences.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, these elevated offerings — think imax, dolby cinema, screenx and 4dx — have bigger screens and better sound or introduce a unique experience, such as moving seats and fog machines. They're particularly popular with Gen Z and millennials, who've yet to be deterred by rising average ticket prices.

While an average standard movie ticket costs around $13, premium tickets average more than $18 each, according to data from EntTelligence.

Sebagaimana diketahui, prices for cosm's events fluctuate based on showtime and venue. Sony's Levine said the company's ticket prices and attendance rates are "higher than I think anybody really would have thought. ".

Unlike Cosm's sports offerings, which can also be viewed from outside the dome from its hall and deck viewing areas at a lower price, theatrical presentations are only available in the dome.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "they have no problem selling these tickets because people want to experience these things, like an immersive format," said mike polydoros, ceo at cinema marketing firm paperairplane media. "That is something they can't get at home. ".

#196. The mystery of how hair knows where to grow may finally be solved

📅 11 Nov 2026

The mystery of how hair knows where to grow may finally be solved

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261109205413.htm

Diungkapkan bahwa long before a mammal is born, its skin begins establishing the precise locations where hair will eventually grow. These developing hair follicles form intricate geometric arrangements that differ from species to species. But what determines where each follicle appears, and how does the body create such orderly patterns?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, researchers at the university of geneva (unige) have identified a surprisingly simple process that may help explain this biological mystery. By studying how cells move in response to chemical signals, the team developed a model that successfully recreates the formation of hair follicle patterns in two mammalian species. Their findings, published in PNAS, suggest that elaborate biological structures can emerge naturally from basic interactions between neighboring cells.

Diungkapkan bahwa the discovery could help explain a much broader phenomenon in nature. Hair, feathers, and most types of scales begin as small structures called placodes that appear during embryonic development. Scientists have spent decades investigating how these early structures establish the distinctive arrangements seen across different animal species.

Challenging a Long-Standing Theory of Hair Growth.

Diungkapkan bahwa for laboratory mice (mus musculus), the leading explanation has traditionally been the expansion-induction model. This theory proposes that when a new placode appears, it releases a chemical that prevents additional placodes from developing too close to it.

Berdasarkan laporan, as the embryo's skin grows and stretches, some areas move far enough away from existing placodes to escape the chemical's influence. New placodes can then develop in those spaces, gradually creating a more complete pattern across the skin.

Although this explanation has gained widespread acceptance, scientists have not experimentally established that it can account for the diversity of follicle patterns found across species.

A Simpler Mechanism for Hair Follicle Formation.

To investigate another possibility, researchers led by Athanasia Tzika, Senior Lecturer, and Michel Milinkovitch, Professor, both in the Department of Genetics and Evolution at UNIGE's Faculty of Science, focused on a process called chemotaxis.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, chemotaxis occurs when cells move in response to differences in chemical concentrations. The same basic process helps guide white blood cells toward areas of inflammation, allowing the immune system to respond where it is needed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the researchers created a mathematical model that tracks how mobile cells in the dermis interact with an attracting chemical signal released by the epidermis, the skin's outer layer. They then simulated the growth of embryonic skin to see whether these interactions could produce the gradual appearance of placodes.

Berdasarkan laporan, remarkably, the model recreated the developmental patterns observed in laboratory mice, including the same sequence of follicle formation that scientists had previously explained using the expansion-induction theory. This suggests that a complex system of instructions may not be necessary to determine where follicles develop.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "our findings show that the observed patterns do not require a complex system telling each placode where to form," explain muhamet ibrahimi and ebrahim jahanbakhsh, researchers in the department of genetics and evolution. "Instead, placodes emerge spontaneously from local interactions between cells and chemical signals. ".

One Simple Process Creates Different Hair Patterns.

The team next investigated whether the same mechanism could explain follicle arrangements in another mammal with a very different coat structure.

Sebagaimana diketahui, they selected the spiny mouse (acomys dimidiatus), a rodent whose hair follicles develop in an unusually regular pattern with a strong directional alignment. This distinctive organization cannot be explained by the traditional expansion-induction model.

Using experimental information gathered from three-dimensional images of developing embryonic skin, the researchers adapted their simulations to reflect the spiny mouse's particular biochemical characteristics and the way its skin grows.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the results showed that the same underlying process of cells responding to chemical signals could also reproduce the spiny mouse's highly organized follicle pattern. The differences between the two species could be explained by variations in their cellular interactions, chemical properties, and skin growth rather than entirely different mechanisms.

Berdasarkan laporan, these findings suggest that the remarkable variety of structures found throughout the animal kingdom may arise from a shared set of relatively simple biological rules. By adjusting how cells interact and respond to their surroundings, nature can generate dramatically different patterns without requiring a separate developmental blueprint for every species.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "our work suggests that simple cellular interactions can generate the remarkable diversity of tissue architectures observed throughout evolution," concludes athanasia tzika. "The differences observed between species therefore result from the same self-organization process, but with variations in the interactions between cells and chemical signals. ".

#198. T-Mobile illegally imposed 50GB cap on low-income home Internet plan, NY says

📅 11 Nov 2026

T-Mobile illegally imposed 50GB cap on low-income home Internet plan, NY says

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/11/t-mobile-illegally-imposed-50-gb-cap-on-low-income-home-internet-plan-ny-says/

Sebagaimana diketahui, law requires 25mbps home internet. T-Mobile lowers speed to 600Kbps after 50GB cap.

T-Mobile violated a New York state law by imposing a 50GB-per-month data cap and reducing speeds to less than a megabit per second on home Internet plans it is required to offer people with low incomes, New York government officials alleged.

Sebagaimana diketahui, t-mobile agreed to a settlement requiring it to scrap the data and speed limits, to offer the required low-income plans to more parts of the state, and to make it easier for customers to find information about the plans. The settlement requires T-Mobile to eliminate the speed limits and expand availability of the plans within 120 days.

Berdasarkan laporan, the alleged legal violation and the settlement are related to t-mobile’s wireless home internet service, not the company’s mobile plans. Governor Kathy Hochul and New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the settlement on Monday, saying that a state investigation found T-Mobile violated the New York Affordable Broadband Act (ABA).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the state law doesn’t specifically mention data caps, but it requires home internet providers with at least 20,000 customers to offer plans at specific prices and minimum speeds to people who meet income-eligibility requirements. T-Mobile’s policy of reducing speeds after customers exceed a monthly data cap violates the law, New York officials said.

“An investigation by the Office of the Attorney General (OAG) found T-Mobile’s offerings did not meet the ABA’s requirements, which mandate that home Internet providers offer high-speed broadband to income-eligible households for $15 per month at speeds of at least 25 Mbps, or $20 per month for speeds of at least 200 Mbps,” the press release said.

Berdasarkan laporan, new york says in the settlement with t-mobile that “after the data cap is reached, the customer’s maximum download speed is reduced from 25 mbps to 600 kbps. ” New York’s press release said “a typical customer could hit the data cap after about four days of usage. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, data caps and speed limits aren’t the only restrictions. T-Mobile also “only offers ABA Internet plans to customers in homes that are eligible for 5G home Internet,” preventing residents in 4G-only areas from accessing the plans, the settlement says. The company also prevented search engines from indexing the webpage that provides detailed information about eligibility for and enrollment in ABA plans, it says.

“T-Mobile did not fully comply with the New York Affordable Broadband Act,” New York said in the settlement.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, t-mobile’s aba webpage confirms that customers are provided only 50gb per month and that speeds after using the allotment are merely “up to 600 kbps. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, although the settlement includes a list of the new york ag’s findings, t-mobile did not admit to any violation. “Respondent neither admits nor denies the OAG’s Finding in paragraph 1-14 above,” the document says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, new york started enforcing the affordable broadband act in january 2025 after winning a nearly four-year court battle against broadband industry lobby groups that tried to kill the law. The groups that sued New York in a failed effort to block the law included CTIA, the wireless industry association that represents T-Mobile and other carriers. The law finally took effect a month after the Supreme Court rejected the broadband industry’s challenge.

When contacted by Ars, T-Mobile did not explain why it imposed the restrictions on low-income plans.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we have a long history of helping customers in new york stay connected through low-cost broadband, and we’re updating our plan to meet the state’s requirements while maintaining the same low price,” t-mobile said in a statement. “We’ve reached an agreement with the New York attorney general that builds on that commitment, provides greater clarity around our offering and makes the plan available to more eligible customers. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the settlement with new york applies to t-mobile’s fixed wireless internet plans, which can be used for home internet service as an alternative to wired broadband. The fixed wireless Internet relies on T-Mobile’s cellular network but provides access at a single location, delivering wireless signals to receivers installed at customer homes.

Berdasarkan laporan, it took almost 18 months for new york to investigate t-mobile’s compliance and reach a settlement with the company. “In June 2025, the New York Department of Public Service contacted the OAG and relayed concerns about certain features of the plan that T-Mobile was offering to customers eligible for reduced-price Internet service under the ABA,” the settlement said.

Diungkapkan bahwa it seems that isps have generally offered the required plans, though cable company optimum failed to comply until ars made some inquiries on behalf of a customer who could not obtain the plan he was entitled to shortly after the law took effect. ISPs knew about the law long in advance due to the multiyear court case that they initiated, but Optimum wasn’t ready to comply with the requirement and rejected the low-income man’s request twice.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, new york officials said the ag’s office “found that t-mobile was only offering aba plans in areas where it had deployed 5g wireless service, even though it offered full-price internet plans that could deliver 25 mbps download speeds in areas where it had 4g service. In addition, T-Mobile specifically coded its website to hide its ABA plan information from search engines, making it difficult for New Yorkers searching for low-priced Internet to find their plans. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the settlement requires t-mobile to stop intentionally limiting download speeds, and says the “temporary reduction of download speeds due solely to network congestion shall not constitute a violation of this assurance. ” There’s also an exception in the state law, which says ISPs shall provide 25Mbps “subject to exceptions adopted by the Public Service Commission where such download speed is not reasonably practicable. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, extending the low-cost service to 4g areas, t-mobile agreed to provide the low-income plans “at every address at which respondent offers residential fixed wireless internet service. ” Speeds lower than 25 Mbps would not violate the settlement if T-Mobile “would be unable to provide a minimum download speed of 25 megabits per second to a residential fixed wireless Internet service customer enrolled in a non-ABA Plan at the same address. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the document says that “t-mobile offers 5g home internet to roughly 40 percent of homes in rural areas of upstate new york and 4g (lte) home internet to the remainder of homes in the regions where t-mobile offers fixed wireless service. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa to make its aba webpage more accessible, the settlement says t-mobile “shall not include a noindex tag on the webpage, or otherwise prevent search engines from indexing the webpage or presenting a link to the webpage in response to search engine queries. ” T-Mobile must also prominently link to the ABA webpage on the part of its website that lists or describes its standard home Internet deals.

Berdasarkan laporan, new york could sue t-mobile if it violates the settlement. The ABA’s enforcement mechanism requires the attorney general to sue a broadband provider on behalf of residents. Such lawsuits can recover restitution and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation.

Berdasarkan laporan, isps that want to raise another challenge to new york’s law could get help from the trump administration, which asserts that states must not enforce price regulations or net neutrality laws against any isp that obtains grants from the $42 billion broadband equity, access, and deployment (bead) program. The grants have not been distributed yet, and California argues that the Trump administration does not have authority to preempt such laws.

In addition to this week’s settlement, New York struck a deal with T-Mobile last month over the carrier violating its promise to never raise prices on certain mobile plans that came with a lifetime price guarantee.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a state investigation “found that from 2017 to 2019, t-mobile advertised ‘price guarantee plans’ to its 4g customers, promising to ‘never change the price you pay,’” the new york attorney general’s office said on october 20. “However, in 2024, T-Mobile changed course and began raising the price of these plans by approximately $5 per phone line. New Yorkers enrolled in approximately 252,957 of these Price Guarantee Plans saw their phone bills increase. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa t-mobile agreed to give affected customers several reimbursement options and a price lock until may 2029. The attorney general’s office estimated that the agreement would provide up to $38 million in value to customers affected by the price hikes. T-Mobile also agreed to pay the state a fine of $98,834. 75.

T-Mobile provided a statement on the price-hike settlement.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the $38 million cited in the press release is an estimate of potential benefits that a group of long-standing t-mobile customers may choose to take advantage of, not the amount in refunds or payments,” t-mobile said. “The agreement provides for approximately $98,000 paid to the state and a range of optional customer benefits. We’re glad to have this matter resolved and remain focused on delivering value to our customers. ”.

#201. NASA’s Parker Solar Probe discovers a hidden pattern in the Sun’s chaotic magnetic fields

📅 12 Nov 2026

NASA’s Parker Solar Probe discovers a hidden pattern in the Sun’s chaotic magnetic fields

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261109205411.htm

Berdasarkan laporan, turbulence is all around us, from milk swirling into a cup of coffee to powerful storms churning through the atmosphere and oceans. But turbulence also occurs throughout space, where it behaves in ways that scientists are still struggling to understand.

Berdasarkan laporan, unlike the air and water on earth, much of the matter in space consists of electrically charged particles in a state (known as the plasma state). These particles interact strongly with magnetic and electric fields, creating turbulence that is fundamentally different from what we experience on Earth. Space plasma is also so thinly spread that particles rarely collide with one another, making its behavior even more unusual.

Sebagaimana diketahui, scientists have long struggled to explain how turbulence develops under these conditions and how energy is distributed among its constantly changing fluctuations. Now, an international research team has uncovered a surprising clue: hidden within the seemingly random motion of space plasma is a distinct magnetic pattern that reverses direction at very small scales.

The discovery, published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, reveals a previously unobserved phenomenon that could improve our understanding of the solar wind and the turbulent conditions that influence space weather.

NASA's Parker Solar Probe Reveals a Hidden Magnetic Reversal.

Researchers from the Technische Universität Braunschweig and the University of Tokyo, working with Tohoku University, Kyushu University, Osaka University, and other international institutions, identified the phenomenon using observations from NASA's Parker Solar Probe.

The collaboration brought together scientists from ten countries, including researchers at the Institute of Theoretical Physics at Technische Universität Braunschweig.

Sebagaimana diketahui, by analyzing highly precise measurements of magnetic fields and particles, the team discovered that turbulent magnetic fields reverse their direction of rotation at a particular range of wavelengths. This marks the first direct observation of such a reversal in space turbulence.

Even more surprisingly, the reversal becomes more pronounced and shifts toward longer wavelengths as the solar wind travels farther from the Sun.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the change occurs at a critical boundary where the behavior of plasma shifts from the collective movement of a flowing fluid to the dynamics of individual particles. This connection suggests that the magnetic reversal may provide an important new way to understand how turbulence operates across different physical scales.

Finding Order in the Chaos of Space Turbulence.

Berdasarkan laporan, at larger scales, plasma moves much like a fluid. Swirling structures called vortices and electromagnetic waves create increasingly complex fluctuations, producing the turbulent conditions found throughout space.

Although these movements appear random, the researchers discovered that the rotation of the magnetic fields follows a consistent pattern.

Diungkapkan bahwa when viewed along a direction pointing outward from the sun, magnetic fields at larger scales tend to rotate counterclockwise. At much smaller scales, however, the preferred rotation switches to clockwise.

This reversal occurs precisely where plasma stops behaving primarily like a fluid and begins exhibiting behavior governed by individual particles.

The finding is particularly striking because it reveals a clear, organized feature within a system otherwise dominated by seemingly unpredictable fluctuations.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we see a clear structure in the spectrum, even though the turbulence represents unstructured motions," says dr. Masatomi Iizawa (TU Braunschweig), the study's first author.

Sebagaimana diketahui, dr. of Tokyo) emphasizes the broader importance of the discovery, stating, "The results are of great significance for both plasma physics and astrophysics. Yokoi (University. ".

Why the Discovery Matters for Solar Storms and Space Weather.

Although the magnetic reversal occurs at extremely small scales, understanding it could have far-reaching consequences for space physics.

Plasma turbulence is a major feature of many environments throughout the universe, including Earth's magnetosphere, the solar wind, regions affected by solar eruptions, interplanetary space, and the disks of material surrounding astronomical objects known as accretion disks.

It also influences the shock waves and clouds of magnetic material that travel through interplanetary space following eruptions on the Sun.

These disturbances can play an important role in geomagnetic storms, making plasma turbulence a critical factor in efforts to predict space weather.

Berdasarkan laporan, by showing how an organized magnetic pattern emerges as turbulent plasma transitions from fluid behavior to particle behavior, the new research provides an important piece of a longstanding physics puzzle. The findings could ultimately help scientists better understand the complex processes that govern the solar wind and improve the physical models used to forecast geomagnetic storms.

#205. 237-million-year-old fossils reveal a bizarre armored sea amphibian

📅 11 Nov 2026

237-million-year-old fossils reveal a bizarre armored sea amphibian

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261109205409.htm

Berdasarkan laporan, a remarkable fossil discovery in china has revealed an ancient amphibian that lived entirely in the ocean, something no amphibian alive today is known to do. The unusual animal, named Gerrothorax maritimus, had a broad, flattened body protected by bony armor and was roughly the size of a giant salamander. Researchers believe it spent much of its life on the seafloor, waiting to ambush passing prey.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the discovery comes from an international team at the university of california, davis, peking university, and the geological museum of guizhou. Their findings, published in Nature Ecology & Evolution, are based on two exceptionally well-preserved skeletons dating back nearly 237 million years to the Late Triassic period.

Both fossils were uncovered in China's Guizhou Province, in a region that was once submerged beneath an ancient ocean hundreds of miles from major landmasses.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "this area is part of an ecosystem that we've been looking at and trying to reconstruct," said study corresponding author ryosuke motani, a professor in the department of earth and planetary sciences at uc davis. "We've been mostly studying marine reptiles and the fish from this place, but now we also have this amphibian, and it's a sort of very unusual member of the lineage. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, the finding is especially surprising because amphibians are generally unable to survive in seawater. Among the more than 8,000 amphibian species living today, none are known to spend their entire lives in marine environments, and fewer than 2% have any ability to tolerate salt.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mammals, reptiles, and birds, by comparison, all include species that can live entirely at sea without relying on land for food or fresh water. Until this discovery, scientists had never identified convincing fossil evidence of an amphibian with the same ability.

A Giant Armored Amphibian Built for the Seafloor.

Because the two skeletons are so complete, researchers were able to piece together the animal's appearance and develop a clearer picture of how it lived.

Diungkapkan bahwa gerrothorax maritimus measured nearly three feet long, but its proportions were far different from those of a modern salamander. Rather than having a long, slender body, it was unusually broad and flattened, with a distinctive disc-shaped form.

Its body was also covered in thick bony armor, which may have helped protect it from large marine predators such as ichthyosaurs.

Berdasarkan laporan, "if you think about today's amphibians, this animal is unusual because it's big," motani said. "It's probably, body mass-wise, about the same as the giant salamander, but what's different is that giant salamanders are elongated whereas this animal is really chunky. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa the structure of its skull, together with its heavy armor, suggests that this ancient amphibian was an ambush predator. Instead of actively chasing its meals, it likely rested on the seafloor until an unsuspecting animal came within reach.

"They would probably just wait at the bottom and then when prey comes around, they would just suck it in," said Motani, who noted that the hunting strategy resembles that of the wobbegong, a type of carpet shark that lives near the seafloor and captures prey using suction.

How Could an Amphibian Survive in Salt Water?.

One of the biggest mysteries surrounding Gerrothorax maritimus is how it managed to survive in an environment that is hostile to nearly all modern amphibians.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the problem comes down largely to amphibian skin. Unlike the relatively waterproof skin of many other animals, amphibian skin allows water and gases to pass through it. This makes it useful for breathing and maintaining hydration, but also leaves amphibians especially vulnerable to the effects of salt water.

Diungkapkan bahwa "that skin is permeable, and that allows the animals to use it for multiple purposes," said motani. "They use it for respiration and water intake, so amphibians don't drink or breathe through the mouth because they can do both through the skin. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, as a result, modern amphibians generally depend on freshwater habitats or environments close to them. A few species have developed limited salt tolerance, including the crab-eating frog. Even these animals can lose weight when exposed to brackish water and must eventually return to freshwater to recover.

The ancient Gerrothorax maritimus, however, may have evolved a very different solution.

Diungkapkan bahwa researchers suggest that its extensive bony armor restricted the movement of water through its skin. This protective covering may have reduced its dependence on absorbing water directly through the skin, allowing the animal to take in seawater through its mouth instead.

Diungkapkan bahwa under this proposed mechanism, water would have been absorbed through the digestive tract, while the animal's gills could have helped eliminate excess salt. Gills are known to have been present in members of the Gerrothorax genus, giving the researchers reason to suspect that this species possessed a more fishlike approach to managing its salt balance.

Together, these adaptations may explain how an amphibian managed to occupy an ecological niche that remains inaccessible to its modern relatives.

Fossil Evidence Points to a Fully Marine Lifestyle.

The researchers also examined whether Gerrothorax maritimus truly lived in the ocean or whether its remains might have been transported there after death.

Several clues strongly favor a marine lifestyle.

Berdasarkan laporan, first, the skeletons were recovered from sediments deposited in a deep marine environment. Their remarkable completeness also provides important evidence about where the animals died.

Berdasarkan laporan, "carcasses at sea, unless they sink to the bottom right away, tend to dry out and lose limbs prior to sinking to the bottom," said motani. "But these animals had their fingers preserved, so that means they probably died near where they lived. ".

The preservation of such delicate skeletal structures suggests that the bodies were not carried long distances before reaching the seafloor.

To investigate further, the team analyzed the fossils' chemical composition, focusing on the relative abundance of different forms of strontium, known as isotopes.

The results closely matched the strontium isotope signatures expected in ocean water during the Late Triassic, providing another independent line of evidence that the animals inhabited a marine environment.

Taken together, the fossil preservation, geological setting, and chemical findings make a compelling case that Gerrothorax maritimus spent its life entirely at sea.

The discovery reveals an unexpected evolutionary path for amphibians, showing that at least one ancient species appears to have overcome the biological limitations that keep its living relatives largely confined to freshwater environments.

The research received funding from the National Natural Science Foundation of China.

#206. Anduril says its first satellite can see adversaries maneuver in orbital night

📅 11 Nov 2026

Anduril says its first satellite can see adversaries maneuver in orbital night

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://arstechnica.com/space/2026/11/anduril-demos-night-vision-sensor-for-tracking-satellites-in-darkness/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “what’s unique is it’s got a huge dynamic range. We can see things in full dark. ”.

Anduril Industries has announced the successful demonstration of a new satellite-based sensor designed to track other spacecraft that may be hiding their maneuvers in Earth’s shadow.

Funded with Anduril’s internal capital, the company’s oven-sized satellite launched on a SpaceX rideshare mission in July with a package of tech demo payloads: an edge-compute processor, a power-management system adaptable to different mission types, and a long-wave infrared space sensor capable of detecting other objects in orbit.

Berdasarkan laporan, anduril reported on the success of the tech demo mission tuesday. The company’s satellite, named Anduril-216, flies about 590 km (366 mi) above Earth, spending about one-third of each orbit in darkness. Anduril-216’s night passes allow its infrared imager to shine.

Diungkapkan bahwa “this is a unique sensor that allows us to take imagery in long-wave [infrared],” said gokul subramanian, anduril’s senior vice president of engineering. “What’s unique about that is it’s got a huge dynamic range. It has very low solar exclusion, so we’re blocked by the Sun very rarely, and we can see things in full dark. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the us military and a growing number of commercial data providers use a network of radars and optical sensors on the ground and in space to monitor satellite traffic. Anduril acquired one of the commercial satellite-tracking companies, ExoAnalytic Solutions, earlier this year. But there’s a gap in optical tracking as satellites fly in Earth’s shadow, so space traffic monitors could temporarily lose track of a spacecraft if it performs a maneuver in orbital night.

Diungkapkan bahwa the space force is charged with tracking satellites for two primary reasons. First, military commanders want to know if an adversary moves its satellite in a threatening manner. Second, the Space Force issues traffic alerts to global satellite operators if there’s a risk of a collision.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “right now, we don’t have ground sensors in our adversaries’ sovereign lands, and then in the eclipse period where we are relying heavily on visible sensors, the satellites that are not illuminated by the sun, we can’t see those,” said adam thurn, vice president and general manager of orbital systems at anduril. “With the long-wave infrared space sensor, we’re looking to close that gap. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, anduril’s long-wave infrared sensor works by detecting heat signatures from spacecraft, even in periods of eclipse. It provides a “unique capability for us to witness when an adversary or other resident space objects are maneuvering during those eclipse periods, where in the past we’ve been fairly blind,” Thurn said.

Diungkapkan bahwa in creating the infrared space sensor, engineers applied imaging technology anduril uses in its autonomous weapons for use in space. Anduril released a single image Tuesday from the sensor on Anduril-216 showing an infrared view of the Moon above Earth’s horizon. The Moon image offers just a taste of what the instrument can do, Thurn said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the long-wave infrared capability we have on orbit can do both unresolved and resolved imagery,” thurn said, suggesting anduril’s sensor could be used to inspect other satellites in orbit if it flies close enough. For now, Thurn said Anduril is focusing on optimizing its tracking sensor for low-Earth orbit, but it could be used in other orbits, and eventually in cislunar space near the Moon.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, apex space, a satellite-manufacturing startup, built the spacecraft platform for anduril-216. Subramanian said Anduril has no plans to start its own satellite production line. Instead, Anduril foresees buying third-party satellite platforms and integrating them with sensor and compute modules to perform a range of different missions in space.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “you’re seeing that today with anduril-216, where we started with a simple mission, which was how do we track satellites, especially in these eclipse periods where the us currently does not have the ability to maintain custody,” subramanian said. “And we designed a mission around that. ”.

The compute module on Anduril-216 is designed to fuse data from different kinds of sensors, such as infrared or visible imagers, and generate tracking solutions on its own, without intervention or analysis from the ground.

Sebagaimana diketahui, subramanian said anduril’s current focus is on acquiring space domain awareness data for sale to the us military, not selling entire satellites or sensors to the government. “At present, Anduril is not offering this system as a merchant supplier,” he said. “That could change in the future. ”.

After all, you don’t need to know everything, only what’s important.

#207. Where's the growth? Legacy automakers face a tougher 2027 as costs rise, market tightens

📅 06 Nov 2026

Where's the growth? Legacy automakers face a tougher 2027 as costs rise, market tightens

Tanggal: 06 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/06/automakers-rising-costs-flat-production-2027.html

DETROIT — There's a growing concern that the global automotive industry may be stuck in neutral, if not reverse, heading into 2027.

The auto industry — from the companies to their customers — has been surprisingly resilient this decade, but there are fears that rising costs, weaker vehicle pricing and a more challenging market could threaten profits and growth going forward.

Berdasarkan laporan, automakers also face pressure outside the u. S. from an onslaught of Chinese carmakers, a thinner new-product pipeline after retreating from some all-electric plans, and company- and region-specific challenges.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "with investor focus increasingly shifting to 2027, the setup appears challenging," barclays analyst dan levy said in an investor note last month. , and a flat global production outlook suggest another year of limited earnings growth. "Rising inflation, continued China pressure, affordability concerns in the U. S. ".

Several Wall Street analysts have said automakers will need continued pricing strength and additional cost savings to offset inflation, higher investment spending and a potentially weaker economy just to maintain their current levels.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "it's a little bit more optimistic in the u. S. and then very pessimistic in Europe," RBC Capital Markets analyst Tom Narayan told CNBC. "As a whole, there's some negativity on '27. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, automakers from the u. S. to Europe to Asia have been facing a growing list of headwinds.

Diungkapkan bahwa for u. S. -based legacy automakers, Ford Motor said it expects next year's results to be in line with 2026, while General Motors grew more cautious about its ability to continue growing earnings as much as it had previously expected.

Diungkapkan bahwa "we continue to believe that 2027 will be another strong year and better than 2026, assuming customer demand remains strong, and commodity, logistics and other recent cost pressures moderate," gm ceo mary barra told investors oct. 20.

Sebagaimana diketahui, gm cfo paul jacobson said that while it's too early to officially forecast, the company is facing additional inflationary costs that could lead to another $2 billion headwind in 2027, like it expects this year. He specifically cited costs of commodity inflation, logistics and DRAM, or dynamic random-access memory chips as challenges.

Those chips are critical components in modern vehicles and are used for everything from temporary data storage and real-time processing from infotainment systems to safety-critical systems.

Berdasarkan laporan, gm and others have been able to offset outside pressures through cost cuts, operational efficiencies and resilient consumer demand for higher-margin vehicles. However, there's a limit to what companies can do.

Berdasarkan laporan, "there's only so much pricing you can push to consumers," narayan said. "They're already at pretty high pricing. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, european automakers including volkswagen, mercedes-benz and bmw in recent weeks reduced their 2026 earnings forecasts in response to u. S. tariffs, the growth of Chinese automakers and rising costs.

Diungkapkan bahwa most recently, bmw this week said accelerated restructuring measures would reduce its automotive pretax earnings margin this year by 2. The company said the restructuring should support "positive effects" into 2027 and a 3% to 5% pretax profit margin for 2028. 5 percentage points. That compares with a 5. 3% automotive margin last year and 3. 4% during the third quarter.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, chrysler parent stellantis, which has large operations in europe and the u. S. , is facing its own challenges, as it's in the midst of a restructuring that aims for a low-single-digit adjusted operating margin this year. It has maintained a 2026 guidance that includes a mid-single-digit percentage increase in net revenue and a low-single-digit adjusted operating margin.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in asia, south korean automaker hyundai motor, which has experienced notable growth in recent years, also cut key metrics when it reported earnings late last month. 3% to 7. 5% and 6. 16 million, and cut its operating-margin target to between 5. The company lowered its 2026 wholesales target to 4 million vehicles, down from 4. 5%, down from a previous goal of 6. 3%.

Sebagaimana diketahui, toyota motor is an outlier for its most recent quarter and outlook, as the world's largest automaker increased its full-year operating income forecast by 500 billion japanese yen (about $3. 2 billion) on Thursday.

Diungkapkan bahwa toyota's results were boosted by weakness in the japanese yen as well as strong hybrid vehicle demand in the u. S. However, the increase in operating income was its first in six quarters.

Broadly, the changes to earnings and outlooks come as production for the global industry slows.

Berdasarkan laporan, consulting and insights firm globaldata expects global light-vehicle production of about 90. 96 million units in 2026, down 2. It forecast a production increase of less than 1% next year. 1% compared with last year. That comes on the heels of strong annual growth earlier this decade, led by China.

Berdasarkan laporan, cox automotive reported the average transaction price of a new u. S. vehicle in September was more than $50,500. That was just shy of the record of $50,614 in December 2025.

Lofty vehicle prices have led to record-high and record-long financing deals, as well as concerns that customers are getting priced out of the new-vehicle market.

Berdasarkan laporan, the typical u. S. new-vehicle payment reached $776 a month in September, the highest since December 2023, according to Cox Automotive.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, cox automotive chief economist jeremy robb, discussing the third quarter for the automotive industry, rated the overall economy, buyer ability and borrowing costs as cautionary "yellow lights. ".

But he did have some "green lights," such as good credit availability and employment conditions, which could give some relief for automakers and consumers, many of whom need vehicles for their everyday lives.

Robb said there's a "tug-of-war" between headwinds such as rising costs, interest rates and fuel prices and tailwinds such as growth in liquid assets and savings that has helped offset some of the additional costs.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "consumers remain under financial pressure, but the vehicle demand continues to hold, showing more resiliency in the auto industry than we've seen in other parts of the economy," robb said during a sept. 24 call, noting consumer sentiment remains low.

#208. Bitter Christmas review: Pedro Almodóvar returns with a cerebral, semi-autobiographical drama

📅 13 Nov 2026

Bitter Christmas review: Pedro Almodóvar returns with a cerebral, semi-autobiographical drama

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://mashable.com/entertainment/bitter-christmas-review

Sebagaimana diketahui, storied spanish filmmaker pedro almodóvar has built his career on melodramas rich in sex and agony. However, in 2019, he got more personal with Pain and Glory, a semi-autobiographical drama in which Antonio Banderas plays a thinly veiled version of the director as he looks back on his work and life, anxious to move forward with a new project. His latest, Bitter Christmas, serves as a sister film, echoing not only the semi-autobiographical element but also by casting a dashing actor in the role of an aging Almodóvar.

Berdasarkan laporan, leonardo sbaraglia stars as raúl, a filmmaker who's hungry for inspiration for a new screenplay. There, a once-revered art-house filmmaker named Elsa (Bárbara Lennie) seeks to move away from directing commercials and return to screenwriting. In his corner are his much younger partner, Santi (Quim Gutiérrez), and his longtime manager, Mónica (Aitana Sánchez-Gijón). However, Bitter Christmas gets self-reflexive as Raúl's story is interwoven with that in his screenplay. Aside from their similar creative quest, both also have May-December romances with younger men, and both find inspiration for their new project in the tragedy that befalls a friend.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in two layers, almodóvar explores what it means to be an artist who may well cannibalize the stories of his loved ones for his art. But he doesn't lose sight of what it means to see your heartache treated as fertilizer to grow that art. In both Raúl's story and Elsa's, the writers are confronted by a female friend is radiantly furious at having her life treated as source material without consent.

So, how do these parallel stories play out?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, almodóvar, who wrote and directs bitter christmas, leaps back and forth between raúl and elsa, whose arcs play out in 2025 and 2004, respectively. Despite the decades between them, these worlds are visually similar, alive with the vivid color palettes that are part of Almodóvar's signature style.

Diungkapkan bahwa his characters are beautiful, always, and favor bold hues of red, magenta, gold, and amber. The production design around them is rich with the texture of lives lived: a book shelf thoughtfully organized but clearly oft-visited, a lamp shedding light on simple but elegant illustrations, a strip club for women that's a mix of chic and sleazy. Across both stories, we're invited to understand these people and their alter egos through such tender details.

Berdasarkan laporan, the ensemble cast strides into this world as if it is truly theirs. Determined close-up shots allow for every micro-expression to register, while wide shots remind us of how close these friends and lovers are, and yet how fragile the space between them can be.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sbaraglia is intriguing in the role of almodóvar's first mirror, raúl. Elsa, however, is a more typical Almodóvar figure — a strong-willed woman who won't be bent by the judgment of others. He speaks with passion, intelligence, and a low-burning frustration, which bursts whenever he's challenged. She is robust, defiant, and ruthlessly loyal to her art.

Berdasarkan laporan, by contrast, the boyfriends santi and bonifacio (patrick criado) are defined by their congeniality and sex appeal. But this feels intentional, as if Raúl simplifies his lover Santi into the himbo archetype of Bonifacio. Gutiérrez, playing the older of the two, gets to weave in more nuance than the Golden Retriever boyfriend Criado is given to play. But why? It's in these difference where Bitter Christmas becomes the most exciting for longtime Almodóvar fans.

Is the simplification of Santi meant to convince Raúl that their relationship is not so serious, so if and when it ends, his heartbreak will be lessened by anticipation? Or is the almost puppy-like sweetness and loyalty of Bonifacio meant as a quiet condemnation of Elsa's opportunism, as she treats him with little regard even as he bends over backwards to please her? Basically, are these boy toys not meant to be mocked, but to reflect Almodóvar's own insecurities through their guilelessness?.

However, it's Monica who becomes Bitter Christmas's most compelling character, and I'm not sure if that's intentional or not.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at first, she seems a supporting character who flutters around the sensitive artist, caring for all the chores, emails, and requests so he won't have to. But no sooner is her dedication defined that she's requesting a "sabbatical. " It's so unusual for this clear workaholic to request time off, much less a lot of time, and with little warning and no explanation, that Raúl is darkly enchanted.

Diungkapkan bahwa forged over decades, their professional and personal relationship is impossibly intertwined, so monica soon shares that her dear friend has suffered a horrendous personal loss. She is going to care for her (not terribly unlike Almodóvar's last film, The Room Next Door. ) However, no sooner has she divulged this painful truth than Raúl remolds it for his fiction. Both within his script and in his life, the filmmaker will have to face the friend betrayed in this specific way.

Diungkapkan bahwa when monica sits down with raúl in a garden cafe to lay into him about his selfishness in this creative endeavor, bitter christmas ignites. It's possible Almodóvar intended such restraint, but it makes Bitter Christmas feel almost as if the movie is holding its breath, waiting for something profound to hit. While much happens in the parallel stories, the energy of Elsa and Raúl feel subdued, as if they are always in their heads looking down on the situation instead of living fully within it. That comes when Monica argues for herself, her privacy, and her friend's dignity.

Berdasarkan laporan, however, no sooner does bitter christmas open up into something exciting than the film itself ends. There will be no satisfying resolution — perhaps until Almodóvar's next movie.

Diungkapkan bahwa at one point in the movie, raúl recognizes that even a minor work from him will be big to his fans. Regarded on its own, this film feels thin. And it seems almost a buffer for those who might critique Bitter Christmas. But Almodóvar devotees might well see it as a Rosetta stone to better understand the revered filmmaker and the whole of his body of work.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, bitter christmas was reviewed out of its north american premiere at the toronto international film festival. Nov. 13, before going nationwide Nov. A. The film will open in NYC and L. 25. #209. ‘Law & Order: SVU’ Goes Back to (Before) the Beginning With Its 600th Episode

📅 13 Nov 2026

‘Law & Order: SVU’ Goes Back to (Before) the Beginning With Its 600th Episode

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/law-and-order-svu-600th-episode-showrunner-interview-1236754391/

Showrunner Michele Fazekas breaks down Christopher Meloni's return and the state of the Benson-Stabler relationship.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, [this story contains spoilers from the 600th episode of law & order: svu. ].

Berdasarkan laporan, law & order: svu reached a huge milestone thursday: 600 episodes, a number that only two scripted primetime shows have ever hit before. Six hundred episodes is an extremely rare feat for a scripted series (The Simpsons and Gunsmoke are the only ones with more), but Thursday’s episode was also the sixth of season 28; 15 more are still to come. The cast and crew celebrated with a cake on set during filming and a dinner afterward — and then went back to work. Related Stories Business Fanatics Studios' Next Big Media Play Is the NBA All-Star Game TV Jason Benetti Will Replace Dan Hicks on Notre Dame Play-by-Play Saturday Following Sudden Passing (Exclusive).

Diungkapkan bahwa “that’s just doing television,” showrunner michele fazekas told the hollywood reporter. “It’s our 600th episode, but it’s also just an episode within 21 episodes [this season]. You’re working on five episodes at the same time at any given moment — you’re in prep on some episodes, you’re writing on some episodes, you’re in post on some episodes. Nothing changed in that regard. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, titled “obedience,” the 600th episode brings elliot stabler (christopher meloni) back to the special victims unit after jury consultant gwen sharpe (j. Smith-Cameron, who also appeared in the season premiere) convinces Benson (Mariska Hargitay) to take another look at an old case. Gwen is convinced the man in prison for the crime, the rape and murder of a young nun in 1998, is innocent.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, stabler is reluctant to revisit the case — with good reason, it turns out. He also cut Benson out of the interrogation in the case, which she went along with at the time because she was new to the squad. He failed to follow a couple of leads that could have pointed to the real culprit, a now-retired priest who led mass at the convent where the victim lived. The case stirs up complicated feelings in the former partners; when Stabler asks Benson why she’s so interested in digging up the case, she retorts, “Why aren’t you?”.

He eventually agrees to work with her, and the pair head upstate to question people who knew the victim (most notably, guest stars Laura Innes and Kathleen Chalfant) and track down the priest.

Sebagaimana diketahui, fazekas, who wrote the episode (brenna malloy directed), said she wanted to give the 600th show the feel of “an old school benson and stabler episode” while also looking at the people they have become in the years since. To that end, the episode’s final scenes will give viewers plenty to discuss.

Fazekas unpacked those scenes, the reasons for going back to the show’s early days and more in an interview with THR.

Given the milestone that this is, was there extra planning that went into it? Or did you have ideas on the board for longer than you might normally?.

Berdasarkan laporan, probably a little bit. I think I had an idea early on in the in the season of what I wished to do, and one of the first things was saying, “Can we bring back Chris Meloni?” Assuming that this is the last centennial episode that we were going to have, it feels like if we could do it, this would be the time to do it. So yeah, there were some earlier ideas than your typical running around trying to figure out what an episode is.

Having Stabler come back into the squad was always part of the plan, then?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it was for me. I also knew early on — because I was on the show the first time around, seasons three through seven — I wanted to kind of go back a little bit to an old school Benson and Stabler episode of SVU and honor that era of the show. But he was. ” I want them to be in a car, driving long distances and hashing stuff out. There were a lot of things that had to happen in order for that to become a reality, including Chris having to be available — he’s busy. I didn’t know what [the reason] was. I just had an idea, and I don’t usually come up with ideas this way, but I was like, “I want it to be a road show. I always find that interesting, just putting two people in a place where they can’t get away, and then they have to hash out their stuff.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the structure of svu is such that cases usually get cleared and some sort of justice is served by the end of the hour. I thought it was really interesting that this one is built on something that they got wrong initially. Why did you want to come at it that way?.

Berdasarkan laporan, in part, it was because you have to explain why are we bringing detective stabler back. So what would be big enough that he would come back? It felt sort of organic for it to be an old case, but it’s a case that actually predates the show. He doesn’t work in SVU anymore. He works in a completely different department. The show starts in 1999, and this case is from 1998.

Diungkapkan bahwa what was not planned but came out in the in the breaking of the story is they were such different people back then. It fits really nicely into what we’re doing with her character this season, and it made sense for why he’s back. Benson was really new, and Stabler was the senior detective, and she has evolved so much because, at the end of the day, we’re still telling the story of Benson. But it also goes to wanting to do and old school SVU episodes, but let’s go back to before SVU was even a thing.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i was also struck by stabler admitting to benson that his catholicism might have blinded him to who the real perpetrator was. His religion has been a thread throughout the character’s run, but I think it’s always interesting when it comes up explicitly in relation to a case.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, chris meloni was a big proponent of that as well. Anybody who was raised Catholic, you think of it as one thing, and it’s very hard for people to accept that this thing that you think is one way has a really dark side. I think allowing your own preconceptions biases you; it goes to that whole issue [of blind spots] generally. At that time [in 1998], it would have been really hard for Stabler to even understand.

Sebagaimana diketahui, you were on the show for a good portion of the benson-stabler partnership during your first tenure, and now you’re back as showrunner. What’s your read on their relationship?.

Berdasarkan laporan, my read is stabler still has work to do on himself that benson has done. I think Stabler is still working on it. Benson has evolved in a way, and I love them together, and I love them as partners and as scene partners. But I think part of this episode is talking about how she, in some ways, has moved on from the struggles back then. Stabler is still doing a lot of the same things that he did 20 years ago, and he’s starting to realize, oh, I need to change that.

And given what goes on between them in this episode — arguing about work and life, and then him inviting her to come to Arizona for a while — what do you think the audience’s read is going to be?.

Berdasarkan laporan, listen, i do think they love each other. I think when he says, “Hey, you want to come to Arizona?” he knows her answer is going to be no. I think they both know. Is there time down the line? Maybe, but I think he’s got some work to do. I don’t think he didn’t mean it, but he also knew what her answer was going to be, and I think now is not the time. It’s easy to ask that question when you know the answer is no. She can have some work to do as well, but I think she’s probably a little further down that path than he is.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i’ve always thought that they love each other in a way that sort of transcends a sexual relationship. They deeply love each other, and they’ve acknowledged that before, and I think this sort of reinforces it. But I also think he knows I’ve got more to do with myself.

Where are you in terms of production now?.

We are shooting episode 10 and in prep on episode 11.

Anything you can say about the next few episodes?.

Diungkapkan bahwa we have a nice little arc going of that we started at the beginning of the season that we continue, where the cases that they’re faced with are messy and don’t have easy answers. Benson is really struggling with feeling like nothing has changed. No matter how hard we work, sometimes it doesn’t matter. I like the idea of pushing her — the episode we’re shooting now and the next episode are pushing her to the edges of not even what is legal, but what is ethically and morally right to do, because she’s starting to not care.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the episode we’re shooting right now, the bad guy is so bad. We’re talking about “Why is he doing what he’s doing?” And she actually says, “I don’t care,” which is a big thing for her. But you also understand it because the guy is such a bad guy.

Anything you can say about how Stephanie March re-enters the show as Alex Cabot?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, benson goes to her and asks for help. They didn’t end things on a totally happy note the last time she was on the show, but Benson goes back to her.

Is Alex still doing the same sort of work she was that last time?.

#210. Silicon Valley Is Still Defending Jensen Huang

📅 12 Nov 2026

Silicon Valley Is Still Defending Jensen Huang

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/silicon-valley-is-still-defending-jensen-huang/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, news of jensen huang’s affair with an alleged asset of china’s ministry of state security was first met with a muted response in silicon valley—including inside nvidia itself. Huang’s resignation, after news of two other alleged romantic relationships with Nvidia staffers, has left both the company and the broader AI industry stunned.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as revelations about huang’s initial affair came out earlier this week, rank-and-file nvidia employees at first pursued business as usual, according to two current and three former employees at the chipmaker, speaking anonymously to protect relationships at the company. They trusted the board to investigate and act accordingly, but few workers thought Huang would actually leave.

Berdasarkan laporan, nvidia’s roughly 60,000 employees are loyal to the point that its global turnover rate is reportedly among the lowest in tech. Huang was the company’s soul and the founder who stuck with it through challenges for 33 years. Workers say they have heard it called having “green in your blood” or being “green-pilled” or on “team green,” referring to the company’s signature color. Employees appreciated that he kept layoffs rare and red tape sparing.

Berdasarkan laporan, “in just three days we went from superhero cape to ‘oops, i forgot my pants,’ and nobody’s quite sure how to swallow that,” one employee said. One former employee insisted in Huang’s defense that something “more sinister” must have been in play, and that affairs alone shouldn’t have led to his departure.

Berdasarkan laporan, huang’s peers in silicon valley echoed that sentiment, remaining vocal in their support of the embattled ceo even after his ouster. “One mistake does not erase a lifetime of leadership and contribution in building NVDA,” venture capitalist Antonio Gracias wrote on X earlier this week, using the company’s ticker symbol.

Berdasarkan laporan, the new york times reported on wednesday that huang has also had an extramarital affair with a vice president at nvidia, and reuters revealed on thursday a second “intimate relationship” with an employee. Before those alleged affairs became public, multiple industry executives told WIRED that Huang is “irreplaceable” and that his biggest mistake, aside from his relationship with Alice Huang, was admitting the affair in writing to the whole company.

Diungkapkan bahwa that appears to still be the prevailing sentiment. “A founder who has spent 30 years building such a unique company so capably has earned the presumption that he should keep leading it,” venture capitalist Sarah Guo wrote on X after Huang resigned, and a few hours before the Reuters report.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, authorities and nvidia’s board have yet to formally accuse huang of wrongdoing in his interactions with the businesswoman and suspected intelligence asset alice huang, and china has denied that she’s a spy. President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that the FBI “is looking into it. ” Nvidia’s board has stated that it doesn’t believe Huang compromised any secrets, but it has hired the law firm Wachtell Lipton to investigate.

Add to all that, some corners of Nvidia had already been whispering about the relationship with Alice Huang; one venture capitalist who declined to be named recalled a recent dinner where an Nvidia executive claimed there had been rumors about Jensen’s romantic relationship with a young Asian woman.

Diungkapkan bahwa on monday, the venture capitalist had estimated a “less than 10 percent” chance huang would lose his job at the top of the world’s most valuable company. “The wind’s going to blow over on this,” they said. “People are going to hate him for three months, and forget this ever happened. ”.

The big anxiety in Silicon Valley remains the possibility that instability at Nvidia will burst an AI bubble, but analysts aren’t so sure.

Berdasarkan laporan, the chief executive of one ai company, who spoke on condition of anonymity so as not to affect business relationships, says nvidia’s recent bankrolling of ai startups and even buying companies such as model-hosting provider hugging face has helped prop up the need for chips. A “new professional CEO won’t do any of that,” meaning “systemic risk for the AI trade and AI bubble increases substantially,” the entrepreneur says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, between bubble talk and huang rumors, nvidia shares in recent days have sunk to their lowest point in more than a year. Nvidia reports its latest quarterly earnings next week.

Inside Nvidia, meetings, projects, and the company’s aggressive culture are rapidly pressing ahead with what’s left of Huang’s vision.

#211. NASA’s CHAPEA Mars crew finally emerges after more than a year in isolation

📅 10 Nov 2026

NASA’s CHAPEA Mars crew finally emerges after more than a year in isolation

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261109205406.htm

After spending more than a year experiencing what life could be like on Mars, four NASA volunteers have finally stepped outside, marking the end of an ambitious experiment designed to prepare humans for future missions to the Red Planet.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the crew completed their simulated mars journey on october 31, 2026, emerging into the outside world for the first time in more than a year. Although the volunteers never actually left Earth, their extended mission recreated many of the challenges astronauts could encounter while living and working millions of miles from home.

The experiment was part of NASA's Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA) program, which investigates how people adapt to the demanding conditions of extended space exploration.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the four volunteers were matthew montgomery (left), james spicer (middle left), ross elder (middle right), and ellen ellis (right). Following the completion of their mission, the crew posed together outdoors, celebrating their return from a simulated journey to another planet.

Sebagaimana diketahui, throughout the experiment, the participants carried out tasks similar to those that future mars explorers may need to perform. These included operating and testing essential systems, caring for crops, conserving limited supplies, and conducting extravehicular activities.

Sebagaimana diketahui, extravehicular activities, often called spacewalks, are operations astronauts perform outside their spacecraft or habitat. In a Mars simulation, these activities help researchers examine how crews might prepare for and carry out work beyond the safety of their living quarters.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the volunteers also had to manage communication delays, an important challenge for anyone traveling to mars. Unlike astronauts aboard the International Space Station, who can communicate with Earth almost instantly, future Mars explorers will experience significant delays because radio signals take time to cross the enormous distance between the two planets.

Berdasarkan laporan, these delays mean astronauts cannot always depend on immediate guidance from mission control. They must be prepared to solve problems, make decisions, and manage unexpected situations with greater independence.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one of the biggest challenges of sending people to mars is keeping them healthy, productive, and safe during long periods away from earth. A crew must be able to manage food, equipment, living conditions, and daily responsibilities while working together in a confined environment.

Sebagaimana diketahui, nasa uses analog missions to explore these challenges before attempting actual journeys into deep space. An analog mission is a realistic simulation that reproduces selected conditions of space exploration while allowing scientists to study how people respond in a controlled setting on Earth.

The CHAPEA program provides an opportunity to investigate how astronauts might handle the practical demands of extended missions, including resource limitations, equipment maintenance, food production, and communication difficulties.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the lessons learned from montgomery, spicer, elder, and ellis will help nasa plan future human exploration missions. Their experiences are expected to inform the development of NASA's planned Moon Base and preparations for eventual crewed expeditions to Mars.

Although this crew's journey took place entirely on Earth, the knowledge gained could help address some of the challenges humans will face when they finally travel to the Red Planet.
