#214. Victorian Psycho review: What if Gothic horror were an eat-the-rich comedy?

📅 13 Nov 2026

Victorian Psycho review: What if Gothic horror were an eat-the-rich comedy?

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://mashable.com/entertainment/victorian-psycho-review

Gothic horror is going from mad to madcap with Victorian Psycho, a horror comedy that follows a murderous governess to her next — and possibly last — appointment.

Diungkapkan bahwa maika monroe stars as winifred notty, a governess who is desperate to make a good impression on her new employers, the pound family. At night, strange noises might be heard about their grand house. Members of the staff vanish without a word. The family's treasures go missing or are vandalized. Could it be a ghost or ghoul whose very presence could drive this poor heroine mad? Well, no. A seemingly fragile young woman must care for the young, defenseless children of a rich and twisted family. The broad strokes of the plotline are tropes of Gothic horror. Because from the very start, Victorian Psycho shows us its protagonist is already mad, and also the vicious thing that goes bump in the night.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the title alone gives some clue of the topsy-turvy approach that virginia feito, who wrote the novel and this adapted screenplay, has to the genre. Director Zachary Wigon (Sanctuary) cements this cheeky attitude with an opening scene in which Winifred addresses the audience in voiceover while looking straight into the camera. There's a sense of Fleabag in this distorted direct address to the audience, as Winifred insists she is the sanest person she's ever met.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this is just the first red flag, warning that winifred notty is much more than naughty. Soon after, a dismembered human ear tumbles out of her luggage; she regards it with slight irritation. From here, Victorian Psycho blooms into a deliciously bonkers spin on Gothic horror with an eat-the-rich edge.

Diungkapkan bahwa on the surface, winifred seems a darling young woman, eager to be accepted into a household that'll appreciate her. She's demure when meeting the servants of the Pound estate, as well as the family themselves. Among them, there is a mightily mustachioed father (Jason Isaacs), a fearsome mother (Ruth Wilson), teen daughter Drusilla (Evie Templeton), and the spoiled little heir to the family fortune, Andrew (Hamnet's Jacobi Jupe).

Want more film and TV news and reviews delivered straight to your inbox? Sign up for Mashable’s Top Stories newsletter or get Mashable push alerts today.

Berdasarkan laporan, but there's a spiky antisocial undercurrent to winifred, especially when she's left alone with the children. She swiftly befriends the children's nurse, Miss Lamb (Thomasin McKenzie), and offers to this wide-eyed waif tales of a ghoul that's prowling the property. She speaks of the wickedness and pain that lie inside all living things, frightening the young Master Andrew, who watches in shock as she bludgeons a fallen deer to death with a rock. Still, few around her could imagine what horrid secrets she's left behind her, and what deranged fantasies fuel her dark heart. For how else to explain the blood all over Winifred's dress?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, when it comes to winifred's violence, wigon is unblinking in brandishing spurts of blood but knows when to keep certain especially heinous homicides off-camera. This keeps the tone of Victorian Psycho thrillingly zany, despite the grim content.

Diungkapkan bahwa as for feito, she seems to pull inspiration from jane austen's brilliantly dummy dialogue for oblivious rich folk. The father bloviates about the value of phrenology, a pseudoscience that proposed personality could be predicted by skull shape. These are caricatures of entitled affluence. The mother punishes a scullery maid by chopping off the girl's long hair after a strand once ended up in her soup.

Sebagaimana diketahui, like with saltburn, there's a delicious lunacy to watching these careless rich assholes embrace an outsider who's sure to bring them to ruin. Not all of Winifred's targets feel as worthy of her brutal brand of comeuppance. Still, the breathtaking cruelty is part of the fucked-up thrill ride.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the american actress's career has been largely defined by horror since she broke through in 2014 with a supporting role in the gripping thriller the guest and then starred in the std-as-slasher allegory it follows. Though she's done a slew of films since then, horror offerings like Watcher, Longlegs, and The Hand That Rocks The Cradle stand out. Yet here, she's turned from haunted heroines of her filmography and Gothic horror in general to become a compelling monster all her own.

Berdasarkan laporan, typically, in these types of stories, like crimson peak, the others, or the turning of the screw, the heroine is an innocent with good character and bravery in the face of an inhuman threat. Here, Winifred is that threat, and Monroe makes a meal out of playing the baddie as if she's been starving for the opportunity (though, yes, she's been the villain before).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there's an electrifying mix of menace and mischievousness in her delivery, whether she's flirting with the nurse or threatening a child. Her face shifts smoothly from a mask of civility to a reveal of wrath or revulsion. However, when Winifred gives over to her dark side, Monroe's performance ratchets into a gnarled physicality of demonic possession, which will likely remind viewers of Lily-Rose Depp's turn in Nosferatu. On top of all of this, Monroe offers a sharp humor through unhinged physicality that cuts deep as a shattered tea cup shard through a jugular.

Berdasarkan laporan, in scenes where winifred is spiraling out of control, high-angle cinematography from nico aguilar distorts her proportions, turning this beautiful woman into a warped stranger. Whip pans, rarely used in period pieces, snap from a could-be victim's expression of shock to Winifred's face, and it can feel like a slap to it. But the gnarliest visual choices are when Aguilar gives a point-of-view of objects of violence, like the aforementioned dismembered ear or the rock used to fatally brain the deer. Such choices not only throw an exciting manic energy into Victorian Psycho but also force the audience to feel a part of the action, either to be gobbled up by Winifred's all-consuming darkness or party to it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, composer ariel marx embellishes this tone of creepy complicity with a score studded with familiar and strange sounds. Sometimes, there are slippery sounds (maybe a theremin? Or a saw being bowed?) and distorted voices, perhaps the cries of babies. You might hear a plunking piano or stinging strings, common instrumental choices for Gothic horror. These aural collisions of the expected and unexpected reflect how Feito and Wigon build on the bones of Gothic horror, but create something more modern with their mesmerizing murderess.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the end, victorian psycho is a hoot, wildly fun, and unapologetically deranged on its surface. Instead, she was made from a society that regards cruelty as another luxury the ultra-wealthy get to take for granted. Then, just beneath that, Feito, Wigon, and Monroe weave a tapestry of class conflict, sexism, and trauma that urges audiences to probe deeper to understand that while Winifred is a monster, she was not born one. Well, that is, until someone reflects it back.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, victorian psycho was reviewed out of the 2026 cannes film festival. 13. It opens in theaters Nov. #215. NASA's secret weapon in the lunar space race may be ... procurement reform?

📅 11 Nov 2026

NASA's secret weapon in the lunar space race may be ... procurement reform?

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://arstechnica.com/space/2026/11/nasa-takes-an-all-hands-on-deck-approach-in-its-return-to-the-moon/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the pace that’s occurring, and the nature of the procurements, is unprecedented. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, senior nasa officials held a lengthy news conference last weekend, laying out a series of lunar contract awards, new contract opportunities, and mission decisions. They followed one after the other: landers, nuclear-powered rovers, scouting drones, power generation, storage, and communication satellites.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “hopefully, we’re keeping industry on their toes trying to catch up to all the solicitations we’re doing,” said carlos garcía-galán, manager of the moon base program, more than 90 minutes into the news conference. “This is what it takes to do the Moon Base in the timeline we have set forth. ”.

The rapid-fire announcement of awards tells us a few things about NASA’s efforts to return to the Moon and establish a durable settlement there during the next decade.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, first, the agency is serious about this effort—the artemis moon base program represents the most credible effort to establish a permanent outpost on another world in nasa’s history. Second, NASA is reaching out to all corners of the US commercial space industry, casting an extraordinarily wide net to reach companies that have yet to fly any hardware into orbit. Third, NASA is getting creative about how it’s buying these services, and this may matter most of all.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there was a lot packed into the announcements this weekend, so to make sense of it all, i called mike gold, a lawyer and former nasa associate administrator who set up the artemis accords, who is now the president of redwire space. He said he was blown away. He was at NASA at the beginning of Artemis and understands what it takes to get the government moving. During a period of seven days, Gold said, NASA put out five proposals for lunar contracts.

Diungkapkan bahwa “the pace that’s occurring, and the nature of the procurements is unprecedented,” gold said. “You are seeing an all-hands-on-deck approach. Big companies, small companies, new companies, old companies. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa what has impressed gold most about nasa’s strategy since announcing the moon base in march, at the ignition event, has been the agency’s evolving procurement strategy. The space agency has adopted a flexible procurement strategy similar to one used by the US Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency.

Berdasarkan laporan, there are two components. NASA has largely used a mechanism called Broad Agency Announcements, which ask for a capability such as providing power on the surface of the Moon. This allows NASA to ask industry for ideas without being too prescriptive and levying a bunch of requirements. It’s rather like instead of telling industry precisely what it wants, NASA asks industry what it can do.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, critically, gold said, the space agency has also used a darpa-style preliminary proposal process. In response to a traditional procurement, interested companies would prepare a detailed proposal, often running dozens, if not hundreds, of pages. This required an extraordinary amount of time.

Berdasarkan laporan, with the moon base, nasa is employing a two-step process. After NASA announces the need for a service, interested companies submit a short white paper describing their solution. After a short review, NASA identifies the concepts it wants to pursue further, and only then do companies invest the time and resources to prepare a detailed proposal.

Sebagaimana diketahui, gold said several lunar opportunities interested redwire, and the company submitted initial proposals in response. But it only had to prepare a full proposal for opportunities that NASA wanted to pursue, including using a variant of its roll-out solar arrays on the Moon to generate power.

“We were able to focus the lion’s share of our resources in what the agency really wanted and what we were best at,” he said.

Berdasarkan laporan, from this shift, it seems clear that nasa is trying to move away from micromanaging every individual lunar-base subsystem and instead seeks to coordinate independently developed commercial capabilities. The space agency is sourcing them from everywhere, from major contractors like Lockheed Martin, SpaceX, Blue Origin, and Northrop Grumman to relatively new startups such as Impulse Space, ispace-US, Voyager Technologies, Quantum Space, and more.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, with questions emerging about how committed spacex is to nasa work in the future, the space agency appears to be seeking to diversify the way it gets cargo to the moon. For example, it is leaning into Relativity Space and its large (but unproven) Terran R rocket, as well as orbital transfer vehicles built by Impulse Space. NASA is prioritizing the creation of a whole ecosystem of potential contractors rather than relying on one or two primes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in doing so, nasa is taking a big risk. It is attempting to accelerate its lunar program by buying services from companies whose hardware is not yet operational and, in some cases, exists only as advanced engineering designs. For NASA, ultimately, it is a high-risk, high-reward approach. But in a demanding contest with China to reach and establish settlements on the Moon, NASA’s post-Apollo timidity is no longer tenable.

Diungkapkan bahwa so how will nasa pay for all of the new stuff? some of the funding is being repurposed from the previously shuttered lunar gateway program, nasa administrator jared isaacman said. 6 billion for the Gateway. For example, as part of the “One Big Beautiful Bill” act passed in 2025, NASA received $2. Some of the funding was already appropriated through the agency’s Commercial Lunar Payload Services Program.

Moreover, Isaacman said, some of these contracts are relatively small and will enable NASA to invest more down the road in successful services.

Berdasarkan laporan, “by doing a lot of littles, and learning from our approach and also putting some good wins on the board, we’re demonstrating that we can be very efficient and responsible with taxpayer dollars,” he said. Some of these missions in the, call it, $200 million range between launch, lander, and payload; potentially, you can add those or drop those inside a $25 billion approximate budget per year without putting the entire program at risk. With this approach, he added, “You give future administrations the option of how they can dial up or down missions. ”.

#216. Scientists uncover a 192-year-old mystery hidden in a mangled silver coin

📅 11 Nov 2026

Scientists uncover a 192-year-old mystery hidden in a mangled silver coin

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261109205359.htm

Berdasarkan laporan, a badly distorted british silver coin dating to 1834 may hold evidence of an unusual accident during the minting process nearly 200 years ago. New scientific analysis suggests that the remarkable damage to the coin was more likely caused by a manufacturing problem than by ordinary wear, corrosion, or a later impact.

Berdasarkan laporan, the findings, reported by ia studio in the journal npj heritage science, center on a silver sixpence issued during the reign of king william iv. The coin was found in an album containing various coins at a car boot sale in Greater Manchester, England. Although the sixpence had an individual price tag of £8, the entire album was subsequently purchased as a single lot rather than the coin being bought separately.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what makes this particular sixpence remarkable is the extent and unusual pattern of its damage. Its central surface appears severely crushed and distorted, yet much of the outer rim and the small grooves along its edge remain relatively intact. The contrast raised an intriguing question about what could have happened to the coin.

Diungkapkan bahwa to investigate, researchers examined the silver piece using powerful microscopes, chemical testing, and detailed three-dimensional surface measurements. The results point toward an unusual sequence of intense compression, potentially while the coin was being struck at the mint.

A Crushed Silver Coin Reveals Unusual Clues.

Berdasarkan laporan, the most striking evidence came from the coin's severely distorted central regions. Detailed measurements revealed deep, sharply defined depressions, elevated ridges, stepped surfaces, and areas where the metal appeared to have been pushed and displaced in overlapping patterns.

Sebagaimana diketahui, these features were particularly pronounced on the front of the coin, known as the obverse, which bears the portrait of william iv. Across the damaged central portrait area, the difference between the highest and lowest measured points reached approximately 0. 75 millimeters.

That may sound small, but it represents a substantial distortion on the surface of a thin silver coin.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the investigators found that the overall damage was most consistent with repeated applications of high pressure concentrated in a limited area. The metal also appears to have been at least partly prevented from spreading outward as the force was applied.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this combination of heavy central damage and relatively well-preserved edges is difficult to reconcile with the gradual effects of circulation or simple corrosion. It also makes a single later impact, with the metal free to move outward, a less convincing explanation.

Instead, the findings favor an unusual problem during the original striking process, although the available evidence does not establish the exact sequence of events with certainty.

Microscopic Analysis Reveals Damage Beneath the Surface.

To better understand the unusual deformation, the investigation combined scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDX) and optical surface profilometry.

The microscopic and chemical examinations provided information about the coin's metal composition and the changes affecting its surface.

Diungkapkan bahwa in areas that had escaped the worst damage, testing identified an underlying silver and copper alloy. The more severely distorted regions contained lower measured concentrations of silver, higher levels of copper, and additional chemical evidence associated with corrosion and contamination.

These substances were especially concentrated inside the depressions formed by the damaged metal.

Sebagaimana diketahui, however, the chemical results largely reflected changes at the surface. Although corrosion and contamination had affected the coin, they could not adequately account for the depth, shape, and distribution of its unusual distortions.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the team also used optical surface profilometry, a technique that maps the height and shape of a surface in three dimensions. This made it possible to examine the coin's damaged areas in much greater detail than ordinary photographs could provide.

The resulting maps showed steep depressions, raised shoulders, abrupt changes in surface height, and multiple layers of metal displacement.

Diungkapkan bahwa using height measurements supplied by the oxford materials characterisation service, the study's author determined that the damaged central portrait region varied in height by approximately 750 micrometers, equivalent to 0. 75 millimeters.

Diungkapkan bahwa taken together, the findings suggest that the coin underwent repeated compression while its sideways movement was at least partly restricted. This explanation fits the evidence better than ordinary wear, which generally smooths a coin's surface over time, or corrosion, which tends to remove or chemically alter material.

A Rare Glimpse Into 19th-Century Coin Production.

The sixpence was produced in 1834, when Britain was already using steam-powered presses to manufacture coins.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, during this period, coins with serious striking defects were typically identified through mint inspections and melted down so the metal could be reused. This was especially important for coins made from precious metals such as silver.

If the unusual deformation occurred during the original minting process, the sixpence may therefore represent a rare surviving example of a manufacturing failure that would ordinarily have been removed from circulation before it ever reached the public.

Such a coin could provide a physical record of a brief mechanical problem during the early era of mechanized coin production.

Berdasarkan laporan, determining whether the damage actually occurred at the mint is challenging, however. Historic metal objects can undergo many changes over decades or centuries, and severe deformation may obscure the physical clues needed to identify its origin.

Diungkapkan bahwa to address this uncertainty, the study examined several kinds of evidence independently. The researchers considered the composition of the underlying metal, chemical changes at the surface, and the three-dimensional geometry of the deformation before comparing the results with different possible explanations.

Berdasarkan laporan, the findings also demonstrate how non-destructive scientific techniques can be used to investigate other historic metal objects. By combining chemical and structural evidence, researchers may be able to distinguish manufacturing defects from later damage even when visual inspection alone provides no clear answer.

How AI Helped Investigate the Coin Mystery.

The investigation also explored how computational tools, including artificial intelligence, could assist in evaluating a historical mystery without replacing physical scientific evidence.

Before any laboratory results were available, the author began by studying high-resolution photographs of the sixpence and systematically reviewing its unusual surface features.

This early examination helped identify several possible causes of the damage and establish what kinds of physical measurements would be needed to test them.

Human-supervised computational tools, including large language models (LLMs), helped organize the observations, develop alternative explanations, compare competing ideas, and formulate questions that could later be investigated through laboratory testing.

Importantly, the initial hypotheses and analytical notes were recorded before the independently produced laboratory measurements became available.

The possible explanations included ordinary circulation wear and corrosion, mechanical damage occurring after minting, later compression under restricted conditions, and deformation during the original manufacturing process.

To investigate these possibilities, independent measurements were commissioned from the Experimental Techniques Centre at Brunel University of London and the Oxford Materials Characterisation Service within the Department of Materials at the University of Oxford.

Once the testing was completed, computational tools were used again to help organize the resulting data and compare the physical findings with the earlier explanations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the important sequence was hypothesis first, independent laboratory measurement second," said a. Ikraam, founder of IA STUDIO and author of the study.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we used the models to ask what features mattered and what evidence could distinguish one explanation from another. The models could support the reasoning process, but they could not decide what happened to the coin. Then the laboratory measurements gave us something physical to test those ideas against. ".

Scientific Evidence Points to a Possible Minting Error.

Although artificial intelligence played a supporting role in organizing observations and evaluating competing possibilities, it did not produce the laboratory measurements or determine the final findings.

The study's conclusions were based on independently generated scientific data, with the author retaining responsibility for interpreting the evidence and deciding which explanation was best supported.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the results favor a rare minting anomaly involving repeated, highly concentrated pressure, rather than damage caused by ordinary circulation, corrosion, or a single unrestricted impact after production. Nevertheless, the research does not conclusively establish every detail of what happened to the sixpence.

Beyond shedding light on the possible origins of a strangely mangled 1834 coin, the investigation illustrates how modern imaging, chemical analysis, and carefully evaluated computational tools can work together to uncover clues hidden in historic objects.

What initially appeared to be little more than a badly damaged silver coin may instead preserve an unusual record of how something went wrong during the early days of mechanized coin manufacturing.

Berdasarkan laporan, “she didn’t show up, so fuck it. And then not coming to the table read. It just kept stalling. “I mean, I love Isabelle Huppert — Heaven’s Gate and all that — but there were issues with her contract. Well, we cast Maggie Cheung instead. I fired her,” he said. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “that invariably happens. As far as I’m concerned, if you’re cast and you are not at that table, I don’t owe you jack shit! You can be fired, especially if I get excited by what somebody else did in your absence,” Tarantino continued. He used Michael Parks being cast in two different roles in his Kill Bill films, replacing Ricardo Montalbán, as another example.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “maggie was fantastic in the movie, but you just didn’t need to know how shosanna acquired the cinema. All we needed was a title card saying Four Years Later and Shosanna explaining that she inherited it from her aunt,” Tarantino explained.

Berdasarkan laporan, following its release in 2009, inglourious basterds went on to gross more than $321 million worldwide. It also earned eight Academy Award nominations, with Christoph Waltz taking home the best supporting actor Oscar for his role as Col. Hans Landa.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i have no moral compass when it comes to giving roles to actors: they have to be right. Period. I owe my film the best actors I can find. I don’t owe them shit. They have to feel like they are right for the world I have created,” Tarantino told Glennie about his approach to casting actors. “I have fired actors in the past. If it’s not right, it is not right. ”.

This supernova imposter erupts every 113 days as the compact object gets close to the unstable massive star.

Sebagaimana diketahui, when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

A cosmic imposter that has faked being a supernova 27 times and counting is actually a hot, luminous, and decidedly unstable star that is being fed on by a vampiric black hole or neutron star, NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory has discovered.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when a massive star reaches the end of the road and runs out of nuclear fuel to power fusion reactions in its core, the star is destroyed in a supernova explosion. That’s what astronomers thought they had found on 11 January 2012, when they observed what appeared to be a supernova on the outskirts of the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, which is about 25 million light-years away in the constellation Coma Berenices.

Yet when the light of the 'supernova' faded, the star was still there, only to continue bursting into light every 113 days.

"For 15 years, astronomers have been watching this star get really bright and then dim again on a regular basis," Mojgan Aghakhanloo of the University of Virginia in Charlottesville said in a statement.

Sebagaimana diketahui, several other supernova imposters have been observed over the past decade or two. Until now, no one knew what causes these stars to repeatedly cry wolf. Thanks to Chandra’s X-ray vision, Aghakhanloo has led a team of astronomers who think they have now uncovered an explanation.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the supernova imposter is named at 2016blu, and is a type of star that we call a 'luminous blue variable,' or lbv. These are the most massive and luminous stars in the universe and their extreme characteristics result in them being highly unstable, undergoing intermittent bouts of mass loss as they eject material from their outer layers into the surrounding space.

However, faking a supernova is not part of their typical behavior, so a new way of looking at AT 2016blu was needed.

"To understand the cause of these eruptions, we realized that we needed X-ray data that was timed so that we’d observe the star when it was in an outburst," team member Núria Torres-Albà, also from the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, aghakhanloo’s team were granted the opportunity to commandeer chandra to target an outburst of at 2016blu at the earliest opportunity. That opportunity arose in March 2026.

Berdasarkan laporan, chandra had previously and coincidentally looked in the direction of ngc 4559 back in 2001 and 2002 and did not notice anything unusual back then. This time around, however, it captured a powerful blast of X-rays coinciding with yet another false supernova outburst.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the x-ray detection allowed aghakhanloo’s team to assemble a picture of what is happening. "Until we were able to get Chandra data at the right time, we couldn’t figure out what was making this happen," he said.

Chandra’s X-ray observations indicate that AT 2016blu has an unseen companion, a compact, high-gravity object that is either a neutron star or a stellar-mass black hole on an elliptical 113-day orbit around the luminous blue variable.

Neutron stars and stellar-mass black holes are the core remnants of massive stars that have gone supernova for real, meaning that at one time AT 2016blu was a binary star system.

Berdasarkan laporan, each time the compact object reaches the point in its orbit that is closest to the luminous blue variable, its powerful gravity is able to pull material from the unstable star. This sets in motion a chain of events that results in the brilliant outbursts.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as the stolen starstuff is dragged away from the wounded star and towards the compact object, it forms an accretion disk swirling around the neutron star or black hole so fast and growing so hot that it emits x-rays. These are the X-rays that Chandra saw.

Berdasarkan laporan, the x-rays are immense, energizing the surrounding cloud of material that had been ejected by the luminous blue variable years before. The cloud is heated and glows extremely brightly in visible light, creating the impression of a supernova.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "we suspected that the bright repeating flashes at optical wavelengths might actually be powered by periodic blasts of high-energy x-rays," said team member nathan smith of the university of arizona in tucson. "The dense gas surrounding the system is heated by the X-rays and then glows in the optical. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, calculations suggest that each year a 440 billion trillion pounds of material at minimum is stolen by the compact object, and possibly two orders of magnitude more than that. This is a huge amount, yet it is only 800 millionths of the mass of the sun, and AT 2016blu’s luminous blue variable is at least 33 times the mass of the sun.

Diungkapkan bahwa nevertheless, it is far greater than the maximum rate of material that a neutron star can safely accrete, referred to as the eddington limit. It’s little wonder that the accretion onto the compact object unleashes such extreme energies.

Berdasarkan laporan, at 2016blu is also connected with another mysterious and rare astrophysical phenomenon, that of ultra-luminous x-ray (ulx) sources. The identity of whatever it is that is powering ULXs remains unclear, but the involvement of compact objects such as black holes and neutron stars is high on the list.

AT 2016blu is bright enough to be considered a ULX, so could it act as a Rosetta stone connecting supernova imposters with ULXs? It’s too early to say that; only one other supernova impostor has so far been found to have X-ray emission typical of material being stolen from one star and accreting onto a compact body, and that is SN 2010da, but in that case it is known that the companion is another massive star, a red supergiant, rather than a compact object.

Berdasarkan laporan, the x-ray detection of at 2016blu is described in a paper published on monday (nov. 9) in The Astrophysical Journal.

Berdasarkan laporan, keith cooper is a freelance science journalist and editor in the united kingdom, and has a degree in physics and astrophysics from the university of manchester. He's the author of "The Contact Paradox: Challenging Our Assumptions in the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence" (Bloomsbury Sigma, 2020) and has written articles on astronomy, space, physics and astrobiology for a multitude of magazines and websites.

Small retailers brace for 'huge hit' this holiday season as shipping costs spike

Tanggal: 06 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/06/small-business-holiday-shipping-costs.html

Berdasarkan laporan, when jenni shields began her small business eight years ago selling handmade hair accessories, she paid $2. 93 to ship an order, or close to $4 in today's dollars when adjusted for inflation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, last year, shields said, an average shipping label for her products cost around $4. But when she took a typical batch of orders to her local U. S. 50. Postal Service office last month in Kansas City, Kansas, she was shocked to see that it was an average of nearly $6 per package.

Shields is just one of the small- and medium-sized retailers who are struggling to keep up with rising shipping costs as the price of fuel continues to trend upward.

Diungkapkan bahwa small business owners such as shields are facing a difficult holiday season. Customer demand is strong, but some retailers said their profits will be dented — if not eaten up entirely — by higher shipping and other costs.

Sebagaimana diketahui, shields said she charges her customers $6 in shipping fees, which includes roughly $1. 50 to cover her packaging supplies. The dramatic upswing this year means she's no longer breaking even on her orders and instead eating the added costs, she said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "i am losing money at this point, and i've really taken a huge hit this year," said shields, the owner of evie pearl handmade, which sells bows, quilted headbands and other accessories. "I feel like it's just been this slow increase up [in shipping costs], and I feel horrible. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, the surge in fuel prices since the u. S. and Israel attacked Iran in February has driven up the cost of shipping by sea, air, rail and road.

That means higher costs across the board, including for shipping giant Amazon, which reported an 11% increase in shipping expenses in the third quarter compared with last year, to individual retailers.

Diungkapkan bahwa globally, air cargo is going for about $3. 37 per kilogram, up 43% from a similar period a year ago, according to transportation marketplace Freightos. Judah Levine, Freightos' head of research, said in addition to higher fuel, demand for fast shipping of hardware used to build data centers is helping to boost air freight rates, even weeks before peak last-minute holiday packages take to the skies.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for businesses, that runup is going to "squeeze their margins in the near-term," said jason seidl, managing director and transportation analyst at td cowen. "Larger companies tend not to be exposed to the spot market, and they'll have what we call dedicated deals in place. ".

But that doesn't help smaller companies, which are walking a delicate line of not wanting to alienate customers who have enjoyed free shipping for nearly a generation.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, todd shelton, founder of the eponymous 23-year-old new jersey clothing company that makes high-end men's jeans, t-shirts and button-up shirts locally, said he started charging customers for return shipping this week for the first time after absorbing the higher expenses this year. The shipping is deducted from customers' refunds.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, shelton said his costs have been rising for materials, too, such as his imported japanese denim and shirt fabric from portugal. The company is still profitable, but the higher costs have eaten into profit margins as they stay elevated, he's considering raising prices or charging for shipping to customers, he said.

Shields said she's considering raising her shipping fees for the first time in six years to keep up with the increases.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the holiday season is one of shields' busiest. But she said she's seen a slowdown in sales because of shipping fees.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "i can't compete with amazon on the free shipping. "I'm seeing so much of my percentage that's supposed to come back to me and my family being put towards the shipping costs. I can't afford that," she said. I can't do that. ".

With no sign of fuel prices declining significantly, Shields, who runs her business out of her spare bedroom at home, said she's not sure that small businesses will be able to emerge on the other side of the holidays.

Diungkapkan bahwa shippers including ups, fedex and usps have all instituted holiday surcharges, with prices varying by package type and lasting through the end of the season. Though that's typical during the peak holiday period each year, those charges have continued to rise over the past few years.

But even as costs everywhere climb, consumers are still spending.

Diungkapkan bahwa according to the national retail federation, retail sales through the end of the year are expected to grow 4. 2%, translating to total spending of $1. That's compared with last year's holiday sales totaling $972 billion, which was 3. 01 trillion. 1% growth.

Some of that growth is from inflation, meaning consumers are simply paying more for the same goods.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "customers all expect to spend more this holiday, but part of why they expect to spend more is they expect things to cost more, not because they'd like to spend more or they were hoping to get more quantity of stuff," said aaron cheris, the global retail practice head at bain & company. "So what I suspect happens is that non-discretionary categories do fine, because you buy the food you were going to need to buy anyway, but then the amount of cash that's left over for [discretionary] goods is less. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa still, cheris said it's shaping up to be a record year for shipping costs, which is putting immense pressure on smaller retailers. That means many retailers may find themselves in financial distress in the first quarter of next year as they struggle to make it through the holiday season.

He added that larger retail companies will also have to reckon with rising costs, though they may not feel those effects until later quarters because they have shipping contracts that have already been locked in and have control over their own delivery fleets.

Berdasarkan laporan, "if anything, it benefits the scale players over the little players, but it's kind of a little bit bad for everybody," cheris said. "I think that is the challenge. ".

#221. Alzheimer’s may have early warning signs outside the brain

📅 10 Nov 2026

Alzheimer’s may have early warning signs outside the brain

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261108233103.htm

Alzheimer's disease is best known for its effects on memory and thinking, but new research suggests that some symptoms may develop in a surprising place: outside the brain.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, scientists at the university of central florida (ucf) have discovered that genetic mutations associated with alzheimer's can interfere with the nerves that control muscle movement, even without involvement from the brain or spinal cord. The findings could help explain why some people with Alzheimer's experience changes in walking, balance, or coordination long before noticeable memory problems emerge.

The discovery raises the possibility that movement difficulties could provide earlier warning signs of the disease and that treatments focused exclusively on the brain may overlook important problems elsewhere in the body.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the research was led by james hickman, a professor at ucf's nanoscience technology center, and research professor xiufang "nadine" guo, working alongside scientists at the healthcare technology company hesperos. Funded by the National Institutes of Health's National Institute on Aging, the study used laboratory systems built from human cells to investigate how inherited Alzheimer's mutations affect movement. The findings were published in Alzheimer's & Dementia: The Journal of the Alzheimer's Association.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "motor deficits may be an earlier indication [of alzheimer's]," guo says. "If we can detect those changes and intervene earlier, that could help delay the onset of central nervous system symptoms. ".

Why Alzheimer's Symptoms May Appear Before Memory Loss.

Diungkapkan bahwa alzheimer's is generally associated with progressive memory loss, confusion, and declining cognitive abilities. However, doctors have also observed that some patients develop physical symptoms, including changes in balance, coordination, and gait (manner of walking), years before clear cognitive difficulties become apparent.

These observations have raised an important question: Are such movement problems simply a consequence of damage occurring in the brain, or could Alzheimer's also interfere directly with nerves elsewhere in the body?.

To investigate, the UCF team focused on familial Alzheimer's, a rare inherited form of the disease that typically develops earlier in life (from 40 to 65 years of age) than the more common form.

Their experiments revealed that motor neurons carrying mutations linked to familial Alzheimer's could disrupt the connections responsible for controlling muscles, even when the brain and spinal cord were completely absent from the experimental system.

Diungkapkan bahwa motor neurons are specialized nerve cells that transmit signals to muscles, telling them when to contract and produce movement. The new findings suggest that Alzheimer's mutations can interfere with this process directly, rather than affecting movement only through damage to the brain.

Berdasarkan laporan, "this is the first time it's been demonstrated that deficits in the peripheral nervous system can arise directly from these mutations," hickman says. "It means drugs that target the brain may not fix problems in the rest of the body. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa the peripheral nervous system includes the nerves located outside the brain and spinal cord. These nerves carry signals between the central nervous system and the rest of the body, helping control movement, sensation, and other essential functions.

Berdasarkan laporan, guo also points out that preserving the ability to move could have benefits beyond physical health. Regular physical activity is associated with better cognitive well-being, so protecting motor function may also help support brain health.

How a Miniature Human Cell System Revealed the Discovery.

To examine the relationship between Alzheimer's mutations and muscle movement, the scientists used an innovative laboratory platform known as "human-on-a-chip" technology.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, developed and manufactured through hesperos, a company co-founded by hickman, these miniature systems bring different types of human cells together under controlled conditions. They allow researchers to recreate specific biological functions and observe how diseases interfere with them.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, unlike conventional laboratory experiments that examine isolated cells, these systems can reproduce important interactions between different tissues. They also provide an alternative to animal models, which do not always accurately reflect how human diseases behave.

For this study, the team created a miniature model of the neuromuscular junction, the connection where a motor neuron communicates with a muscle cell.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the model was deliberately designed without a brain or spinal cord. This was a crucial part of the experiment because it allowed the researchers to investigate whether Alzheimer's-related changes could cause movement problems independently of the central nervous system.

Berdasarkan laporan, the scientists combined healthy muscle cells with motor neurons derived from stem cells that carried genetic mutations associated with familial alzheimer's disease. Stem cells are cells that can develop into specialized types of cells, making them valuable tools for studying human diseases in the laboratory.

The researchers then examined how effectively the altered nerve cells communicated with otherwise healthy muscle tissue.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the results showed that the alzheimer's-associated mutations could interfere with normal nerve-to-muscle function. This suggests that at least some movement difficulties linked to the disease may arise directly in the peripheral nervous system rather than being caused entirely by degeneration in the brain.

Why Damaged Nerve Connections Can Affect Walking and Balance.

Every voluntary movement depends on successful communication between the nervous system and the muscles.

Berdasarkan laporan, at the neuromuscular junction, an electrical signal traveling along a motor neuron triggers chemical communication that causes a muscle to contract. This process makes everyday activities possible, from walking and maintaining posture to lifting objects and performing precise movements.

Berdasarkan laporan, when the connection becomes impaired, muscles may respond less effectively to nerve signals. Depending on the severity and location of the problem, this can contribute to weakness, reduced coordination, and difficulty sustaining physical activity.

To evaluate these effects, the research team measured how consistently nerve signals produced muscle contractions and how long the muscles could continue contracting before becoming fatigued.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, these measurements provided a direct assessment of how well the nerve and muscle cells worked together. They also resemble aspects of the functional testing physicians use when examining patients with movement disorders.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "you can't move unless the motor circuit works," hickman says. "When a doctor taps your knee to check your reflex, they're testing that exact connection. ".

By demonstrating impaired nerve-to-muscle communication in a system containing no brain or spinal cord, the study provides evidence that mutations linked to familial Alzheimer's can produce effects beyond the central nervous system.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, the experiments do not establish that these changes necessarily occur before memory loss in patients. Further research will be needed to determine how closely the laboratory findings reflect the progression of Alzheimer's in people, particularly those with the more common forms of the disease.

Could This Discovery Lead to Earlier Alzheimer's Detection?.

The findings suggest a potentially important new direction for Alzheimer's research: looking beyond memory and other cognitive symptoms when investigating the disease.

If future studies confirm that changes in motor function are detectable early in certain patients, tests of walking, coordination, or nerve-to-muscle activity might eventually help identify disease-related changes before more obvious neurological symptoms develop.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the results also raise questions about treatment. Many Alzheimer's therapies are designed to address processes occurring in the brain, but medications that target the central nervous system may not necessarily correct abnormalities affecting peripheral nerves and muscles.

Understanding these separate effects could help researchers investigate treatments that protect physical function alongside cognitive health.

Human-on-a-Chip Technology Could Transform Disease Research.

Beyond the implications for Alzheimer's, the researchers see considerable potential in using human-on-a-chip systems to investigate other diseases and evaluate possible treatments.

Because these platforms contain human cells and reproduce measurable biological activities, they can help scientists observe disease-related changes in conditions that more closely resemble human physiology than some conventional experimental models.

This approach may be particularly useful in drug development, where researchers need to understand not only how a potential treatment affects individual cells but also how it influences interactions between different tissues.

Such systems can also uncover biological effects that may be difficult to detect in animal experiments, potentially helping researchers identify promising therapies and recognize limitations earlier in development.

For Hickman, the progress represents the culmination of three decades of work devoted to understanding disease through more realistic laboratory models.

"These systems let us study disease in a way that's closer to what actually happens in the human body, and that's what we need to develop better treatments," he says.

Such an investment may give markets “a shot of confidence as the artificial-intelligence trade shows signs of strain,” The Wall Street Journal reported.

Sebagaimana diketahui, still, tsmc has plenty of money to spare on such a bet. #227. Scientists discover that necks didn't evolve for the reason we thought

📅 11 Nov 2026

Scientists discover that necks didn't evolve for the reason we thought

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261108233101.htm

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the first animals to make the transition from water to land nearly 380 million years ago may have had a surprising limitation: they could barely turn their heads. Although scientists have long believed that the evolution of necks gave these pioneering creatures greater freedom to look around, new research suggests their necks were actually remarkably stiff.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the discovery challenges a decades-old explanation for why animals developed distinct necks in the first place. Rather than evolving to improve head movement, necks may have emerged as part of broader changes to the skeleton that allowed animals to use their front limbs for movement.

Berdasarkan laporan, to investigate this possibility, an international team of researchers combined new fossil evidence with experiments on living fish and computer models of ancient anatomy. Their findings, published October 14 in the journal Nature, offer a new perspective on one of the most important evolutionary transitions in Earth's history.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "this is a really interesting time in earth's history where some of the first forests are forming, and there's a really radical reorganization of the earth," said tom stewart, an assistant professor of biology at penn state and a member of the research team. What's cool is that many of the changes that were occurring in the skeleton at this time, about 380 million years ago, are still reflected in our own bodies today. "So, understanding exactly when our lineage made that transition from water to land, how it was achieved, and which anatomical systems were changing is an important part of that story. ".

Why Scientists Thought Animals Evolved Necks.

For decades, the prevailing explanation was that necks evolved to give early tetrapods, the ancestors of four-limbed vertebrates, greater control over their heads as they adapted to life outside the water.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the reasoning seemed straightforward. An animal living in shallow water or moving onto land would benefit from looking downward or turning its head from side to side to locate prey, recognize threats, and explore its surroundings. A flexible neck would allow it to do this without repositioning its entire body.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, modern fish generally lack a distinct neck because their shoulder structures connect directly to their skulls. To look in another direction, they typically have to turn their bodies instead. Separating the head from the shoulders therefore appeared to be an important step toward greater mobility.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, determining how these ancient animals actually moved has been difficult. Much of their backbone consisted of soft tissue that rarely survives long enough to become fossilized, leaving scientists with an incomplete picture of how their necks functioned.

Diungkapkan bahwa "the fish that were undergoing these changes had a vertebral column that was largely made up of soft tissue, which, unlike bone, is rarely preserved in the fossil record," stewart said. "In these cases, we can look to modern animals to serve as analogues for the past, like how living birds can teach us about now extinct dinosaurs. ".

Ancient Fish Fossils Reveal a Turning Point in Evolution.

Some of the best evidence for the transition from water to land comes from fish that lived during the Devonian Period, approximately 420 to 360 million years ago.

Sebagaimana diketahui, these ancient animals possessed an unusual combination of features. While they retained many characteristics of aquatic fish, some had stronger, more substantial fins that may have helped support their weight. Such adaptations could have allowed them to lift themselves off the bottom or push through shallow water.

At the same time, certain species began showing a clear separation between the skull and shoulders, creating the first distinct necks.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one especially important example is tiktaalik, a fossil fish first described in 2006. Its remains were discovered on Ellesmere Island in Nunavut, Canada, in the northern Arctic. Because Tiktaalik is closely related to the earliest vertebrates with limbs, its anatomy provides valuable clues about the evolutionary changes that eventually made life on land possible.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "tiktaalik is one of these fossil fish, and it was first described in 2006," stewart said. "It has been reasonably assumed for decades that this separation of head and shoulders must have allowed the head to move more freely, so the hypothesis that neck mobility was an evolutionary driver for this change in the tetrapod body plan has prevailed, at least until now. ".

Tiktaalik also helps researchers understand other major changes that occurred during this evolutionary transition, including the shift from drawing food into the mouth through suction underwater to biting on land, as well as the gradual transformation of swimming structures into limbs used for walking.

Diungkapkan bahwa "the materials have been really important because tiktaalik is one of the closest relatives to limbed vertebrates," stewart said. "It helps us to reconstruct a lot of intermediary steps in the transition to life on land, such as the move from suction feeding in water to biting on land or from swimming to walking. ".

How Modern Sturgeon Helped Solve an Ancient Mystery.

The key to testing the traditional explanation for neck evolution came from an unexpected source: the sturgeon, a modern fish sometimes described as a living fossil because it retains several ancient anatomical features.

Berdasarkan laporan, early tetrapods had backbones that were very different from those of most vertebrates living today. Instead of relying primarily on a series of large vertebrae connected by joints, their spinal columns contained a prominent structure called the notochord.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the notochord is a long, flexible rod of tissue that runs through the vertebral column and helps support the body. In these ancient animals, the individual vertebrae were relatively small and arranged around a much larger tube of soft tissue.

Sebagaimana diketahui, because this arrangement responds to forces differently from a modern backbone, researchers had struggled to determine how much flexibility it would have allowed. That uncertainty prevented them from directly testing the idea that necks initially evolved to improve head movement.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sturgeon provided an opportunity to overcome that problem. Although they are only distantly related to the ancient animals being studied, their backbones have a similar notochord structure.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the research team measured the stiffness and mechanical properties of the notochord in modern sturgeon. They then incorporated those measurements into models of fossil animals, including early tetrapods such as Tiktaalik, to estimate how far their necks could actually move.

Diungkapkan bahwa the results were striking. Even when the head and shoulders were anatomically separated, the structure of the backbone would have severely restricted movement. The earliest necks appear to have been much less flexible than researchers had assumed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we know that tetrapods did eventually gain higher neck mobility," said dana korneisel, a postdoctoral researcher at uppsala university in sweden and first author of the paper. "Clearly it was advantageous eventually, but it was not an advantage available to these early tetrapods yet because of the limitations of their anatomy. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the researchers had expected the new models to clarify how much additional movement early necks provided. Instead, they found that most of the animals they examined would have gained little ability to reposition their heads.

Diungkapkan bahwa "i undertook this study to find out how big of a difference this change in anatomy made for these animals," korneisel said. "The vertebral columns of sturgeon are built a lot like those of early tetrapods, but they didn't seem terribly stiff. So, after doing the modeling, the lack of significant head mobility for almost all of these animals was a huge surprise. ".

The findings suggest that the first animals with distinct necks could not simply turn their heads to survey their surroundings the way many modern land animals can.

Their ability to lift their heads was also extremely limited, sometimes falling below what would be expected in fish.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "head elevation in these animals was no more than what you would expect in fish and, sometimes, even less," korneisel said. "We found that the kind of head twisting that we can do when we shake our heads was not feasible in any of these animals. ".

The researchers also cautioned that their estimates may actually overstate how much movement was possible.

Diungkapkan bahwa their models considered the mechanical properties of the backbone itself, but other structures would have added further restrictions. Muscles, skin, and even bones embedded within the skin of some early tetrapods may have made their necks still more rigid.

Necks May Have Evolved for Walking Before Looking.

Together, the findings point to a different explanation for the origin of the neck.

Instead of first appearing because animals needed to turn their heads, the separation of the skull and shoulders may have developed alongside anatomical changes that allowed the front limbs to support and move the body.

In other words, the earliest necks may have been a consequence of adaptations for locomotion rather than an adaptation for improved vision or head movement.

Diungkapkan bahwa greater neck flexibility eventually evolved and became an important advantage for land vertebrates. But the new evidence suggests that this benefit came later, after the basic structure of the neck was already established.

Berdasarkan laporan, the discovery also highlights the importance of the notochord in understanding animal evolution. Backbones dominated by this structure are uncommon among living vertebrates, but they were widespread during much of Earth's history. Studying modern animals that retain similar anatomy can therefore help scientists reconstruct how extinct creatures moved and behaved.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "we want to understand how these early tetrapods were living and how that is reflected in changes to their bodies," stewart said. The cool part of this story is that it combines data from fossils and studies of living animals in a mechanical, functional perspective to reconstruct what the changes we see in the animal's anatomy mean for their behavior. "Trying to reconstruct where an animal lived, how it moved, what its behavior was, is a really difficult thing. ".

By bringing together fossil discoveries, experiments on living fish, and biomechanical modeling, the researchers have challenged a familiar explanation for an anatomical feature that remains central to the bodies of humans and many other vertebrates today.

Berdasarkan laporan, along with stewart and korneisel, the international research team included cassandra m. A. Donatelli of the University of Washington; Linfang Han, Marcos Martinez, Tetsuto Miyashita, and Emily M. Traynor, Benjamin K. Otoo, and Hillary C. Standen of the University of Ottawa in Canada; and Andrew L. Maddin of Carleton University in Canada.

Diungkapkan bahwa the research received support from the steven cohen award for student research, presented by the society of vertebrate paleontology, and the natural sciences and engineering research council of canada (rgpin-06442). Keep in mind that due to the demand for the 30th Celebration UPCs, sellers have little incentive to discount listings much below market price (around $360 per Ultra-Premium Collection).

For now, it's worth keeping the retailer pages above close at hand, so you can compare prices for any available stock and decide what’s best for your trading card budget.

Diungkapkan bahwa maddie’s quite an earnest character. It’s so human to still feel like a kid, like, “I feel like it would be me,” and also the bigger picture of people claiming someone else’s loss. Berdasarkan laporan, the rule that we have internally is that the show’s perspective on the supernatural needs to mimic a relationship with faith. I don’t know the meaning of life. Sebagaimana diketahui, it’s part of why i love and gravitate towards spiritual journalism — journalism that follows people’s unexplainable events. #230. Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production in Texas next year to ramp Cybercab, Musk says

📅 06 Nov 2026

Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production in Texas next year to ramp Cybercab, Musk says

Tanggal: 06 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/06/tesla-cybertruck-texas-musk.html

Tesla CEO Elon Musk on Friday said the electric vehicle maker will "be winding down" production of the Cybertruck at its Texas gigafactory around the middle of next year.

Musk, who hailed the Cybertruck as the future of the pickup truck segment, said in a post on X early Friday morning that the end of production at the massive facility would make room for manufacturing of its Cybercab robotaxi.

The Cybertruck is exclusively produced at the company's plant in Texas alongside the Tesla Model Y and two-seat Cybercab, which Musk has touted as a crucial product for the automaker moving forward.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, musk did not say whether the company would produce the cybertruck at a different facility, but he later responded to a user on x who called the update an "end of an era" and said the cybertruck was the "best vehicle tesla has ever made. ".

"True, but the Cybertruck fleet will be around for a long time," Musk said.

Berdasarkan laporan, tesla began cybertruck deliveries in late 2023. The company did not immediately respond to a request for comment from CNBC.

The Cybertruck and its polarizing design gained a niche following, but it did not achieve mass-market sales, despite Musk's pre-launch prediction that annual sales would eventually total 250,000.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "trucks have been the same for a very long time," musk said when the truck was unveiled in 2019. Trucks have been basically the same. We want to try something different. "Like 100 years. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, while tesla does not break out its sales by model or region, cox automotive estimated sales of the cybertruck last year at 20,237 units in the u. S. , down 48% from 38,965 in 2024.

One big buyer of the Cybertruck last year was Musk's aerospace and tech conglomerate, SpaceX, which spent $131 million buying up the angular steel trucks at Tesla's suggested retail price, according to a SpaceX financial filing.

The distinct look of the vehicle made some owners a target of rude gestures and more serious road rage, one owner told CNBC last May, after Musk became the biggest funder of Donald Trump's presidential campaign and led the so-called Department of Government Efficiency, an effort to slash the federal workforce and regulations.

Diungkapkan bahwa wired wrote in an october 2025 feature story, "there is likely no object that feels more emblematic of us president donald trump's return to the white house than the tesla cybertruck. " The magazine interviewed owners who described being spit on and sworn at due to their choice of vehicle.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the cybertruck's specifications also fell short of those tesla advertised early on, and in some cases fell short of those offered by leading fuel-burning pickups. There have also been many quality and production problems associated with the vehicles.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the 2024 tesla cybertruck was the subject of 11 voluntary recalls, according to the national highway traffic safety administration website. Issues ranged from a "trapped" acceleration pedal risk that could cause unintended acceleration, to software defects and an inverter fault that could result in sudden loss of drive power.

#231. Scientists finally discover why we learn to love bitter coffee

📅 09 Nov 2026

Scientists finally discover why we learn to love bitter coffee

Tanggal: 09 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261108233100.htm

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a first taste of black coffee can be surprisingly unpleasant. Its sharp bitterness is the kind of flavor our brains are naturally inclined to avoid. Yet millions of people eventually come to enjoy that same taste, often looking forward to their morning cup. What changes?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, scientists at uc san francisco may have uncovered an important part of the answer. Their research reveals a little-understood dopamine pathway linking the digestive system and the brain, helping explain how we develop a liking for certain flavors through repeated experience.

Berdasarkan laporan, dopamine is a chemical messenger involved in motivation, reward, and learning. Researchers have long known that it helps the brain recognize experiences worth repeating. However, most studies have examined rapid dopamine signals that appear within seconds of encountering something rewarding, such as the sight of a favorite meal.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the new research, published november 4 in nature, examines a different system. This slower pathway responds to information coming from inside the body, allowing the brain to learn about the benefits of food after it has been consumed.

"We've shown that this slow dopamine system is what drives us to learn to like certain foods over time, and we can see where and how that happens," said Zachary Knight, PhD, professor of Physiology and senior author of the study.

Diungkapkan bahwa the findings offer a possible explanation for why an initially unpleasant flavor can gradually become enjoyable. Once the brain connects the taste of coffee with caffeine's stimulating effects, Knight explained, "that coffee starts to taste a lot better. ".

How the Gut Sends Reward Signals to the Brain.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, scientists have spent decades investigating dopamine and its influence on behavior. Its familiar, rapidly acting signals help us respond to opportunities for reward. But dopamine also operates on a slower timescale, through a system that has received far less attention.

According to Knight, this slower process largely unfolds outside our conscious awareness.

Diungkapkan bahwa when food enters the digestive tract, specialized sensors detect nutrients, including sugar and fat. Information about those nutrients travels toward the brain, where it can produce a dopamine response that develops gradually and continues for several minutes.

Diungkapkan bahwa to investigate this process, knight worked with james grove, phd, who was a graduate student at the time. They introduced nutrients directly into the stomachs of mice while monitoring dopamine activity throughout their brains.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the researchers used either sugar water or a liquid resembling a milkshake. Delivering these substances directly into the stomach allowed them to separate the effects of nutrients from the experience of tasting food.

The results revealed a powerful, prolonged dopamine response in a specific brain region called the anterior basolateral amygdala, or BLA.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the amygdala is involved in emotional processing and learning, including forming associations between experiences and their consequences. Scientists already knew that dopamine was released in this particular region, but its purpose had remained unclear.

"We could see that this dopamine is part of a different system and begin to understand its role," he said.

Scientists Find a Brain Circuit That Changes Food Preferences.

Sebagaimana diketahui, finding the dopamine signal was only the beginning. The researchers next wanted to determine whether it actually influenced how animals learned to prefer different flavors.

Berdasarkan laporan, they first interrupted the newly identified pathway in mice. The animals continued eating normally, indicating that the disruption did not prevent them from consuming food. However, they lost the ability to learn that an unfamiliar flavor was associated with receiving calories.

The team then conducted the opposite experiment.

Sebagaimana diketahui, after mice tasted a flavor containing no calories, the researchers artificially activated dopamine fibers in the bla. Remarkably, the animals developed a preference for that flavor even though it provided no nutritional reward.

In effect, stimulating the pathway reproduced the learning signal that nutrients would ordinarily generate.

Together, the experiments showed that this dopamine system plays a critical role in teaching the brain which flavors predict rewarding nutritional effects.

A Surprising Discovery in the Left Side of the Brain.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the researchers also looked for evidence that a comparable process occurs in humans. Brain imaging studies conducted by Knight's collaborators revealed a strikingly similar pattern.

Sebagaimana diketahui, dana small, phd, a psychologist at yale university, revisited data from an earlier positron emission tomography (pet) study involving 13 men. Participants had consumed either a milkshake or a drink without calories.

Her analysis found that dopamine release following nutrient delivery was especially concentrated in the left side of the BLA.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a separate study led by marc tittgemeyer, phd, and his colleagues provided additional evidence. Using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), which measures changes in brain activity associated with blood flow, the researchers examined 38 adults after they consumed glucose, a simple sugar.

They observed increased activity in the same brain region.

One of the most unexpected findings was that the response was not evenly distributed between the brain's two hemispheres.

In both mice and humans, nutrients produced a considerably stronger dopamine response in the left BLA than in the corresponding region on the right.

That imbalance surprised Knight because brain networks responsible for essential functions, such as feeding, are generally expected to work in a relatively symmetrical fashion.

Sebagaimana diketahui, why the left side plays such a prominent role remains unanswered. Knight's laboratory is now investigating what causes this unusual difference.

Could This Discovery Help Scientists Change Food Cravings?.

Diungkapkan bahwa identifying the pathway provides researchers with a clearer picture of how the digestive system influences the brain's learned responses to food. It also raises an intriguing possibility: Could scientists eventually use this knowledge to change which foods people find appealing?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one area of interest involves glp-1 medications, a class of drugs that mimic a hormone naturally released by the gut. These medications can substantially alter appetite and eating behavior.

Knight's team did not investigate GLP-1 drugs in the new study, so it remains unknown whether they influence the dopamine pathway the researchers identified.

Diungkapkan bahwa still, knight suggests that one possible explanation for some of their effects could involve reducing the dopamine signals generated when nutrients reach the digestive system. If that happens, foods might gradually become less rewarding because the brain would receive weaker signals reinforcing their flavors.

For now, this remains a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated effect of the medications.

Diungkapkan bahwa the broader implications extend beyond hunger and fullness. Many approaches to changing eating behavior focus on reducing appetite or increasing feelings of satisfaction after a meal. The newly mapped pathway suggests that the brain's process of learning food preferences could eventually become another target.

By influencing how the brain connects flavors with their consequences, future treatments might someday help people develop different preferences rather than simply making them feel less hungry.

"By understanding the steps between nutrient detection in the gut and learning in the brain, it might be possible to fine-tune them to subtly change our preferences for different foods," Knight said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the discovery offers a new perspective on why our tastes can change over time. From learning to enjoy bitter coffee to developing a preference for calorie-rich foods, what we love to eat may depend partly on a quiet conversation between the gut and brain that continues long after the first bite.

The research was supported by the National Institutes of Health (grants R01-DK106399, R01-DK138127, R01-NS116626, and R01-DK145100 and F31-NS120468).

Philae drifted and bounced around the comet for two hours before Rosetta's cameras lost track of it.

Diungkapkan bahwa when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on nov. 12, 2014, a European spacecraft named Philae landed on Comet 67P. To say it was a bumpy landing would be an understatement.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the european space agency's philae lander separated from an orbiter called rosetta ahead of its historic landing in 2014. It was supposed to use harpoons to secure itself on to the surface of Comet 67P, but the harpoons never fired.

Berdasarkan laporan, when it touched down, it immediately bounced back up into space. The first bounce brought Philae half a mile above the comet's surface before gravity brought it back down.

Berdasarkan laporan, philae was missing for almost two years before scientists found it. Images from Rosetta showed Philae stuck in a dark crevice on top of the rubber duck-shaped comet.

The European Space Agency's Rosetta and Philae expedition was a first-of-its-kind mission, an endeavour to not just rendezvous with a comet and watch it change over time as it approached the sun (that was Rosetta's job), but also to soft-land a probe on its icy and rocky surface to see what a comet is truly made of.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the rosetta and philae mission succeeded on both counts, but philae's historic landing was marred by its turbulent touchdown. Philae actually landed three different times on Comet 67/P, all because the harpoons designed to secure it in place didn't fire as planned.

Sebagaimana diketahui, after the first landing, philae bounced up and drifted around the comet for two hours, making another bounce before rosetta's cameras lost track of it. Scientists figured it was stuck in a shady spot where sunlight couldn't reach its solar panels. Because it was solar-powered, Philae needed to be facing the sun properly to generate enough power for sustained operation on the comet's surface.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, still, philae did have some power stored in batteries, which lasted for more than two days on the surface. That allowed Philae to perform some science with its 10 instruments in the time it had on Comet 67/P. Most notably, Philae found organic molecules that had never been detected on a comet before.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the rosetta orbiter continued to orbit comet 67p until september 2016, and it was in that month -- just weeks before rosetta itself landed on the comet on sept. 30, 2016 -- that the spacecraft rediscovered the Philae lander lying on its side in a rocky crevice.
