#269. Scientists discover why some mosquitoes love you and others don't

📅 11 Nov 2026

Scientists discover why some mosquitoes love you and others don't

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261106174541.htm

Some people seem to attract mosquitoes wherever they go, but new research reveals that being a mosquito magnet depends on which species is doing the biting.

Berdasarkan laporan, in a study published in iscience, researchers at florida international university (fiu) tested how three of the world's most dangerous mosquito species responded to 119 human volunteers. Surprisingly, not a single participant attracted all three species. Instead, each species favored a different group of people, largely based on their individual body chemistry and natural skin odors.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the discovery could change how scientists approach the prevention of mosquito-borne diseases. Because different mosquito species respond to different chemical signals from human skin, researchers may eventually be able to create next-generation, species-specific repellents that offer more targeted protection.

"Isolating the components of human odor that attract or repel mosquitoes could lead to novel strategies to combat vector-borne diseases," said Matthew DeGennaro, a neurogeneticist who leads the research team and directs the Biomolecular Sciences Institute at FIU, Miami's state university.

Different Mosquito Species Prefer Different People.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the researchers investigated three species responsible for spreading serious illnesses, including yellow fever, dengue, zika, west nile and other diseases. These were Aedes aegypti, Aedes albopictus (Asian tiger mosquito) and Culex quinquefasciatus (southern house mosquito).

Sebagaimana diketahui, led by ph. D. student Kaylee Marrero, the investigation was the first to directly compare how several mosquito species reacted to the same human participants. The findings revealed unexpected differences in the chemical and microbial signals each species appeared to use when choosing whom to bite.

Berdasarkan laporan, "we didn't expect the species to prefer different people when we started the study," marrero said. "Each species having a distinct microbial signature that they use as a cue was so surprising to me. ".

Each mosquito species showed its own distinct preferences:.

The Hidden Chemistry Behind Mosquito Attraction.

Berdasarkan laporan, human body odor is far more complicated than it might seem. Our skin releases a mixture of more than 1,000 volatile organic compounds, many of which scientists have yet to fully identify or understand.

Berdasarkan laporan, the researchers found that the three mosquito species did not share a common preference for particular individuals. Instead, each consistently favored its own subset of volunteers, suggesting that different species have evolved distinct methods for detecting and interpreting human scent.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to investigate what made certain people more appealing, the team collected samples of participants' body odors and skin microbiomes alongside the mosquito preference tests. They then examined which chemical compounds and microorganisms were present and measured their relative abundance.

The results showed strong connections between the mosquitoes' preferences and differences in the chemical and microbial makeup of people's skin.

Berdasarkan laporan, "this connected so well with the differences in skin bacteria and odors," degennaro said. "It is clear to me now that our skin microbiomes define our human odor signature. Each species found its own way to decode that signature. ".

Could This Discovery Lead to Better Mosquito Repellents?.

Understanding why one mosquito species finds a person attractive while another does not could open new possibilities for preventing dangerous infections.

By identifying the specific chemical compounds and skin bacteria that attract or discourage different mosquitoes, the FIU researchers are helping establish a scientific foundation for more precisely targeted repellents.

The findings could also improve public health strategies by allowing communities to focus on the particular mosquito species responsible for spreading disease in their region.

Rather than assuming that all mosquitoes are drawn to the same people for the same reasons, future prevention methods may be designed around the distinct chemical preferences of each species.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on thursday (nov. 12), the Euclid space telescope released its first major batch of data, capturing the light of more than a billion objects over an area of sky as big as 9,500 full moons. The data release lays the foundation for one of the largest-ever 3D maps of the cosmos and many groundbreaking discoveries about the nature of dark energy and dark matter.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the european space agency's (esa) euclid space telescope has been called the "dark universe detective" because of its capability to investigate the dual mysteries of dark matter, the universe's most mysterious stuff, and dark energy, the force accelerating the expansion of the universe. Collectively, these cosmic elements are sometimes referred to as the dark universe.

Berdasarkan laporan, the new data release, designated dr1-foundation, was built from 13 months of observations and is accompanied by a multitude of images, including large sky mosaics. It marks the first major release of mission data since Euclid launched in mid-2023.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "these are far more than beautiful pictures; today marks a scientific milestone in our study of the cosmos," esa's director of science, carole mundell said in a statement. "This major Euclid data release represents the largest space-based survey of its kind, laying the foundation of future discovery in a new regime for astronomy and demonstrating the excellence of European technology, science and international collaboration. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa the esa put into raw numbers the sheer number of celestial objects viewed by the dark universe detective and contained in dr1-foundation. That includes light spectra from 160 million sources, over 900 million galaxies, and 60 million candidates for quasars, regions of space dominated by feeding supermassive black holes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "this is a change in scale from euclid's previous releases, which included a few days of observations over around 60 degrees squared of sky," esa's euclid project scientist valeria pettorino said. This unlocks groundbreaking science. "We're now releasing more than a year of data covering a significantly larger area. ".

Euclid can see such a vast number of cosmic objects thanks to the fact that its space-based position helps it avoid interference caused by Earth's atmosphere.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this includes clusters of galaxies and even larger superclusters. The study of these objects, some of the largest structures in the cosmos, can reveal how matter came together across the larger network of gas, dust and dark matter called the cosmic web.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "euclid doesn't just look far back in time  — it does so across huge areas of sky," euclid consortium member barbara sartoris of jl lagrange laboratory, nice, france, explained. "We will explore these in the coming months to learn how these giants grew, and decipher what they reveal about the dark universe. "This gives us an unprecedented view of large samples of ancient galaxy clusters that were previously out of reach. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, another exciting element of the new euclid data release is the 15,000 strong gravitational lensing candidates catalogued by the space telescope. Gravitational lensing is an element of the universe first explained in Einstein magnum opus, general relativity, in 1915.

Sebagaimana diketahui, general relativity says that objects with mass cause the very fabric of space to warp, and that gravity arises from this warping. But there is another consequence. When light passes this curvature, its usually straight path is curved. That means when light from a single background source passes an object with great mass, like a galaxy or galaxy cluster, a strong gravitational lens, it can arrive at our telescopes at different times.

Diungkapkan bahwa as a result of this strong lensing, background sources can be greatly amplified. It is an effect that the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has been using to great effect to study galaxies in the early universe.

Thus, the prospect of mapping 15,000 strong gravitational lenses is monumental, especially in studying the rate at which the universe is expanding and thus the effect of dark energy.

Berdasarkan laporan, "strong lensing provides unique insight into the dark universe, allowing us to 'weigh' individual galaxies, including their invisible dark matter, and explore how the universe is expanding," natalie lines of the university of portsmouth, u. , and member of the Euclid Consortium, said. K. That day is finally here. "Over 10 years ago, we forecast that Euclid would revolutionize the field of strong lens discovery. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, arguably, the most exciting thing about dr1-foundation is that euclid is just getting started. The area of sky covered from spring 2024 to spring 2025 represents just 14% of Euclid's target for its entire six-year survey.

That means whatever scientists discover from this data release could be the tip of the iceberg in terms of how the Dark Universe Detective will change our understanding of the cosmos.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "dr1-foundation includes raw data, calibrated images, catalogues, and spectra over a huge sky area, with enough statistics touncover even rare objects," valeria said. "It will be used to map the large-scale structure of the universe in unprecedented detail.

He also writes about science communication for Elsevier and the European Journal of Physics. ’s Open University. whose articles have been published in Physics World, New Scientist, Astronomy Magazine, All About Space, Newsweek and ZME Science. #271. Consumers are spending on physical gifts even as travel tops wish lists, Visa survey finds

📅 05 Nov 2026

Consumers are spending on physical gifts even as travel tops wish lists, Visa survey finds

Tanggal: 05 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/05/visa-holiday-shopping-physical-gifts-travel.html

Consumers are hoping for more travel and experiences this holiday season, but physical gifts continue to win the lion's share of their wallets, according to a new report from Visa on Thursday.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the report found that more than half of survey respondents are putting travel and live events at the top of their wish lists. Still, only 15% of those respondents are prioritizing spending on experiences for others, while 27% of them plan to favor physical gifts.

Berdasarkan laporan, that gap between what shoppers want and what they plan to buy is largely due to higher travel costs, lower consumer sentiment and an emphasis on value, according to michael brown, visa's principal u. S. economist.

Berdasarkan laporan, "there is some interesting trade-offs there that we're seeing on the part of consumers," brown told cnbc. "If I'm traveling more, I'm probably going to be gifting those physical goods less, so this is really the broader context. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, the survey was conducted among roughly 4,660 u. S. adults ages 18 and older, designed to be representative of the broader population of consumers.

Sebagaimana diketahui, brown said budget pressure also factors into traveling for the holidays, as visa expects more people to celebrate the holidays "a little bit closer to home" than in the past given rising airfares and general inflation. In September, consumer prices rose 3. 7% annually, driven higher by surging energy costs.

Berdasarkan laporan, airlines have hiked the price of plane tickets this year as their fuel costs have risen by billions of dollars due to the war in the middle east. And even if fuel prices drop, executives have said fares are likely to stay high, with fares up more than 22% in September compared with a year earlier, according to the consumer price index.

Those trends mean consumers will likely be more intentional about where they're spending, especially as inflation drives up prices across the board.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "consumers are aspirational. They want those experiences, they want to travel, they want to be out in the world," Brown said. "However, the economic reality is with prices rising, with economic uncertainty, they need to balance the reality of today's economic environment with those aspirations. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, the report also found that only households with an income above $200,000 spent more on trips departing between nov. 1 and early next year compared with 2025 into 2026. On the other hand, many other income groups pulled back on their travel spending.

"If you think about that segment, a lot of them own equities, and the equity market runup over the last several months has created a lot of positivity among that specific affluent demographic, and I think that's one of the factors that continues to motivate even aggregate macro spend today," Brown said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, meanwhile, less affluent shoppers are placing an emphasis on value. Visa's consumer survey from October showed that roughly one-third of consumers with an income below $100,000 are going to switch to lower-cost brands or stores when shopping for holiday gifts this season.

Sebagaimana diketahui, though visa is projecting a 4. 1% this year, down from the 1. 5% year-over-year increase in holiday sales growth, much of that figure is due to inflation. Without those price increases, sales are expected to rise just 1. 3% increase during the 2025 holiday season.

Diungkapkan bahwa ultimately, brown said the survey findings may be encouraging for the broader retail scene this holiday season. With less emphasis on travel and more projected spending on physical gifts, it could boost the sector at a time when spending is under pressure.

At the same time, he said that consumers may just be expecting to spend more this holiday season because they've become accustomed to the higher prices.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "but, of course, consumers are internalizing higher prices of things, and i think that's why they're reporting higher anticipated spend this year," brown said. "I think these numbers just need to be looked at through the lens of the inflation and particularly consumers' perception of where inflation is going to go. I think that weighed heavily on consumer psychology this season. ".

#272. Climate Change Has Pushed the World's Ice Out of Its Safe Zone

📅 12 Nov 2026

Climate Change Has Pushed the World's Ice Out of Its Safe Zone

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/climate-change-abolishes-ice/

The world is no longer safe for frozen H2O.

New research published in Science on Thursday shows that the conditions that have kept ice, frozen soil, and snow stable are slipping away due to the burning of fossil fuels—and the implications are grave for the entire globe.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the climate of the past 12,000 or so years has been remarkably steady. That’s allowed for all kinds of wonderful things to happen, like human civilization flourishing. But rising temperatures are pushing the climate outside that envelope, and the new research looks at what the team behind the new findings has called the “safe operating space” for the icy, snowy landscape known as the cryosphere.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the scientists looked at changes to polar sea and land ice, mountain glaciers, permafrost, and snow cover over the past 12 millennia to analyze conditions that have allowed both civilization and other ecosystems to thrive. They then identified boundaries on those conditions that, if crossed, would upend the stability and safety humans have enjoyed for millennia.

Diungkapkan bahwa the results show an “accelerating and partly irreversible loss of cryospheric integrity. ” Arctic and Antarctic sea ice have both fallen outside the safe operating threshold, as have snow cover and the area of permafrost—frozen soil laden with carbon. While land ice hasn’t yet fallen out of its safe space, it’s on the brink. And because of warming that’s already been locked into the climate system, it’s likely to also fall outside the threshold in the coming centuries.

Diungkapkan bahwa while it may feel like the antarctic ice sheet or permafrost covering alaska are distant concerns, they’re anything but. Any degradation means that CO2, as well as even more potent methane, could end up in the atmosphere, accelerating global warming even further. Permafrost, meanwhile, holds trillions of tons of carbon dioxide. The West Antarctic Ice Sheet, which a growing body of evidence shows is nearing the brink of irreversible decline, has enough ice to raise sea levels by 11 feet (3 meters). Other examples of major risks abound, including how melting Greenland land ice could slow down or even collapse the ocean conveyor belt that helps keep Europe temperate.

“The consequences of a changing cryosphere extend beyond regions where ice and snow are disappearing,” says Albert Norström, a climate researcher at the Stockholm Resilience Center who co-authored the new paper.

Sebagaimana diketahui, dipping outside the safe operating space doesn’t mean that the world will see 11 feet of sea level rise in the next year, a trillion-ton co2 eruption, or a day after tomorrow scenario. But it does mean that the odds of crossing dangerous tipping points are rising.

Diungkapkan bahwa “as we scratch 1. 5 [degrees Celsius] and go above it, we are just really gambling with potentially triggering some of these Earth system tipping points,” Norström says. The safe operating space framework also “takes a broader perspective” that assesses slower changes over time and “how far, in this case, the cryosphere is moving away from the conditions that have supported a relatively stable Earth system,” he adds.

Berdasarkan laporan, cutting emissions is the most obvious and straightforward way to stop the cryosphere from sliding further outside our comfort zone. But there are a growing number of proposals to pursue more radical interventions that could protect the world’s ice. Scientists have already draped glaciers in the Alps in blankets during the summer to prevent melting. Other researchers have explored techniques to pump cold sea water to the surface to help thicken ice and modeled whether a manmade barrier could stabilize the West Antarctic Ice Sheet.

Berdasarkan laporan, these geoengineering approaches have the potential to be costly, and there’s no guarantee they would work. They’d also do nothing to stop the root cause of warming: burning fossil fuels. Norström says emissions cuts are the most urgent way to protect ice and snow (and ourselves), but with the cryosphere sliding into a more dangerous space, “in principle, we shouldn't put the lid on” research for more far-flung interventions.

Diungkapkan bahwa “the safe operating space is a precautionary framework,” he says. “It ensures that we try to stay as far downstream from the point where these really potentially existential or huge consequences and risks can happen. ”.

Update: 11/12/2026, 4:13 PM EST: WIRED corrected the name of Albert Norström.

#275. A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster

📅 07 Nov 2026

A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster

Tanggal: 07 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261106174537.htm

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the discovery comes from an international collaboration involving research groups at the regensburg center for ultrafast nanoscopy (run), led by profs. Jascha Repp, Rupert Huber, Franz Giessibl, and Klaus Richter, along with a team at the Max Planck Institute in Hamburg led by Angel Rubio.

Watching Electrons Move at Incredible Speeds.

Berdasarkan laporan, understanding how matter behaves at the smallest scales is essential for developing the next generation of technology. Advances in clean energy, quantum computing, and powerful electronics for artificial intelligence all depend on knowing how chemical reactions unfold, how light interacts with materials, and how electrons travel through electronic devices.

Sebagaimana diketahui, however, even the sharpest microscopic photographs cannot reveal the full picture. Scientists also need to observe how these processes change over time, effectively creating slow-motion movies of events occurring at the atomic scale.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at run, researchers are developing ultrafast microscopes capable of recording the movements of electrons, atoms, and molecules with extraordinary precision in both space and time. About ten years ago, scientists in Regensburg used ultrafast scanning tunneling microscopy to resolve the movement of a single molecule across space and time for the first time.

Diungkapkan bahwa tracking individual electrons presents an even greater challenge. At these microscopic distances, electrons can move roughly a thousand times faster than atoms and molecules, with important changes taking place over just attoseconds.

Berdasarkan laporan, to appreciate how extreme these scales are, consider that an atom is approximately ten million times smaller than a millimeter. An attosecond is one-billionth of a billionth of a second. The difference between an attosecond and a second is comparable to the difference between one second and the entire age of the universe.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, making these measurements is especially difficult because electrons do not behave like ordinary objects. Their motion follows the unusual laws of quantum mechanics rather than the familiar rules of classical physics.

Ultrafast Lasers Reveal Quantum Tunneling.

Sebagaimana diketahui, to observe electron behavior at these extraordinary speeds, the researchers built a new laser system that provides much finer time resolution than earlier experiments. The system allows them to control and study the quantum motion of individual electrons directly.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in the experiments, carefully timed laser pulses drive electrons from an extremely sharp metal tip toward a silver surface. The distance they travel is only a few atomic diameters.

Diungkapkan bahwa the researchers detect this movement by measuring the resulting electrical current. To determine exactly when the electrons move, they use two pulses of light separated by a precisely controlled interval.

Diungkapkan bahwa simon maier, the lead author of the paper, explains: "by varying the time interval between the two laser pulses, we can directly observe how the electrons respond. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, this approach revealed clear evidence of electron motion occurring on attosecond timescales. It showed that the laser pulses could transfer electrons within these incredibly brief intervals while allowing scientists to observe the process as it happened.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what makes the result particularly remarkable is how the electrons travel. Instead of moving like conventional particles, they behave as quantum waves. This allows them to pass through an energy barrier separating the metal tip from the silver surface, even though classical physics predicts they should not have enough energy to cross it.

This phenomenon, known as quantum tunneling, is somewhat like an object passing through a solid wall without breaking or damaging it.

"Our measurement can be understood as a high-speed camera for the electron wave packets, since you can see at what point in time the tunneling process takes place," explains Katharina Glöckl, a doctoral student and co-author of the publication.

Diungkapkan bahwa to understand the measurements more deeply, researchers working with prof. Angel Rubio performed sophisticated quantum simulations of the electrons' behavior near the "space-time limit. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, their calculations closely reproduced the experimental findings and uncovered another remarkable detail. The electrons did not respond to the light field instantaneously. Instead, their motion lagged behind it by approximately 500 attoseconds.

At such extreme scales, several fundamental features of quantum physics become important simultaneously.

Diungkapkan bahwa for example, the researchers found that the laser pulses could not be described entirely by treating light as a wave or entirely by treating it as individual particles called photons. This combination was essential for exploring electron behavior so close to the "space-time limit. Their effects displayed characteristics of both descriptions. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa the team also discovered that controlling electron motion over extremely short intervals changes how the electrons are distributed in space. Quantum mechanics describes these electrons using wave packets, which represent how their wave properties extend across different locations.

The relationship between the timing of electron motion and the spatial extent of these wave packets revealed the central limitation behind the discovery.

Diungkapkan bahwa raffael spachtholz, another co-author of the study, explains: "the more precisely we want to pin down the electron's position in time, the more energy we need to provide. And as a result, the electron wave packet spreads out more spatially. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa in other words, improving the precision of an electron's timing comes with a cost. The more tightly researchers define when its motion occurs, the more broadly its quantum wave packet spreads through space.

To examine this relationship experimentally, the team placed a single atom on the surface to confine the electron wave packets to an extremely small region immediately before the laser pulses arrived.

This setup allowed the scientists to directly measure the connection between the electrons' spatial distribution and the timing of their motion.

Importantly, even when the electrons received substantial energy from the laser pulses, their wave packets remained sufficiently localized for microscopy with atomic spatial resolution and attosecond time resolution.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the findings provide experimental insight into a fundamental space-time constraint that scientists had previously only suspected. They also make it possible to systematically investigate how changes in electron motion over time affect the spatial structure of quantum wave functions.

Could Quantum Electronics Become Hundreds of Thousands of Times Faster?.

Beyond revealing a new aspect of quantum behavior, the discovery could open the door to technologies that operate on timescales far beyond the capabilities of today's electronics.

One especially promising possibility involves using precisely controlled electron wave packets to influence chemical reactions.

Sebagaimana diketahui, transferring a single electron to a molecule represents the smallest possible transfer of electric charge. But when that electron is concentrated within an exceptionally small region of space and time, the resulting local peak current density can reach as much as 1 trillion amperes per square centimeter.

Such extreme conditions could give scientists new ways to control chemical bonds and observe how molecules change during reactions.

Diungkapkan bahwa "in the future, we want to use such wave packets to specifically trigger chemical reactions and observe, on the relevant length and time scales, how chemical bonds can be broken or altered," explains prof. Jascha Repp enthusiastically.

Berdasarkan laporan, the implications could extend well beyond chemistry. Greater control over electron motion may eventually help engineers develop electronic devices and quantum information systems that operate at speeds approaching the fundamental limits of electron dynamics.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "in the long term, the insights gained could also contribute to operating electronics and quantum information processing at the intrinsic speed limit of electron motion itself -- hundreds of thousands of times faster than the currently dominant cmos technology," adds prof. Rupert Huber.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that possibility remains a long term technological goal rather than an achievement demonstrated in the current experiments. Nevertheless, the findings provide a new foundation for exploring how electrons can be manipulated at the smallest distances and shortest timescales.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for repp and huber, the results suggest that the range of potential applications is extraordinarily broad. They believe that future advances in controlling electrons at the space-time limit may ultimately depend more on human creativity than on the constraints imposed by nature.

Sebagaimana diketahui, when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

An astronaut from Pakistan is set to launch on China's Shenzhou 24 mission in the coming weeks and become the first-ever international visitor to the Tiangong space station.

A pair of astronaut candidates from Pakistan have been training at the Astronaut Centre of China in Beijing, following an agreement reached between China and Pakistan in Islamabad in February 2025 and a subsequent selection process.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, china's human spaceflight agency confirmed in a nov. 7 press statement that the upcoming Shenzhou 24 mission will carry one of the astronauts. The agency also released a mission patch.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "china and pakistan are all-weather strategic cooperative partners," foreign ministry spokesperson guo jiakun said nov. "Having the Pakistani astronaut on board China's spaceships will mark the first-ever joint mission of Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program. 9. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it is not yet known which of the two candidates will fly on shenzhou 24. They were named in Pakistani press reports as Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud, both pilots from the country's military forces. The pair were chosen from a wider pool of around 20 finalists.

Diungkapkan bahwa the chosen candidate will fly as a payload specialist on shenzhou 24 along with two chinese colleagues, while the other will be on standby as a backup. While the Chinese astronauts will be starting a six-month-long stay in space, the Pakistani astronaut will spend roughly a week in orbit aboard Tiangong during a standard crew rotation period. He will then return to Earth aboard the departing Shenzhou 23 spacecraft, along with two Chinese astronauts who will have completed a six-month-long stay in orbit.

Berdasarkan laporan, the arrangement means changes to china's usual "three in, three out" tiangong crew rotations. One of the three Shenzhou 23 astronauts, who arrived at Tiangong on May 24, will stay aboard and complete China's first-ever year-long stay in orbit, while the Pakistani astronaut will take their seat aboard Shenzhou 23 to return home.

During his stay in space, the Pakistani astronaut will be responsible for four research payloads selected from more than 300 proposals, according to Pakistan's space agency, SUPARCO.

Diungkapkan bahwa china has not announced a timeline for the launch of the shenzhou 24 mission, but it is expected to lift off before the end of november. The Shenzhou 23 astronauts currently aboard Tiangong are closing in on 180 days in orbit, nearing an end to their six months in space.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, shenzhou 24 will launch from jiuquan satellite launch center in the gobi desert on a long march 2f rocket. The identities of the crew for China's human spaceflight missions are typically closely guarded, and will only be revealed in a press conference a day ahead of launch. Shenzhou 24's Long March 2F rocket will be rolled out to the pad around a week ahead of launch.

The partnership between the two countries has already produced Chinese-launched Pakistani satellites, including a lunar cubesat, and a Pakistani-built rover due to fly on the Chang'e-8 lunar landing mission.

Diungkapkan bahwa andrew is a freelance space journalist with a focus on reporting on china's rapidly growing space sector. Away from space, Andrew enjoys trail running in the forests of Finland. Andrew first caught the space bug when, as a youngster, he saw Voyager images of other worlds in our solar system for the first time. He began writing for Space. com in 2019 and writes for SpaceNews, IEEE Spectrum, National Geographic, Sky & Telescope, New Scientist and others. You can follow him on Twitter @AJ_FI.

#278. An ancient ocean full of giant predators reveals a surprising twist in evolution

📅 08 Nov 2026

An ancient ocean full of giant predators reveals a surprising twist in evolution

Tanggal: 08 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261106174535.htm

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, an extraordinary collection of fossils in central colombia is revealing a surprising chapter in earth's evolutionary history. Researchers have uncovered evidence of a time when ancient animal groups that were approaching extinction lived alongside newer groups that would eventually flourish. The discovery suggests that major evolutionary transitions can occur without the widespread destruction associated with mass extinctions.

Berdasarkan laporan, scientists from mcgill university and the centro de investigaciones paleontológicas (cip) identified this unusual pattern while studying fossils from colombia's paja formation. The ancient marine ecosystem preserves an exceptional mixture of surviving Jurassic lineages and emerging Cretaceous groups, offering a rare glimpse into a period of profound biological change.

Sebagaimana diketahui, drawing on these findings, mcgill biology professor hans larsson and phd graduate dirley cortés have proposed a new concept called a "biotic inflection. " The term describes an evolutionary turning point when older groups nearing extinction coexist with newer lineages that are beginning to expand and diversify.

A Perfect Storm for Ancient Ocean Biodiversity.

Berdasarkan laporan, the researchers believe an unusual combination of environmental conditions helped make this remarkable coexistence possible. Warm greenhouse temperatures, elevated sea levels, and coastal waters rich in nutrients may have supported an unusually diverse range of marine life.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, another important factor was the emergence of new ocean connections between the eastern pacific and the early atlantic through the region that is now colombia. Together, these conditions likely created opportunities for different groups of animals to thrive within the same ecosystem. Many of these environmental influences continue to shape biodiversity around the world today.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the paja formation records an extraordinary process in the history of life, when a 'perfect storm' of environmental factors we know to promote ecological complexity coincided with ancient lineages that were about to disappear. At the same time, new groups were beginning to flourish," Larsson said.

A Lost World of Giant Marine Reptiles and Predators.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the evidence comes from the early cretaceous paja formation near villa de leyva, colombia. This fossil-rich region has preserved an astonishing variety of prehistoric marine animals, providing scientists with an unusually detailed picture of an ancient ocean ecosystem. Most of the fossils collected from the formation are housed at the CIP.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "this geological formation has produced an exceptionally rich fossil record that includes giant marine reptiles like long-necked plesiosaurs and marine crocodile relatives, as well as turtles, sharks, crustaceans and others," cortés explained. "Together, these animals formed the Paja Biota, one of the most ecologically complex marine communities found to date. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, in a previous study, the researchers reconstructed the feeding relationships among animals in the paja biota. Their analysis revealed an exceptionally intricate food web, with an unusually large variety of apex predators occupying the highest levels of the ecosystem.

This remarkable complexity makes the Paja Formation especially valuable for investigating how ecosystems change as older evolutionary groups decline and new ones become established.

Could This Discovery Change How Scientists Understand Evolution?.

Diungkapkan bahwa the proposed biotic inflection offers a potentially important new way to understand major changes in earth's biodiversity. Rather than being driven by a mass extinction, some evolutionary transitions may involve periods of extraordinary diversity, when declining lineages and emerging groups coexist.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, the researchers emphasize that more evidence is needed to establish how common this pattern may have been. Additional fossil discoveries, more accurate estimates of fossil ages, and comparisons with geological formations in other parts of the world will help determine whether similar transitions occurred elsewhere in Earth's history.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "i think we've discovered a new model of global biodiversity change. Now we'll need to see just how widespread this could be in Earth's history and how we can quantify its impacts," Larsson said.

Berdasarkan laporan, the research received funding from the natural sciences and engineering research council of canada, the smithsonian tropical research institute, the anders foundation, the 1923 fund, gregory d. and Jennifer Walston Johnson, the Fonds de recherche Nature et technologies Québec, and the McGill Biology Department Writing-Year Award 2024-2025.
